3	/// The export queue (road map 2's phase 7e): the exports a person has
4	/// confirmed but does not want to sit and watch, run one after another while
5	/// the editor stays live.
6	///
7	/// **There is no AppKit in this file, and that is the design rather than
8	/// tidiness.** A queue window can be checked by neither of this project's two
9	/// instruments: the offscreen harness renders an `EditorViewController` into a
10	/// window and nothing else, and MCP drives the app through tools — and the
11	/// agent's `export` enqueues here, so a tool reaches this list but never the
12	/// window (below, spec §11 #326). What a proof CAN do is
13	/// compile a probe out of the whole of `app/Sources`
14	/// (`tools/proof/phase6_chrome.py`'s `build_probe`), make one of these,
15	/// enqueue two jobs, spin the main run loop until `isIdle` and read `jobs`
16	/// back — without an `NSWindow` ever being ordered front. So the job list and
17	/// its state machine live here, where a script can reach them, and
18	/// `ExportQueueWindowController.swift` is a READER of this and nothing else:
19	/// it holds no job, decides nothing, and closing it stops nothing.
20	/// `AudioNormalize.swift` and `CaptionLayout.swift` are the same split — the
21	/// arithmetic where a script can call it, the dialog around it — and phase 5's
22	/// level meter is the closest sibling, where the MODEL publishes a number
23	/// precisely so that a proof need not photograph a window.
24	///
25	/// **The agent's `export` is a job here (spec §11 #326).** It keeps its
26	/// refusals synchronous, then enqueues exactly as Add to Queue does and
27	/// answers the job's id at once; `export_status` follows the job and
28	/// `cancel_export` calls `cancel` (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`). The
29	/// queue's own API is unchanged by it: the mirror reads `job(_:)` and
30	/// observes `didChangeNotification` like the window does, and no tool
31	/// exists for a person's own queued job.
32	///
33	/// **One job at a time, on the MAIN thread, a fresh `Exporter` for each.**
34	/// `Exporter.export`'s own doc says main-thread-only and one export at a time,
35	/// and it means both: it schedules a run-loop `Timer` — which must be
36	/// invalidated on the thread it was scheduled on — and calls its progress and
37	/// completion handlers on the main thread. So this is a CHAIN and not a pool:
38	/// `start()` runs the head of the list and each completion runs the next. A
39	/// `DispatchQueue` of exporters would be the wrong shape whatever the machine's
40	/// core count, and not only because of the timer — an `Exporter` carries
41	/// per-export state (`recipeKey`, `cancelRequested`, the loudness scratch
42	/// buffer), which is why each job gets its own rather than one being reset
43	/// between jobs. Every method below is main-thread-only for that reason, like
44	/// the exporter it drives.
45	///
46	/// **What a job holds is the whole of what it will write, captured when it was
47	/// confirmed.** The `ReelProject` is a handle and handles are immutable (spec
48	/// §5.5) — every edit and every undo makes a NEW one — so a queued write cannot
49	/// be reached by an edit made after it, and it needs no clone: `Exporter.export`
50	/// publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key it mints for itself, never the
51	/// document's, so even the frames the compositor serves this export come from
52	/// this handle. The document may be edited, undone or CLOSED while the job
53	/// waits; the handle is retained here and the Rust project behind it lives
54	/// until the job is gone.
55	///
56	/// **And the media URLs are resolved at ENQUEUE, which is what makes them part
57	/// of that same snapshot.** `ProjectDocument.mediaURLs()` resolves a bookmark
58	/// and asks the filesystem whether the file is there (`mediaURL(for:)`), so it
59	/// is a reading of the disk at the moment it is called: resolving at RUN time
60	/// would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after the job was
61	/// queued, which is the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. That
62	/// rule is structural here rather than remembered — `enqueue` takes a
63	/// `[UInt32: URL]` and a job holds no document, so there is nothing to ask
64	/// again later even if somebody wanted to.
65	///
66	/// **The REVERSE resolution is the third thing in that snapshot, and it was
67	/// missing.** Handle immutability covers the project and nothing beside it:
68	/// which clips play from a pre-rendered backwards file is a reading of the
69	/// disk too (`ProjectDocument.reverseState`, `ReverseCache.existing`), it
70	/// cannot be derived from a bare handle, and it lives in a side table keyed by
71	/// object IDENTITY — which the document overwrites on every edit and removes
72	/// when it closes. So a job queued from a timeline holding a reversed clip
73	/// used to answer `.none` the moment anything was edited, and `.none` means
74	/// "not reversed": the export took the forward asset at the mirrored source
75	/// window, unslated and unreported. It is captured here at enqueue, exactly as
76	/// the URLs are, and PINNED to this job's own handle for the length of its
77	/// write (`ReverseSource.pin`). Anything else the picture depends on that is
78	/// neither in the handle nor derivable from it joins that list.
79	///
80	/// **A bundled-encoder job also waits for memory (spec §11 CX-18).** An AV1 or VP9 job
81	/// starts only while `ExportEncoderLedger` admits it: nothing else booked, or the running
82	/// encoder exports — an Export… sheet's beside this queue's — fitting with it in a quarter
83	/// of physical memory. A held job says why in its `message` and is PASSED OVER by a later
84	/// job the ledger admits, an AVFoundation job always; the chain stays one job at a time.
85	/// The running job is booked from just before its `export` call to its finish, and a
86	/// booking's end — the queue's own or a sheet's — re-runs `start()` through the ledger's
87	/// notification.
88	final class ExportQueueController {
89	    /// The app's one queue: the export sheet's Add to Queue fills it and
90	    /// Window ▸ Export Queue shows it.
91	    static let shared = ExportQueueController()
92	
93	    /// Where a job is. A closed set with no associated values, so the two
94	    /// readers ask it different questions without either having to spell a
95	    /// message: the window's row draws its own wording (which carries a
96	    /// percentage the state cannot know), and a probe compares the case and
97	    /// reads `Job.message` for the sentence. The raw values are the same
98	    /// strings a probe writes into its JSON answer.
99	    enum State: String {
100	        /// Queued and not started. The only state a job can be enqueued in.
101	        case waiting
102	        /// The one job an `Exporter` is running. At most one at any moment.
103	        case running
104	        /// The file landed.
105	        case completed
106	        /// Stopped by a person, either before it started or mid-write — in
107	        /// which case its half-written file has been removed.
108	        case cancelled
109	        /// The exporter refused or failed. Whatever it had written is LEFT on
110	        /// disk, which is `ExportProgressSheetController`'s posture and not a
111	        /// new one: a cancel is a person saying "not this", where a failure is
112	        /// evidence, and the file names itself in the message.
113	        case failed
114	
115	        /// Whether the job is over, however it ended — the test for "may be
116	        /// removed from the list" and for "no longer holds a project handle
117	        /// worth keeping".
118	        var isFinished: Bool { self == .completed || self == .cancelled || self == .failed }
119	    }
120	
121	    /// One confirmed export. Everything it needs was read when it was
122	    /// enqueued; see the type doc for why that is the whole point of it.
123	    struct Job {
124	        /// Monotonic within one launch. The window's rows and every method
125	        /// below address a job by this rather than by index, because a job can
126	        /// be removed from the middle of the list while a later one runs.
127	        let id: UInt64
128	        /// The timeline as it was confirmed — immutable, and retained here, so
129	        /// the document behind it may be edited, undone or closed.
130	        ///
131	        /// A FINISHED job goes on holding it, and that is a real cost stated
132	        /// rather than hidden: a handle is the project's model and not its
133	        /// media, so it is JSON-sized, and Clear Finished (or Remove) is what
134	        /// releases it along with the row that says where the file went.
135	        /// Dropping the handle at the finish would buy those bytes back and
136	        /// cost the field its `let` — an immutable job whose contents change
137	        /// once is a harder thing to reason about than a list somebody tidies.
138	        let project: ReelProject
139	        /// The media files as they resolved AT ENQUEUE.
140	        let urls: [UInt32: URL]
141	        /// Which of this timeline's clips play from a pre-rendered backwards
142	        /// file, as that resolved AT ENQUEUE — the type doc's third piece of
143	        /// the snapshot. Read from `ReverseSource` here and published back to
144	        /// it under this job's own handle while the job runs, because the
145	        /// document's copy is overwritten by the next edit and dropped when it
146	        /// closes.
147	        let reverse: ReverseResolution
148	        let settings: ExportSettings
149	        let destination: URL
150	        /// What this export asks of the PICTURE besides the timeline — the
151	        /// burn-in (`RecipeOptions`). Carried per job, because two jobs from
152	        /// one document may legitimately differ in it.
153	        let options: RecipeOptions
154	        /// The document's compiled graphics as they stood AT ENQUEUE (G-13) —
155	        /// the type doc's list again: a module saved after Add to Queue is not
156	        /// in the handle, and the document's set is swapped by that save and
157	        /// dropped when it closes. `Exporter.export` pins it for the write.
158	        let graphics: GraphicSet?
159	        var state: State = .waiting
160	        /// 0…1, and only meaningful while `state` is `.running`.
161	        var progress: Double = 0
162	        /// The line a person reads when it is over: what was written and what
163	        /// the file measured, or why it stopped — plus the one thing worth
164	        /// saying mid-flight, that a cancel is in hand. While it waits, the
165	        /// ledger's sentence when the memory limit holds it (CX-18), else nil.
166	        var message: String?
167	        /// What the exporter says it is doing right now, or nil for "writing",
168	        /// which is the caller's own wording. Today the only phase is the
169	        /// loudness measurement, which on an audio-only export is half the wait
170	        /// and the half where nothing is on disk yet.
171	        ///
172	        /// A field of its own rather than a use of `message`, because the two
173	        /// are written by different things at the same time: the progress tick
174	        /// arrives ten times a second and would otherwise wipe the "Stopping…"
175	        /// a person had just asked for.
176	        var phase: String?
177	        /// Set on a COMPLETED job when a later job starts writing to the same
178	        /// path, because from that moment this row's file is not this row's
179	        /// any more — `Exporter.startWriting` removes whatever is at the
180	        /// destination before it builds its pipeline, so the earlier export is
181	        /// gone whether the later one succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
182	        ///
183	        /// The row stops claiming "Exported …" and stops offering Show in
184	        /// Finder. It is a fact about what happened rather than a state: the
185	        /// job really did complete, and rewriting its `state` would lose that.
186	        ///
187	        /// One case marks it where the file in fact survives, and it is the
188	        /// honest direction of the two: a later job whose COMPOSITION fails to
189	        /// build returns before the delete, so nothing was destroyed. It is
190	        /// left alone rather than reached for, because knowing which failures
191	        /// precede the delete means reading `Exporter`'s stages from here, and
192	        /// a shared destination implies a shared project — a build that failed
193	        /// for job 2 would almost always have failed for job 1.
194	        var superseded: Bool = false
195	        /// What the graphics warned while a COMPLETED job's file was drawn
196	        /// (G-24 (c)): the row's count and its tooltip's list.
197	        var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
198	        var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning] = []  // spec §11 CU-37 (c)
199	        /// What a COMPLETED job's sound measured, read off its exporter at the
200	        /// finish — the figures the row's message summarises, kept whole for
201	        /// `export_status`'s `loudness` (spec §11 #326). nil otherwise.
202	        var loudness: ExportLoudness? = nil
203	
204	        /// What the row calls this job. The file name and not the path: the
205	        /// row is narrow, and the full path is the tooltip's job.
206	        var name: String { destination.lastPathComponent }
207	    }
208	
209	    /// Posted after any change to `jobs` — an enqueue, a progress tick, a
210	    /// finish, a cancel, a removal — with the controller as the `object`, so
211	    /// an observer of the shared queue is never woken by a probe's own
212	    /// instance. Main thread, like everything else here.
213	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
214	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportQueueDidChange")
215	
216	    /// Every job this launch still knows about, in the order they were added.
217	    /// A finished one stays until it is removed, because "it is done and here
218	    /// is where it went" is the queue's other job.
219	    private(set) var jobs: [Job] = []
220	
221	    /// The exporter running `runningID`'s job, and nil whenever nothing is
222	    /// running. Set and cleared together with the job's state, so `isIdle` can
223	    /// be answered from `jobs` alone.
224	    private var exporter: Exporter?
225	
226	    /// The handle whose reverse resolution is pinned in `ReverseSource` right
227	    /// now — the running job's, and nil whenever nothing is running. Held
228	    /// separately from the job so that `launch` and `finished` are provably one
229	    /// pin and one release, whatever happens to the list in between.
230	    private var pinnedProject: ReelProject?
231	
232	    /// The running job's booking in the encoder ledger (CX-18), nil whenever nothing runs
233	    /// or the running job is an AVFoundation one. Taken BEFORE `end` in `finished`: the
234	    /// ledger's post can launch — and book — the next job inside that call.
235	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
236	
237	    private let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger.shared
238	
239	    /// True only while `start()` is inside `Exporter.export`. An early refusal
240	    /// — `noPlan`, `emptyTimeline` — completes SYNCHRONOUSLY, so `finished`
241	    /// can run before `export` has returned; without this flag the next job
242	    /// would be launched from inside the previous one's stack frame and a
243	    /// queue of refusals would recurse as deep as it is long. With it, a
244	    /// re-entrant `start()` is refused and the frame already on the stack
245	    /// picks the next job up in its own loop.
246	    private var isLaunching = false
247	
248	    private var nextID: UInt64 = 1
249	
250	    /// Internal rather than private, and deliberately: a proof compiles a
251	    /// probe out of `app/Sources` and makes its OWN queue, so that running two
252	    /// jobs in a script cannot disturb — or be disturbed by — the app's shared
253	    /// one. It is the same reason `ExportPresetsStore` is a value a test can
254	    /// make.
255	    init() {
256	        // A booking's end — a sheet's as much as this queue's — may admit a held job.
257	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
258	            self, selector: #selector(ledgerChanged(_:)),
259	            name: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification, object: ledger)
260	    }
261	
262	    @objc private func ledgerChanged(_ note: Notification) { start() }
263	
264	    @available(*, unavailable)
265	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
266	        fatalError("ExportQueueController does not support NSCoder")
267	    }
268	
269	    // MARK: - Asking
270	
271	    /// Nothing waiting and nothing running. The queue's own "are we there
272	    /// yet", and what a probe spins the run loop until.
273	    ///
274	    /// Answered from `jobs` rather than from `exporter`, so it means the same
275	    /// thing to a caller that cannot see the private state.
276	    var isIdle: Bool {
277	        !jobs.contains { $0.state == .waiting || $0.state == .running }
278	    }
279	
280	    /// The job an exporter is writing right now, if any.
281	    var runningJob: Job? { jobs.first { $0.state == .running } }
282	
283	    /// How many are still queued behind it.
284	    var waitingCount: Int { jobs.filter { $0.state == .waiting }.count }
285	
286	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> Job? { jobs.first { $0.id == id } }
287	
288	    // MARK: - Filling
289	
290	    /// Adds one confirmed export and starts the queue if it is not already
291	    /// running. Answers the job's id, so a caller can follow it.
292	    ///
293	    /// The arguments are `Exporter.export`'s, and that is not a coincidence:
294	    /// a job is exactly the call that will be made, held until its turn. Both
295	    /// `project` and `urls` are read by the CALLER, at the moment the save
296	    /// panel answered (`EditorViewController.enqueueExport`), which is what
297	    /// the type doc means by capturing at enqueue.
298	    ///
299	    /// **Two jobs may name one file, and the queue still does not refuse it —
300	    /// but it no longer pretends the person was warned.** The reason first
301	    /// given here was that "the save panel asked about replacing an existing
302	    /// file both times", and that is false in exactly the case that matters:
303	    /// `NSSavePanel` prompts only when something is at the path as Save is
304	    /// confirmed, and job 1 spends its build and its whole loudness
305	    /// measurement pass with nothing at the destination — `Exporter.export`
306	    /// does both before `startWriting` deletes and `AVAssetWriter` creates —
307	    /// so two Add to Queue actions in quick succession are never asked
308	    /// anything. Refusing here would still be wrong: overwriting your own
309	    /// export is a thing a person is allowed to do, and the queue must not be
310	    /// the one place in the app where they may not. What was wrong was the
311	    /// silence AFTERWARDS, and `launch` is where that is answered — the
312	    /// earlier row is marked `superseded` the moment a later job starts
313	    /// writing to its path, so no row goes on offering a file that another
314	    /// job has since deleted or replaced.
315	    @discardableResult
316	    func enqueue(
317	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
318	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
319	    ) -> UInt64 {
320	        let id = nextID
321	        nextID += 1
322	        jobs.append(
323	            Job(
324	                id: id, project: project, urls: urls,
325	                // The third piece of the enqueue-time snapshot; the type doc
326	                // says why it cannot be left to be asked again at run time.
327	                reverse: ReverseSource.shared.resolution(publishedFor: project),
328	                settings: settings, destination: url, options: options, graphics: graphics))
329	        didChange()
330	        start()
331	        return id
332	    }
333	
334	    // MARK: - Running
335	
336	    /// Runs the first waiting job the encoder ledger admits, if nothing is
337	    /// running already — passing over a held one (CX-18 (7)). Idempotent
338	    /// and safe to call at any time: `enqueue` calls it, every completion
339	    /// calls it, the ledger's change calls it, and a caller may call it itself.
340	    ///
341	    /// The loop is for the synchronous-refusal case `isLaunching` describes: a
342	    /// job the exporter refuses without ever going asynchronous has already
343	    /// finished by the time `launch` returns, and this frame takes the next
344	    /// one rather than recursing into it.
345	    func start() {
346	        guard !isLaunching else { return }
347	        isLaunching = true
348	        defer { isLaunching = false }
349	        while exporter == nil, let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: {
350	            $0.state == .waiting && ledger.admits($0.settings)
351	        }) {
352	            launch(at: index)
353	        }
354	        noteHeld()
355	    }
356	
357	    /// Every waiting encoder job's `message` set to why it is held, or cleared when it is
358	    /// not — leaving out this queue's own running booking, which it waits behind anyway.
359	    private func noteHeld() {
360	        var changed = false
361	        for index in jobs.indices
362	        where jobs[index].state == .waiting && jobs[index].settings.writer != nil {
363	            let sentence = ledger.waitingSentence(for: jobs[index].settings, ignoring: ledgerToken)
364	            if jobs[index].message != sentence {
365	                jobs[index].message = sentence
366	                changed = true
367	            }
368	        }
369	        if changed { didChange() }
370	    }
371	
372	    /// One job handed to one fresh `Exporter`. The exporter is stored BEFORE
373	    /// the call, because an early refusal calls back before `export` returns
374	    /// and `finished` has to find it there.
375	    private func launch(at index: Int) {
376	        let job = jobs[index]
377	        jobs[index].state = .running
378	        jobs[index].progress = 0
379	        jobs[index].message = nil
380	        jobs[index].phase = nil
381	        // Any COMPLETED row naming this same path stops claiming its file
382	        // here, and here rather than when the file is actually deleted: the
383	        // delete happens inside `Exporter.startWriting`, seconds later and in
384	        // a file this one may not reach into, and being early is the honest
385	        // direction — a row that stops offering a file just before it is
386	        // destroyed costs a person nothing, where one that offers it just
387	        // after sends them to the Finder for something that is gone.
388	        for other in jobs.indices
389	        where other != index && jobs[other].state == .completed
390	            && jobs[other].destination == job.destination
391	        {
392	            jobs[other].superseded = true
393	        }
394	        // The job's own reverse resolution, held against its own handle for
395	        // exactly the length of this write. At most one pin exists at a time,
396	        // which is the invariant `ReverseSource.pin` asks its callers for and
397	        // which this class keeps for free by running one job at a time.
398	        ReverseSource.shared.pin(job.reverse, for: job.project)
399	        pinnedProject = job.project
400	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
401	        ledgerToken = ledger.begin(job.settings)
402	        let exporter = Exporter()
403	        self.exporter = exporter
404	        didChange()
405	        exporter.export(
406	            project: job.project, urls: job.urls, settings: job.settings, to: job.destination,
407	            options: job.options, graphics: job.graphics,
408	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(job.id, value) },
409	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(job.id, result) })
410	    }
411	
412	    private func progressed(_ id: UInt64, _ value: Double) {
413	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
414	            jobs[index].state == .running
415	        else { return }
416	        jobs[index].progress = min(max(value, 0), 1)
417	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. The progress
418	        // sheet asks the same question with the same call; a row that said
419	        // "Writing" through the measurement would be claiming a file that does
420	        // not exist yet.
421	        jobs[index].phase = exporter?.phaseDescription
422	        didChange()
423	    }
424	
425	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes, and the mirror of
426	    /// `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` — deliberately, because there
427	    /// must not be two accounts of what finishing an export means. The
428	    /// exporter is cleared first, so the `start()` at the foot can hand the
429	    /// next job a fresh one.
430	    private func finished(_ id: UInt64, _ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
431	        // Read BEFORE the exporter is dropped: `Exporter.finish` publishes the
432	        // measurement and then calls this, so the report is there now and only
433	        // now.
434	        let report = exporter?.loudnessReport
435	        let measured = report.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
436	        let warnings = exporter?.graphicWarnings ?? []
437	        let cursorWarnings = exporter?.cursorWarnings ?? []
438	        exporter = nil
439	        // The pin goes with the exporter, and from `pinnedProject` rather than
440	        // from the job, so that releasing it cannot depend on the job still
441	        // being in the list. Exactly one release per `launch`, which is what
442	        // `ReverseSource.pin` asks for; a pin left behind would retain the
443	        // Rust project for the life of the process.
444	        if let pinned = pinnedProject {
445	            ReverseSource.shared.unpin(pinned)
446	            pinnedProject = nil
447	        }
448	        if let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) {
449	            jobs[index].phase = nil
450	            switch result {
451	            case .success(let url):
452	                jobs[index].state = .completed
453	                jobs[index].progress = 1
454	                jobs[index].graphicWarnings = warnings
455	                jobs[index].cursorWarnings = cursorWarnings
456	                jobs[index].loudness = report
457	                // The count BEFORE the loudness figures: the row truncates
458	                // its tail (`ExportQueueRowView`).
459	                jobs[index].message = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”\(ExportStemsPipeline.summary(jobs[index].settings))."
460	                    + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings, hover: false)
461	                    + Exporter.cursorWarningSuffix(cursorWarnings, hover: false) + measured
462	            case .failure(let error):
463	                if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
464	                    // A cancelled job leaves nothing behind, and this line is
465	                    // DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than the thing that achieves it
466	                    // — measured, because the obvious reading is wrong and a
467	                    // reader who believes it would be relying on a guarantee
468	                    // this line does not provide. Both pipelines already
469	                    // clean up after themselves: `AVAssetWriter.cancelWriting()`
470	                    // removes its own part-file (`ExporterWriter.swift` says
471	                    // so where it calls it) and `ImageSequenceWriter.report`
472	                    // removes its own. Deleting this line changes no observable
473	                    // outcome — phase 7's proof mutated it away and scored
474	                    // 77/77 — so the check beside it is written as the OUTCOME
475	                    // ("nothing is left behind") and not as a guard on this
476	                    // call. Keep it: it costs nothing, it states the policy
477	                    // where the policy is decided, and it is what holds if a
478	                    // third pipeline ever arrives that is less tidy.
479	                    // `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` is the same line
480	                    // for the same reason.
481	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: jobs[index].destination)
482	                    jobs[index].state = .cancelled
483	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
484	                    jobs[index].message = "Cancelled."
485	                } else {
486	                    jobs[index].state = .failed
487	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
488	                    jobs[index].message = error.localizedDescription
489	                }
490	            }
491	        }
492	        didChange()
493	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch and book the next job.
494	        let token = ledgerToken
495	        ledgerToken = nil
496	        ledger.end(token)
497	        start()
498	    }
499	
500	    // MARK: - Stopping and tidying
501	
502	    /// Stops one job, whether it has started or not.
503	    ///
504	    /// A WAITING job is simply marked: it has no exporter to stop and no file
505	    /// to remove, because nothing has been written under its name. A RUNNING
506	    /// one is asked to stop and answers through `finished`, which is where its
507	    /// file is removed — one exit, so a cancel from the window and a cancel
508	    /// from a script clean up identically. A finished job is left alone.
509	    func cancel(_ id: UInt64) {
510	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
511	        switch jobs[index].state {
512	        case .waiting:
513	            jobs[index].state = .cancelled
514	            jobs[index].message = "Cancelled before it started."
515	            didChange()
516	        case .running:
517	            jobs[index].message = "Stopping…"
518	            exporter?.cancel()
519	            didChange()
520	        case .completed, .cancelled, .failed:
521	            break
522	        }
523	    }
524	
525	    /// Stops everything. The WAITING jobs go first and the running one last,
526	    /// and the order is load-bearing: cancelling the running job posts its
527	    /// completion, and a completion starts the next waiting job — so stopping
528	    /// the writer first would start the very jobs this is meant to stop.
529	    func cancelAll() {
530	        for job in jobs where job.state == .waiting { cancel(job.id) }
531	        if let running = runningJob { cancel(running.id) }
532	    }
533	
534	    /// Drops one finished row. A job still waiting or running is not removed —
535	    /// cancel it first, which is what the window's one button does in its two
536	    /// states.
537	    func remove(_ id: UInt64) {
538	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
539	            jobs[index].state.isFinished
540	        else { return }
541	        jobs.remove(at: index)
542	        didChange()
543	    }
544	
545	    /// Drops every finished row and leaves the queue itself running.
546	    func clearFinished() {
547	        let before = jobs.count
548	        jobs.removeAll { $0.state.isFinished }
549	        if jobs.count != before { didChange() }
550	    }
551	
552	    private func didChange() {
553	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
554	    }
555	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)

  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts

  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).

  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media

  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off

  before the re-copy, `reanchoringCursorFiles` re-points a cursor file found
  again at `<package>/media/<same name>` (spec §11 CU-52).

  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

8	/// **Why a ledger and not a pool size.** The queue runs one job at a time (#326, road map
9	/// 2's 7e) and stays that way; what can run beside its job is an Export… sheet, which a
10	/// person started and which is never held (CX-18 (6)). So the question a queued AV1 or VP9
11	/// job asks is not "how many jobs" but "does the memory the others hold, with mine, fit", and
12	/// the answer has to see the sheets too — which is why the account is one shared object
13	/// both writers book into, rather than state inside `ExportQueueController`.

15	/// **The budget is a quarter of physical memory**, G-37's share for graphic rasters, so an
16	/// export's two large consumers stay within half the Mac together. A job is admitted when
17	/// nothing is booked — one export always runs, however large — or when the booked costs and
18	/// its own fit.

40	    }
41	
42	    /// What bundled-encoder exports may hold together, in bytes.
43	    var budget: UInt64 { Self.budget(physicalMemory: physicalMemory) }
44	
45	    /// Each running booking's cost, in booking order.
46	    var runningCosts: [UInt64] { entries.map(\.cost) }
47	
48	    // MARK: - The rule
49	
50	    /// A quarter of physical memory (CX-18 (3)).
51	    static func budget(physicalMemory: UInt64) -> UInt64 { physicalMemory / 4 }
52	
53	    /// Whether a job costing `cost` may start beside `running`: always when nothing runs,
54	    /// else when the sum fits `budget` (CX-18 (5)).
55	    static func admits(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> Bool {
56	        guard !running.isEmpty else { return true }
57	        let (inUse, over) = running.reduce((UInt64(0), false)) { sum, next in
58	            let added = sum.0.addingReportingOverflow(next)
59	            return (added.partialValue, sum.1 || added.overflow)
60	        }
61	        let total = inUse.addingReportingOverflow(cost)
62	        return !over && !total.overflow && total.partialValue <= budget
63	    }
64	
65	    /// The held job's sentence: what runs, what the Mac allows, what this one needs.
66	    static func waitingSentence(cost: UInt64, running: [UInt64], budget: UInt64) -> String {
67	        let inUse = running.reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 &+ $1 }
68	        return "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about "
69	            + "\(gigabytes(inUse)) of the \(gigabytes(budget)) this Mac allows them, and this "
70	            + "one needs about \(gigabytes(cost))."
71	    }
72	
73	    private static func gigabytes(_ bytes: UInt64) -> String {
74	        String(format: "%.1f GB", Double(bytes) / 1_073_741_824)
75	    }
76	
77	    // MARK: - Asking
78	
79	    /// Whether `settings` may start now, leaving out the booking `token` (the queue's own
80	    /// running job, which a waiting job is behind anyway). True for an AVFoundation row.
81	    func admits(_ settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> Bool {
82	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return true }
83	        return Self.admits(
84	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
85	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
86	    }
87	
88	    /// The held sentence for `settings`, or nil when it is admitted.
89	    func waitingSentence(for settings: ExportSettings, ignoring token: UInt64? = nil) -> String? {
90	        guard !admits(settings, ignoring: token) else { return nil }
91	        return Self.waitingSentence(
92	            cost: ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget),
93	            running: costs(ignoring: token), budget: budget)
94	    }
95	
96	    private func costs(ignoring token: UInt64?) -> [UInt64] {
97	        entries.filter { $0.token != token }.map(\.cost)
98	    }
99	
100	    // MARK: - Booking
101	
102	    /// Books an export about to start and answers its token, or nil — booking nothing —
103	    /// for an AVFoundation row. Called BEFORE `Exporter.export`, whose early refusals finish
104	    /// synchronously inside it.
105	    func begin(_ settings: ExportSettings) -> UInt64? {
106	        guard settings.writer != nil else { return nil }
107	        let token = nextToken
108	        nextToken += 1
109	        entries.append(
110	            (token, ExportEncoderCosts.memoryBytes(for: settings, budget: budget)))
111	        post()
112	        return token
113	    }
114	
115	    /// Ends a booking. A nil or unknown token is a no-op; a removal posts, and the queue's
116	    /// observer may launch its next job — and book it — inside this call, which is why a
117	    /// caller clears its own token BEFORE calling this.
118	    func end(_ token: UInt64?) {
119	        guard let token, let index = entries.firstIndex(where: { $0.token == token }) else {
120	            return
121	        }
122	        entries.remove(at: index)
123	        post()
124	    }
125	
126	    private func post() {
127	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
128	    }
129	}

183	    /// screen syncs**, and `show()` was not everything. `isVisible` is false
184	    /// for a MINIATURIZED window and for every window of a HIDDEN app (⌘H

192	    /// three notifications rather than one because there are three ways back.

199	    /// dropped. Unconditional and idempotent: `sync` rebuilds only when the
200	    /// job IDS have changed, so paying for it on every key change is cheaper

206	    private func sync() {
207	        let jobs = queue.jobs
208	        let ids = jobs.map { $0.id }
209	        if ids != rowOrder { rebuild(jobs) }
210	        for job in jobs { rows[job.id]?.update(job) }
211	
212	        emptyLabel.isHidden = !jobs.isEmpty
213	        let finished = jobs.filter { $0.state.isFinished }.count
214	        clearButton.isEnabled = finished > 0
215	        cancelAllButton.isEnabled = !queue.isIdle
216	        summaryLabel.stringValue = Self.summary(
217	            running: queue.runningJob != nil, waiting: queue.waitingCount, finished: finished)

225	        var parts: [String] = []
226	        if running { parts.append("1 exporting") }
227	        if waiting > 0 { parts.append("\(waiting) waiting") }
228	        if finished > 0 { parts.append("\(finished) finished") }
229	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")

380	    /// Repaints from the job. Called on every change notification, so it must
381	    /// be cheap and must not rebuild anything.

390	        // beside it for a file that actually landed.

395	    /// The full path and what the file will be — the row is narrow and the
396	    /// name alone cannot say which of two exports of one project this is —
397	    /// then the memory hold's whole sentence while a job waits on it (the status label
398	    /// truncates its tail, so the row alone may cut it short; CX-18), then each graphic
399	    /// warning a completed job gave, one per line, then each cursor warning (spec §11 CU-38 (c)).
400	    static func toolTip(for job: ExportQueueController.Job) -> String {
401	        var tip =
402	            job.destination.path + "\n"
403	            + "\(job.settings.container.uppercased()) · \(job.settings.width) × "
404	            + "\(job.settings.height) · \(job.settings.fps.displayName) fps"
405	        if job.state == .waiting, let held = job.message { tip += "\n" + held }
406	        if let graphics = Exporter.graphicWarningDetails(job.graphicWarnings) {
407	            tip += "\n" + graphics
408	        }
409	        if let cursors = Exporter.cursorWarningDetails(job.cursorWarnings) {
410	            tip += "\n" + cursors
411	        }
412	        return tip
413	    }

415	    /// The row's status line; internal so a probe reads it (CX-18).
416	    static func status(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) -> String {
417	        switch job.state {
418	        case .waiting:
419	            // The memory hold's sentence when the encoder ledger holds it (CX-18).
420	            return job.message ?? "Waiting"
421	        case .running:
422	            // A message set mid-flight ("Stopping…") is the person's own
423	            // request and outranks the percentage they stopped watching.
424	            if let message = job.message { return message }
425	            let percent = Int((min(max(job.progress, 0), 1) * 100).rounded())
426	            return "\(job.phase ?? "Writing") · \(percent) %"
427	        case .completed where job.superseded:
428	            // REPLACING the "Exported …" line rather than appending to it: the
429	            // label truncates its TAIL, so a note added on the end is the half
430	            // that disappears in a narrow window and the stale claim is the
431	            // half that survives. The row's own name already says which file.
432	            return "Overwritten by a later export to the same file."
433	        case .completed, .cancelled, .failed:
434	            return job.message ?? job.state.rawValue
435	        }
436	    }

6	/// **What is here is the URL and the thread; the WRITE is `FrameWriter`'s.**
7	/// That split is the feature's whole point: `render_frame` calls the same
8	/// `FrameWriter.writeFrame`, which labels the frame BT.709 (spec §11 PR-11)
9	/// and writes it, so the two paths cannot produce different bytes for
10	/// one frame, and a proof script — which can drive the agent but can never
11	/// press a menu item or type into a save panel — is still measuring what this
12	/// command does. Anything about the picture that ends up in this file instead
13	/// of in `FrameWriter.swift` is a place the menu and the agent can drift.
14	///
15	/// **The picture is the EDITED project's, and so is the time it is asked
16	/// for** (road map 2's phase 9). Inside a nest `document.playhead` is measured
17	/// from the NEST's own zero — `setNestPath` subtracts the nest clip's start —
18	/// while `document.project` is still the timeline, so a command that spends
19	/// one in the other names a frame nobody asked for: the timeline at a tick
20	/// counted from somewhere inside it. Two ticks, two containers, no error.
21	/// Rendering `document.editedProject` at that same tick needs no mapping at
22	/// all, because the tick is already in that project's time base, and it
23	/// restores the identity this file was split for: `render_frame` renders
24	/// `editedProject` at `document.playhead` too (`AgentServer+Render.swift`),
25	/// so the menu item and the tool still write one frame's bytes and both write
26	/// the frame the canvas is showing. With no nest open the two handles are the
27	/// same object and nothing about this command changes.
28	///
29	/// That puts Save Frame on the `editedProject` side of the split
30	/// `ProjectDocument.editedProject` documents, where an EXPORT stays on the
31	/// `project` side, and the two are not in tension: an export's subject is the
32	/// FILE, which is always the whole timeline, and a frame grab's subject is
33	/// the PICTURE, which is whatever is on the canvas. The canvas is the thing a
34	/// person is looking at when they reach for ⌥⌘E.
35	///
36	/// **The render is off-main.** `Exporter.renderFrame` opens asset tracks and
37	/// decodes, and its own doc says to call it off the main thread;
38	/// `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` is the seam this copies (:77-81 for
39	/// the queue, :187-194 for the hop out and back), down to the reason for a
40	/// queue of its own rather than the compositor's build queue — a grab must not
41	/// be stuck behind a preview rebuild, and a preview rebuild must not be stuck
42	/// behind a grab. It is a SECOND queue object rather than the eyedropper's
43	/// because that one is `private` to its file, and widening it would put two
44	/// unrelated commands in one line for no gain; both are named in
45	/// `app/CLAUDE.md`'s seam list.
46	///
47	/// **A frame showing a deep still or a deep VP9 track is saved deep** (spec
48	/// §11 PR-9, PR-12): a PNG or HEIC passes `keepsDepth`, the same expression
49	/// `render_frame` passes (`format.carriesDepth`), and `renderFrame` reads such
50	/// a frame through the reader, so the two still write one frame's bytes; a
51	/// JPEG never does.
52	///
53	/// The hop back does nothing on success: a save panel that has written the
54	/// file the person named has said everything it has to say. A failure gets an
55	/// alert naming the path, which is why `FrameWriter` throws rather than
56	/// answering a bare `false`.
57	///
58	/// **Save Frame passes NO timecode burn-in**, and the asymmetry is deliberate:
59	/// the export sheet and the `export` tool burn one in when asked, and
60	/// `render_frame` carries the option too (agent parity, and the only way a
61	/// script can photograph a burn-in), while this command never offers it —
62	/// a frame grab is a grab of the PICTURE, not of a review deliverable, and a
63	/// still somebody is about to put in a document should not arrive stamped.
64	/// It reaches that by calling `Exporter.renderFrame` WITHOUT its `options`
65	/// argument, whose default is `RecipeOptions.none`; if that default were ever
66	/// taken away this file would stop compiling, which is the right way for the
67	/// question to be asked again.
68	extension EditorViewController {
69	
70	    /// One frame composed for one file is a decode, not a redraw — the
71	    /// eyedropper's argument for its own queue, and the same answer here.
72	    private static let frameGrabQueue = DispatchQueue(
73	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.saveframe", qos: .userInitiated)
74	
75	    // MARK: - The command
76	
77	    /// File ▸ Save Frame…. A selector declared `@objc` on an extension needs
78	    /// no forward in the frozen `EditorViewController.swift` (`pickChromaKey`
79	    /// is the precedent); only the validator arm is wired there, in one line.
80	    @objc func saveFrame(_ sender: Any?) { saveFrameCommand() }
81	
82	    /// The panel, then the render, then the write.
83	    ///
84	    /// The refusals happen HERE, ahead of the panel, which is
85	    /// `removeSilencesCommand`'s rule: a save panel whose only possible answer
86	    /// is "there is nothing at the playhead to save" should not open at all.
87	    /// The test is the validator's — a zero-duration project is the one
88	    /// `Exporter.renderFrame` answers nil for — and it is asked of the project
89	    /// that will be RENDERED, which inside a nest is the nest: a person who
90	    /// has emptied the nest they are inside is looking at a blank canvas, and
91	    /// the timeline's own duration would open a panel for a frame that cannot
92	    /// be composed.
93	    func saveFrameCommand() {
94	        guard let document = document, let window = view.window,
95	              window.attachedSheet == nil, document.editedProject.duration > 0
96	        else {
97	            NSSound.beep()
98	            return
99	        }
100	        // The TIME is fixed here and nowhere else. It is the person's own
101	        // choice, it is spelled into the name they are about to edit, and a
102	        // frame grab whose file disagrees with its own filename is worse than
103	        // one taken a moment early — so unlike the project below, the playhead
104	        // is not re-read when the panel comes back. It is left exactly as the
105	        // document holds it, which inside a nest means the nest's own time
106	        // (see the type doc): the render below is handed the same container,
107	        // so there is nothing to map, and the timecode in the name is the one
108	        // the toolbar and the ruler were showing when ⌥⌘E was pressed.
109	        let time = max(0, document.playhead)
110	        // The canvas the time is MEASURED in, for the same reason. A nest
111	        // borrows the parent's `fps` and `timecode_frames` (`core/src/
112	        // scope.rs`'s table — only the width and height are the nest's), so
113	        // the two canvases spell a tick identically and this line changes no
114	        // name; it is written this way to say which container the tick came
115	        // from, so the next person to touch it does not have to work it out.
116	        //
117	        // The base is `displayStem`: the title with the package's own
118	        // extension off and NOTHING else off. A bare `deletingPathExtension`
119	        // stood here and offered "Board v1.2" as `Board v1 ….png` — the same
120	        // character the format popup below used to eat, fixed on the same
121	        // terms (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
122	        let stem = frameStem(
123	            base: document.displayStem, at: time,
124	            canvas: document.editedProject.snapshot.canvas)
125	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
126	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = "\(stem).\(FrameWriter.Format.png.fileExtension)"
127	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
128	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
129	        panel.allowedContentTypes = [FrameWriter.Format.png.contentType]
130	        panel.message = "Write the frame at the playhead as a still image."
131	        let options = SaveFrameOptions(panel: panel, stem: stem)
132	        panel.accessoryView = options.view
133	        // The completion is what keeps `options` alive: the panel retains the
134	        // accessory VIEW, not the object whose action the format popup calls,
135	        // and a deallocated target would leave a live popup that changes
136	        // nothing (`CaptionExportOptions`' note, and the same hazard).
137	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
138	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
139	            self?.renderAndWriteFrame(
140	                from: document, at: time, format: options.format, to: url, in: window)
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    /// The suggested name: the document's, then the timecode of the frame
145	    /// being saved.
146	    ///
147	    /// A frame grab named after the project alone collides with the previous
148	    /// one every single time, and a save panel's answer to a collision is a
149	    /// replace-or-cancel alert — so the default name would train a person to
150	    /// retype it. The time is spelled by `ReelTime.format` under the canvas's
151	    /// own `timecode_frames`, because the toolbar and the ruler spell it that
152	    /// way and inventing a second spelling of a time is the thing that
153	    /// formatter exists to prevent.
154	    ///
155	    /// The colons come out. A colon is legal in a POSIX path and is exactly
156	    /// what a person would type, but the Finder renders one as `/` — so a file
157	    /// saved as `Talk 00:00:04:12.png` is listed as `Talk 00/00/04/12.png` and
158	    /// reads as four folders that are not there.
159	    private func frameStem(base: String, at t: Ticks, canvas: CanvasSnapshot) -> String {
160	        let time = ReelTime.format(t, fps: canvas.fps, frames: canvas.timecodeFrames)
161	        let safe = time.replacingOccurrences(of: ":", with: "-")
162	        return base.isEmpty ? safe : "\(base) \(safe)"
163	    }
164	
165	    // MARK: - The render
166	
167	    /// Reads the document on the main thread, composes off it, and comes back
168	    /// with a URL or an error.
169	    ///
170	    /// The PROJECT is read here rather than captured when the panel opened,
171	    /// which is `CaptionExporter`'s rule and holds for its reason: a save
172	    /// panel is window-modal, so nothing the person does can change the
173	    /// document under it, but an agent's edit can (MCP runs on the main
174	    /// thread and a sheet does not stop it), and what the project says NOW is
175	    /// what should land. The `t` it is asked about came the other way, from
176	    /// the command — see `saveFrameCommand`, where the reason is written down.
177	    ///
178	    /// It is the EDITED project, which is the whole of phase 9's correction
179	    /// here and is argued in the type doc: `time` is measured in whatever
180	    /// container is open, so this is the one handle it can be spent against.
181	    /// One seam is left open by that pairing and is named rather than
182	    /// guarded: an agent's `set_scope` between the panel opening and its OK
183	    /// would spend the old container's tick in the new container. It is the
184	    /// agent-only half of a race this method already documents for edits, the
185	    /// window-modal panel rules the person out, and the honest guard for it
186	    /// would be a second opinion here about which container a tick belongs
187	    /// to — which is `ProjectDocument`'s to hold, and holding it twice is
188	    /// what made this file wrong in the first place.
189	    private func renderAndWriteFrame(
190	        from document: ProjectDocument, at time: Ticks, format: FrameWriter.Format,
191	        to url: URL, in window: NSWindow
192	    ) {
193	        let project = document.editedProject
194	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
195	        let graphics = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
196	        EditorViewController.frameGrabQueue.async { [weak self] in
197	            let result: Result<URL, Error>
198	            // `render_frame`'s expression, so the two stay one frame's bytes: a
199	            // JPEG of an HLG project is its SDR version (spec §11 HD-14 (e)).
200	            let options = RecipeOptions.none.forFrame(format, output: project.snapshot.canvas.output)
201	            // A cut-out clip waits up to 30 s for its masks (spec §11 CO-22 (f)).
202	            let rendered = Exporter.renderFrameReported(
203	                project: project, urls: urls, at: time, maxWidth: nil, options: options,
204	                graphics: graphics, keepsDepth: format.carriesDepth,
205	                cutoutWait: Exporter.frameCutoutWait)
206	            if let image = rendered.image {
207	                result = Result { try FrameWriter.writeFrame(image, as: format, to: url) }
208	            } else {
209	                result = .failure(SaveFrameError.noFrame)
210	            }
211	            let uncut = Self.uncutNote(rendered.uncut, in: project.snapshot)
212	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.frameSaved(result, in: window, uncut: uncut) }
213	        }
214	    }
215	
216	    /// Back on the main thread. Success is silent — the file is where the
217	    /// person put it — unless a cut-out clip was drawn whole because its
218	    /// masks were not ready (`uncut`, its media's file names; spec §11 CO-22
219	    /// (f)), which an informational sheet says; a failure is an alert on the
220	    /// window that asked. The whole path mutates nothing, so there is no undo
221	    /// step to group and none of `performGroupedEdit`'s off-event machinery
222	    /// applies.
223	    func frameSaved(
224	        _ result: Result<URL, Error>, in window: NSWindow, uncut: UncutFrameNote = UncutFrameNote()
225	    ) {
226	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else {
227	            if !uncut.isEmpty { showUncutFrameNote(uncut, in: window) }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        let alert = NSAlert(error: error)
231	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
232	    }
233	
234	    /// What the sheet after a save that drew cut-out clips whole says (CO-22 (f)): the uncut
235	    /// clips' media file names, and the noun of their masks (CO-106).
236	    struct UncutFrameNote {
237	        var names: [String] = []
238	        var noun = "person masks"
239	        var isEmpty: Bool { names.isEmpty }
240	    }
241	
242	    /// The sheet after a save that drew cut-out clips whole (CO-22 (f)).
243	    private func showUncutFrameNote(_ note: UncutFrameNote, in window: NSWindow) {
244	        let alert = NSAlert()
245	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
246	        alert.messageText = "Saved without Remove Background"
247	        alert.informativeText = note.names.joined(separator: ", ")
248	            + " drawn whole: the \(note.noun) were not ready within 30 seconds."
249	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
250	    }
251	
252	    /// The uncut clips' names for the sheet — each one's media file name, in order, each once —
253	    /// and the noun: "person masks" when no uncut clip is a foreground picture, "foreground
254	    /// masks" when every one is, "masks" otherwise (`CutoutWants.kind(of:)`, CO-106).
255	    private static func uncutNote(_ clips: [UInt32], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
256	        -> UncutFrameNote
257	    {
258	        let all = snapshot.clips + snapshot.nests.flatMap(\.clips)
259	        var note = UncutFrameNote()
260	        var foreground = 0, uncut = 0
261	        for id in clips {
262	            guard let clip = all.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else { continue }
263	            uncut += 1
264	            if CutoutWants.kind(of: clip) == .foreground { foreground += 1 }
265	            guard let name = snapshot.media(for: clip)?.name, !note.names.contains(name)
266	            else { continue }
267	            note.names.append(name)
268	        }
269	        if foreground > 0 { note.noun = foreground == uncut ? "foreground masks" : "masks" }
270	        return note
271	    }
272	
273	    // MARK: - Validation
274	
275	    /// The half of `validateUserInterfaceItem` this file owns. `nil` means
276	    /// "not mine" and leaves the other answers alone — which is why the
277	    /// document is read INSIDE the arm rather than guarded ahead of the
278	    /// switch: an arm that answered `false` with no document would be
279	    /// answering for every other command in the chain as well.
280	    ///
281	    /// The arm is load-bearing, not decoration. Without it Save Frame… falls
282	    /// through to `validateUserInterfaceItem`'s closing `return true` and is
283	    /// live on an empty timeline, where it can only open a panel and then put
284	    /// up an alert. `duration > 0` is the honest test because it is exactly
285	    /// the question `Exporter.renderFrame` refuses on: a plan of zero length
286	    /// has no frame at any time. Nothing else about the timeline can be asked
287	    /// cheaply and answered correctly here — a project whose visible clips are
288	    /// all text, shapes or images DOES render (`CompositionBuilder` gives it a
289	    /// placeholder track), so a "has a video track" test would grey out a
290	    /// command that works.
291	    ///
292	    /// It asks the EDITED project, matching the command and the render: with
293	    /// a nest open the frame that would be written is the nest's, so an
294	    /// emptied nest inside a full timeline is exactly the case the arm exists
295	    /// for. `editedProject` is memoised per parent handle
296	    /// (`ProjectDocument`), so asking it from a validator — which runs on
297	    /// every menu update — costs a pointer comparison after the first call,
298	    /// and at the top level it IS `project`.
299	    func validateSaveFrameAction(_ action: Selector) -> Bool? {
300	        guard action == #selector(EditorViewController.saveFrame(_:)) else { return nil }
301	        return (document?.editedProject.duration ?? 0) > 0
302	    }
303	}
304	
305	// MARK: - Failures this file owns
306	
307	/// The one failure that is about the TIME rather than about the file, so it
308	/// does not belong in `FrameWriter` — which is handed an image and knows
309	/// nothing about playheads or plans.
310	private enum SaveFrameError: LocalizedError {
311	    /// `Exporter.renderFrame` answered nil, which it does for every reason at
312	    /// once and says nothing about which — no plan, a composition it could not
313	    /// build, a time past the end. It carries no payload for that reason: a
314	    /// tick count in an alert is noise to the person reading it, and there is
315	    /// nothing here that could turn one into the sentence that would help.
316	    case noFrame
317	
318	    var errorDescription: String? {
319	        switch self {
320	        case .noFrame:
321	            return "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the "
322	                + "timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing."
323	        }
324	    }
325	}

4	
5	/// The one choice a frame grab has — which container — carried in the save
6	/// panel's accessory view rather than in a sheet of its own.

8	/// `CaptionExportOptions` is the pattern and its argument holds here too: a
9	/// sheet for one popup would be the heavier answer, and chaining a sheet out
10	/// of a sheet is what `ReverseProgressSheetController` records as not working
11	/// in this app. The line under the popup is not decoration either — it is what
12	/// each format does with alpha, said out loud at the moment the format is
13	/// chosen, which is the only place a person with a transparent canvas
14	/// (phase 7b) will read it before the JPEG has already flattened.
15	///
16	/// It owns nothing but its controls; the panel's completion holds it for as
17	/// long as the panel is up.

19	    private weak var panel: NSSavePanel?

21	    private let formatPopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)

25

27	        self.panel = panel
28	        self.stem = stem

30	        for format in FrameWriter.Format.allCases {

32	            // The row carries the FORMAT, never its position in the list.
33	            // `NSPopUpButton.addItem(withTitle:)` removes an existing row with
34	            // the same title before adding the new one, so a popup read by
35	            // `indexOfSelectedItem` is one duplicated title away from writing
36	            // a different format than the row named and reporting success —
37	            // phase 4's measured defect, in `app/CLAUDE.md`'s pitfall list.
38	            // These three titles are distinct; reading the object makes that
39	            // stop mattering.

41	        }

43	        formatPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
44	
45	        hint.font = DS.sans(11)
46	        hint.textColor = DS.textMuted
47	        hint.isEditable = false
48	
49	        let grid = NSGridView(views: [[fieldLabel("Format:"), formatPopup]])
50	        grid.rowSpacing = 8
51	        grid.columnSpacing = 12
52	        grid.column(at: 0).xPlacement = .trailing
53	        grid.column(at: 0).width = 60
54	        grid.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
55	        hint.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
56	
57	        let container = NSView()
58	        container.addSubview(grid)
59	        container.addSubview(hint)
60	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
61	            grid.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.topAnchor, constant: 12),
62	            grid.centerXAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.centerXAnchor),
63	            hint.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: grid.bottomAnchor, constant: 6),
64	            hint.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.bottomAnchor, constant: -12),
65	            hint.centerXAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.centerXAnchor),
66	            container.widthAnchor.constraint(greaterThanOrEqualTo: grid.widthAnchor, constant: 32),
67	            container.widthAnchor.constraint(greaterThanOrEqualTo: hint.widthAnchor, constant: 32),

79	        formatPopup.action = #selector(formatChanged(_:))

83	    @available(*, unavailable)

90	    }

92	    /// The panel's filter and its name field both name the container, so both
93	    /// move together — otherwise AppKit appends `.png` to a name the person

101	    /// survives as the fallback for a field emptied to nothing.

124	    }
