3	/// The export queue (road map 2's phase 7e): the exports a person has
4	/// confirmed but does not want to sit and watch, run one after another while
5	/// the editor stays live.
6	///
7	/// **There is no AppKit in this file, and that is the design rather than
8	/// tidiness.** A queue window can be checked by neither of this project's two
9	/// instruments: the offscreen harness renders an `EditorViewController` into a
10	/// window and nothing else, and MCP drives the app through tools — and the
11	/// agent's `export` enqueues here, so a tool reaches this list but never the
12	/// window (below, spec §11 #326). What a proof CAN do is
13	/// compile a probe out of the whole of `app/Sources`
14	/// (`tools/proof/phase6_chrome.py`'s `build_probe`), make one of these,
15	/// enqueue two jobs, spin the main run loop until `isIdle` and read `jobs`
16	/// back — without an `NSWindow` ever being ordered front. So the job list and
17	/// its state machine live here, where a script can reach them, and
18	/// `ExportQueueWindowController.swift` is a READER of this and nothing else:
19	/// it holds no job, decides nothing, and closing it stops nothing.
20	/// `AudioNormalize.swift` and `CaptionLayout.swift` are the same split — the
21	/// arithmetic where a script can call it, the dialog around it — and phase 5's
22	/// level meter is the closest sibling, where the MODEL publishes a number
23	/// precisely so that a proof need not photograph a window.
24	///
25	/// **The agent's `export` is a job here (spec §11 #326).** It keeps its
26	/// refusals synchronous, then enqueues exactly as Add to Queue does and
27	/// answers the job's id at once; `export_status` follows the job and
28	/// `cancel_export` calls `cancel` (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`). The
29	/// queue's own API is unchanged by it: the mirror reads `job(_:)` and
30	/// observes `didChangeNotification` like the window does, and no tool
31	/// exists for a person's own queued job.
32	///
33	/// **One job at a time, on the MAIN thread, a fresh `Exporter` for each.**
34	/// `Exporter.export`'s own doc says main-thread-only and one export at a time,
35	/// and it means both: it schedules a run-loop `Timer` — which must be
36	/// invalidated on the thread it was scheduled on — and calls its progress and
37	/// completion handlers on the main thread. So this is a CHAIN and not a pool:
38	/// `start()` runs the head of the list and each completion runs the next. A
39	/// `DispatchQueue` of exporters would be the wrong shape whatever the machine's
40	/// core count, and not only because of the timer — an `Exporter` carries
41	/// per-export state (`recipeKey`, `cancelRequested`, the loudness scratch
42	/// buffer), which is why each job gets its own rather than one being reset
43	/// between jobs. Every method below is main-thread-only for that reason, like
44	/// the exporter it drives.
45	///
46	/// **What a job holds is the whole of what it will write, captured when it was
47	/// confirmed.** The `ReelProject` is a handle and handles are immutable (spec
48	/// §5.5) — every edit and every undo makes a NEW one — so a queued write cannot
49	/// be reached by an edit made after it, and it needs no clone: `Exporter.export`
50	/// publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key it mints for itself, never the
51	/// document's, so even the frames the compositor serves this export come from
52	/// this handle. The document may be edited, undone or CLOSED while the job
53	/// waits; the handle is retained here and the Rust project behind it lives
54	/// until the job is gone.
55	///
56	/// **And the media URLs are resolved at ENQUEUE, which is what makes them part
57	/// of that same snapshot.** `ProjectDocument.mediaURLs()` resolves a bookmark
58	/// and asks the filesystem whether the file is there (`mediaURL(for:)`), so it
59	/// is a reading of the disk at the moment it is called: resolving at RUN time
60	/// would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after the job was
61	/// queued, which is the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. That
62	/// rule is structural here rather than remembered — `enqueue` takes a
63	/// `[UInt32: URL]` and a job holds no document, so there is nothing to ask
64	/// again later even if somebody wanted to.
65	///
66	/// **The REVERSE resolution is the third thing in that snapshot, and it was
67	/// missing.** Handle immutability covers the project and nothing beside it:
68	/// which clips play from a pre-rendered backwards file is a reading of the
69	/// disk too (`ProjectDocument.reverseState`, `ReverseCache.existing`), it
70	/// cannot be derived from a bare handle, and it lives in a side table keyed by
71	/// object IDENTITY — which the document overwrites on every edit and removes
72	/// when it closes. So a job queued from a timeline holding a reversed clip
73	/// used to answer `.none` the moment anything was edited, and `.none` means
74	/// "not reversed": the export took the forward asset at the mirrored source
75	/// window, unslated and unreported. It is captured here at enqueue, exactly as
76	/// the URLs are, and PINNED to this job's own handle for the length of its
77	/// write (`ReverseSource.pin`). Anything else the picture depends on that is
78	/// neither in the handle nor derivable from it joins that list.
79	///
80	/// **A bundled-encoder job also waits for memory (spec §11 CX-18).** An AV1 or VP9 job
81	/// starts only while `ExportEncoderLedger` admits it: nothing else booked, or the running
82	/// encoder exports — an Export… sheet's beside this queue's — fitting with it in a quarter
83	/// of physical memory. A held job says why in its `message` and is PASSED OVER by a later
84	/// job the ledger admits, an AVFoundation job always; the chain stays one job at a time.
85	/// The running job is booked from just before its `export` call to its finish, and a
86	/// booking's end — the queue's own or a sheet's — re-runs `start()` through the ledger's
87	/// notification.
88	final class ExportQueueController {
89	    /// The app's one queue: the export sheet's Add to Queue fills it and
90	    /// Window ▸ Export Queue shows it.
91	    static let shared = ExportQueueController()
92	
93	    /// Where a job is. A closed set with no associated values, so the two
94	    /// readers ask it different questions without either having to spell a
95	    /// message: the window's row draws its own wording (which carries a
96	    /// percentage the state cannot know), and a probe compares the case and
97	    /// reads `Job.message` for the sentence. The raw values are the same
98	    /// strings a probe writes into its JSON answer.
99	    enum State: String {
100	        /// Queued and not started. The only state a job can be enqueued in.
101	        case waiting
102	        /// The one job an `Exporter` is running. At most one at any moment.
103	        case running
104	        /// The file landed.
105	        case completed
106	        /// Stopped by a person, either before it started or mid-write — in
107	        /// which case its half-written file has been removed.
108	        case cancelled
109	        /// The exporter refused or failed. Whatever it had written is LEFT on
110	        /// disk, which is `ExportProgressSheetController`'s posture and not a
111	        /// new one: a cancel is a person saying "not this", where a failure is
112	        /// evidence, and the file names itself in the message.
113	        case failed
114	
115	        /// Whether the job is over, however it ended — the test for "may be
116	        /// removed from the list" and for "no longer holds a project handle
117	        /// worth keeping".
118	        var isFinished: Bool { self == .completed || self == .cancelled || self == .failed }
119	    }
120	
121	    /// One confirmed export. Everything it needs was read when it was
122	    /// enqueued; see the type doc for why that is the whole point of it.
123	    struct Job {
124	        /// Monotonic within one launch. The window's rows and every method
125	        /// below address a job by this rather than by index, because a job can
126	        /// be removed from the middle of the list while a later one runs.
127	        let id: UInt64
128	        /// The timeline as it was confirmed — immutable, and retained here, so
129	        /// the document behind it may be edited, undone or closed.
130	        ///
131	        /// A FINISHED job goes on holding it, and that is a real cost stated
132	        /// rather than hidden: a handle is the project's model and not its
133	        /// media, so it is JSON-sized, and Clear Finished (or Remove) is what
134	        /// releases it along with the row that says where the file went.
135	        /// Dropping the handle at the finish would buy those bytes back and
136	        /// cost the field its `let` — an immutable job whose contents change
137	        /// once is a harder thing to reason about than a list somebody tidies.
138	        let project: ReelProject
139	        /// The media files as they resolved AT ENQUEUE.
140	        let urls: [UInt32: URL]
141	        /// Which of this timeline's clips play from a pre-rendered backwards
142	        /// file, as that resolved AT ENQUEUE — the type doc's third piece of
143	        /// the snapshot. Read from `ReverseSource` here and published back to
144	        /// it under this job's own handle while the job runs, because the
145	        /// document's copy is overwritten by the next edit and dropped when it
146	        /// closes.
147	        let reverse: ReverseResolution
148	        let settings: ExportSettings
149	        let destination: URL
150	        /// What this export asks of the PICTURE besides the timeline — the
151	        /// burn-in (`RecipeOptions`). Carried per job, because two jobs from
152	        /// one document may legitimately differ in it.
153	        let options: RecipeOptions
154	        /// The document's compiled graphics as they stood AT ENQUEUE (G-13) —
155	        /// the type doc's list again: a module saved after Add to Queue is not
156	        /// in the handle, and the document's set is swapped by that save and
157	        /// dropped when it closes. `Exporter.export` pins it for the write.
158	        let graphics: GraphicSet?
159	        var state: State = .waiting
160	        /// 0…1, and only meaningful while `state` is `.running`.
161	        var progress: Double = 0
162	        /// The line a person reads when it is over: what was written and what
163	        /// the file measured, or why it stopped — plus the one thing worth
164	        /// saying mid-flight, that a cancel is in hand. While it waits, the
165	        /// ledger's sentence when the memory limit holds it (CX-18), else nil.
166	        var message: String?
167	        /// What the exporter says it is doing right now, or nil for "writing",
168	        /// which is the caller's own wording. Today the only phase is the
169	        /// loudness measurement, which on an audio-only export is half the wait
170	        /// and the half where nothing is on disk yet.
171	        ///
172	        /// A field of its own rather than a use of `message`, because the two
173	        /// are written by different things at the same time: the progress tick
174	        /// arrives ten times a second and would otherwise wipe the "Stopping…"
175	        /// a person had just asked for.
176	        var phase: String?
177	        /// Set on a COMPLETED job when a later job starts writing to the same
178	        /// path, because from that moment this row's file is not this row's
179	        /// any more — `Exporter.startWriting` removes whatever is at the
180	        /// destination before it builds its pipeline, so the earlier export is
181	        /// gone whether the later one succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
182	        ///
183	        /// The row stops claiming "Exported …" and stops offering Show in
184	        /// Finder. It is a fact about what happened rather than a state: the
185	        /// job really did complete, and rewriting its `state` would lose that.
186	        ///
187	        /// One case marks it where the file in fact survives, and it is the
188	        /// honest direction of the two: a later job whose COMPOSITION fails to
189	        /// build returns before the delete, so nothing was destroyed. It is
190	        /// left alone rather than reached for, because knowing which failures
191	        /// precede the delete means reading `Exporter`'s stages from here, and
192	        /// a shared destination implies a shared project — a build that failed
193	        /// for job 2 would almost always have failed for job 1.
194	        var superseded: Bool = false
195	        /// What the graphics warned while a COMPLETED job's file was drawn
196	        /// (G-24 (c)): the row's count and its tooltip's list.
197	        var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
198	        var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning] = []  // spec §11 CU-37 (c)
199	        /// What a COMPLETED job's sound measured, read off its exporter at the
200	        /// finish — the figures the row's message summarises, kept whole for
201	        /// `export_status`'s `loudness` (spec §11 #326). nil otherwise.
202	        var loudness: ExportLoudness? = nil
203	
204	        /// What the row calls this job. The file name and not the path: the
205	        /// row is narrow, and the full path is the tooltip's job.
206	        var name: String { destination.lastPathComponent }
207	    }
208	
209	    /// Posted after any change to `jobs` — an enqueue, a progress tick, a
210	    /// finish, a cancel, a removal — with the controller as the `object`, so
211	    /// an observer of the shared queue is never woken by a probe's own
212	    /// instance. Main thread, like everything else here.
213	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name(
214	        "com.kgalligan.framejob.exportQueueDidChange")
215	
216	    /// Every job this launch still knows about, in the order they were added.
217	    /// A finished one stays until it is removed, because "it is done and here
218	    /// is where it went" is the queue's other job.
219	    private(set) var jobs: [Job] = []
220	
221	    /// The exporter running `runningID`'s job, and nil whenever nothing is
222	    /// running. Set and cleared together with the job's state, so `isIdle` can
223	    /// be answered from `jobs` alone.
224	    private var exporter: Exporter?
225	
226	    /// The handle whose reverse resolution is pinned in `ReverseSource` right
227	    /// now — the running job's, and nil whenever nothing is running. Held
228	    /// separately from the job so that `launch` and `finished` are provably one
229	    /// pin and one release, whatever happens to the list in between.
230	    private var pinnedProject: ReelProject?
231	
232	    /// The running job's booking in the encoder ledger (CX-18), nil whenever nothing runs
233	    /// or the running job is an AVFoundation one. Taken BEFORE `end` in `finished`: the
234	    /// ledger's post can launch — and book — the next job inside that call.
235	    private var ledgerToken: UInt64?
236	
237	    private let ledger = ExportEncoderLedger.shared
238	
239	    /// True only while `start()` is inside `Exporter.export`. An early refusal
240	    /// — `noPlan`, `emptyTimeline` — completes SYNCHRONOUSLY, so `finished`
241	    /// can run before `export` has returned; without this flag the next job
242	    /// would be launched from inside the previous one's stack frame and a
243	    /// queue of refusals would recurse as deep as it is long. With it, a
244	    /// re-entrant `start()` is refused and the frame already on the stack
245	    /// picks the next job up in its own loop.
246	    private var isLaunching = false
247	
248	    private var nextID: UInt64 = 1
249	
250	    /// Internal rather than private, and deliberately: a proof compiles a
251	    /// probe out of `app/Sources` and makes its OWN queue, so that running two
252	    /// jobs in a script cannot disturb — or be disturbed by — the app's shared
253	    /// one. It is the same reason `ExportPresetsStore` is a value a test can
254	    /// make.
255	    init() {
256	        // A booking's end — a sheet's as much as this queue's — may admit a held job.
257	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
258	            self, selector: #selector(ledgerChanged(_:)),
259	            name: ExportEncoderLedger.didChangeNotification, object: ledger)
260	    }
261	
262	    @objc private func ledgerChanged(_ note: Notification) { start() }
263	
264	    @available(*, unavailable)
265	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
266	        fatalError("ExportQueueController does not support NSCoder")
267	    }
268	
269	    // MARK: - Asking
270	
271	    /// Nothing waiting and nothing running. The queue's own "are we there
272	    /// yet", and what a probe spins the run loop until.
273	    ///
274	    /// Answered from `jobs` rather than from `exporter`, so it means the same
275	    /// thing to a caller that cannot see the private state.
276	    var isIdle: Bool {
277	        !jobs.contains { $0.state == .waiting || $0.state == .running }
278	    }
279	
280	    /// The job an exporter is writing right now, if any.
281	    var runningJob: Job? { jobs.first { $0.state == .running } }
282	
283	    /// How many are still queued behind it.
284	    var waitingCount: Int { jobs.filter { $0.state == .waiting }.count }
285	
286	    func job(_ id: UInt64) -> Job? { jobs.first { $0.id == id } }
287	
288	    // MARK: - Filling
289	
290	    /// Adds one confirmed export and starts the queue if it is not already
291	    /// running. Answers the job's id, so a caller can follow it.
292	    ///
293	    /// The arguments are `Exporter.export`'s, and that is not a coincidence:
294	    /// a job is exactly the call that will be made, held until its turn. Both
295	    /// `project` and `urls` are read by the CALLER, at the moment the save
296	    /// panel answered (`EditorViewController.enqueueExport`), which is what
297	    /// the type doc means by capturing at enqueue.
298	    ///
299	    /// **Two jobs may name one file, and the queue still does not refuse it —
300	    /// but it no longer pretends the person was warned.** The reason first
301	    /// given here was that "the save panel asked about replacing an existing
302	    /// file both times", and that is false in exactly the case that matters:
303	    /// `NSSavePanel` prompts only when something is at the path as Save is
304	    /// confirmed, and job 1 spends its build and its whole loudness
305	    /// measurement pass with nothing at the destination — `Exporter.export`
306	    /// does both before `startWriting` deletes and `AVAssetWriter` creates —
307	    /// so two Add to Queue actions in quick succession are never asked
308	    /// anything. Refusing here would still be wrong: overwriting your own
309	    /// export is a thing a person is allowed to do, and the queue must not be
310	    /// the one place in the app where they may not. What was wrong was the
311	    /// silence AFTERWARDS, and `launch` is where that is answered — the
312	    /// earlier row is marked `superseded` the moment a later job starts
313	    /// writing to its path, so no row goes on offering a file that another
314	    /// job has since deleted or replaced.
315	    @discardableResult
316	    func enqueue(
317	        project: ReelProject, urls: [UInt32: URL], settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL,
318	        options: RecipeOptions = .none, graphics: GraphicSet? = nil
319	    ) -> UInt64 {
320	        let id = nextID
321	        nextID += 1
322	        jobs.append(
323	            Job(
324	                id: id, project: project, urls: urls,
325	                // The third piece of the enqueue-time snapshot; the type doc
326	                // says why it cannot be left to be asked again at run time.
327	                reverse: ReverseSource.shared.resolution(publishedFor: project),
328	                settings: settings, destination: url, options: options, graphics: graphics))
329	        didChange()
330	        start()
331	        return id
332	    }
333	
334	    // MARK: - Running
335	
336	    /// Runs the first waiting job the encoder ledger admits, if nothing is
337	    /// running already — passing over a held one (CX-18 (7)). Idempotent
338	    /// and safe to call at any time: `enqueue` calls it, every completion
339	    /// calls it, the ledger's change calls it, and a caller may call it itself.
340	    ///
341	    /// The loop is for the synchronous-refusal case `isLaunching` describes: a
342	    /// job the exporter refuses without ever going asynchronous has already
343	    /// finished by the time `launch` returns, and this frame takes the next
344	    /// one rather than recursing into it.
345	    func start() {
346	        guard !isLaunching else { return }
347	        isLaunching = true
348	        defer { isLaunching = false }
349	        while exporter == nil, let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: {
350	            $0.state == .waiting && ledger.admits($0.settings)
351	        }) {
352	            launch(at: index)
353	        }
354	        noteHeld()
355	    }
356	
357	    /// Every waiting encoder job's `message` set to why it is held, or cleared when it is
358	    /// not — leaving out this queue's own running booking, which it waits behind anyway.
359	    private func noteHeld() {
360	        var changed = false
361	        for index in jobs.indices
362	        where jobs[index].state == .waiting && jobs[index].settings.writer != nil {
363	            let sentence = ledger.waitingSentence(for: jobs[index].settings, ignoring: ledgerToken)
364	            if jobs[index].message != sentence {
365	                jobs[index].message = sentence
366	                changed = true
367	            }
368	        }
369	        if changed { didChange() }
370	    }
371	
372	    /// One job handed to one fresh `Exporter`. The exporter is stored BEFORE
373	    /// the call, because an early refusal calls back before `export` returns
374	    /// and `finished` has to find it there.
375	    private func launch(at index: Int) {
376	        let job = jobs[index]
377	        jobs[index].state = .running
378	        jobs[index].progress = 0
379	        jobs[index].message = nil
380	        jobs[index].phase = nil
381	        // Any COMPLETED row naming this same path stops claiming its file
382	        // here, and here rather than when the file is actually deleted: the
383	        // delete happens inside `Exporter.startWriting`, seconds later and in
384	        // a file this one may not reach into, and being early is the honest
385	        // direction — a row that stops offering a file just before it is
386	        // destroyed costs a person nothing, where one that offers it just
387	        // after sends them to the Finder for something that is gone.
388	        for other in jobs.indices
389	        where other != index && jobs[other].state == .completed
390	            && jobs[other].destination == job.destination
391	        {
392	            jobs[other].superseded = true
393	        }
394	        // The job's own reverse resolution, held against its own handle for
395	        // exactly the length of this write. At most one pin exists at a time,
396	        // which is the invariant `ReverseSource.pin` asks its callers for and
397	        // which this class keeps for free by running one job at a time.
398	        ReverseSource.shared.pin(job.reverse, for: job.project)
399	        pinnedProject = job.project
400	        // Booked BEFORE `export`, whose early refusals finish synchronously inside it.
401	        ledgerToken = ledger.begin(job.settings)
402	        let exporter = Exporter()
403	        self.exporter = exporter
404	        didChange()
405	        exporter.export(
406	            project: job.project, urls: job.urls, settings: job.settings, to: job.destination,
407	            options: job.options, graphics: job.graphics,
408	            progress: { [weak self] value in self?.progressed(job.id, value) },
409	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.finished(job.id, result) })
410	    }
411	
412	    private func progressed(_ id: UInt64, _ value: Double) {
413	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
414	            jobs[index].state == .running
415	        else { return }
416	        jobs[index].progress = min(max(value, 0), 1)
417	        // The exporter names its own phase while it has one. The progress
418	        // sheet asks the same question with the same call; a row that said
419	        // "Writing" through the measurement would be claiming a file that does
420	        // not exist yet.
421	        jobs[index].phase = exporter?.phaseDescription
422	        didChange()
423	    }
424	
425	    /// The one exit for all three outcomes, and the mirror of
426	    /// `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` — deliberately, because there
427	    /// must not be two accounts of what finishing an export means. The
428	    /// exporter is cleared first, so the `start()` at the foot can hand the
429	    /// next job a fresh one.
430	    private func finished(_ id: UInt64, _ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
431	        // Read BEFORE the exporter is dropped: `Exporter.finish` publishes the
432	        // measurement and then calls this, so the report is there now and only
433	        // now.
434	        let report = exporter?.loudnessReport
435	        let measured = report.map { " \($0.summary)." } ?? ""
436	        let warnings = exporter?.graphicWarnings ?? []
437	        let cursorWarnings = exporter?.cursorWarnings ?? []
438	        exporter = nil
439	        // The pin goes with the exporter, and from `pinnedProject` rather than
440	        // from the job, so that releasing it cannot depend on the job still
441	        // being in the list. Exactly one release per `launch`, which is what
442	        // `ReverseSource.pin` asks for; a pin left behind would retain the
443	        // Rust project for the life of the process.
444	        if let pinned = pinnedProject {
445	            ReverseSource.shared.unpin(pinned)
446	            pinnedProject = nil
447	        }
448	        if let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) {
449	            jobs[index].phase = nil
450	            switch result {
451	            case .success(let url):
452	                jobs[index].state = .completed
453	                jobs[index].progress = 1
454	                jobs[index].graphicWarnings = warnings
455	                jobs[index].cursorWarnings = cursorWarnings
456	                jobs[index].loudness = report
457	                // The count BEFORE the loudness figures: the row truncates
458	                // its tail (`ExportQueueRowView`).
459	                jobs[index].message = "Exported “\(url.lastPathComponent)”\(ExportStemsPipeline.summary(jobs[index].settings))."
460	                    + Exporter.graphicWarningSuffix(warnings, hover: false)
461	                    + Exporter.cursorWarningSuffix(cursorWarnings, hover: false) + measured
462	            case .failure(let error):
463	                if case Exporter.ExportError.cancelled = error {
464	                    // A cancelled job leaves nothing behind, and this line is
465	                    // DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than the thing that achieves it
466	                    // — measured, because the obvious reading is wrong and a
467	                    // reader who believes it would be relying on a guarantee
468	                    // this line does not provide. Both pipelines already
469	                    // clean up after themselves: `AVAssetWriter.cancelWriting()`
470	                    // removes its own part-file (`ExporterWriter.swift` says
471	                    // so where it calls it) and `ImageSequenceWriter.report`
472	                    // removes its own. Deleting this line changes no observable
473	                    // outcome — phase 7's proof mutated it away and scored
474	                    // 77/77 — so the check beside it is written as the OUTCOME
475	                    // ("nothing is left behind") and not as a guard on this
476	                    // call. Keep it: it costs nothing, it states the policy
477	                    // where the policy is decided, and it is what holds if a
478	                    // third pipeline ever arrives that is less tidy.
479	                    // `ExportProgressSheetController.finished` is the same line
480	                    // for the same reason.
481	                    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: jobs[index].destination)
482	                    jobs[index].state = .cancelled
483	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
484	                    jobs[index].message = "Cancelled."
485	                } else {
486	                    jobs[index].state = .failed
487	                    jobs[index].progress = 0
488	                    jobs[index].message = error.localizedDescription
489	                }
490	            }
491	        }
492	        didChange()
493	        // Cleared before `end`, whose post may launch and book the next job.
494	        let token = ledgerToken
495	        ledgerToken = nil
496	        ledger.end(token)
497	        start()
498	    }

500	    // MARK: - Stopping and tidying
501	
502	    /// Stops one job, whether it has started or not.
503	    ///
504	    /// A WAITING job is simply marked: it has no exporter to stop and no file
505	    /// to remove, because nothing has been written under its name. A RUNNING
506	    /// one is asked to stop and answers through `finished`, which is where its
507	    /// file is removed — one exit, so a cancel from the window and a cancel
508	    /// from a script clean up identically. A finished job is left alone.
509	    func cancel(_ id: UInt64) {
510	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
511	        switch jobs[index].state {
512	        case .waiting:
513	            jobs[index].state = .cancelled
514	            jobs[index].message = "Cancelled before it started."
515	            didChange()
516	        case .running:
517	            jobs[index].message = "Stopping…"
518	            exporter?.cancel()
519	            didChange()
520	        case .completed, .cancelled, .failed:
521	            break
522	        }
523	    }
524	
525	    /// Stops everything. The WAITING jobs go first and the running one last,
526	    /// and the order is load-bearing: cancelling the running job posts its
527	    /// completion, and a completion starts the next waiting job — so stopping
528	    /// the writer first would start the very jobs this is meant to stop.
529	    func cancelAll() {
530	        for job in jobs where job.state == .waiting { cancel(job.id) }
531	        if let running = runningJob { cancel(running.id) }
532	    }
533	
534	    /// Drops one finished row. A job still waiting or running is not removed —
535	    /// cancel it first, which is what the window's one button does in its two
536	    /// states.
537	    func remove(_ id: UInt64) {
538	        guard let index = jobs.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }),
539	            jobs[index].state.isFinished
540	        else { return }
541	        jobs.remove(at: index)
542	        didChange()
543	    }
544	
545	    /// Drops every finished row and leaves the queue itself running.
546	    func clearFinished() {
547	        let before = jobs.count
548	        jobs.removeAll { $0.state.isFinished }
549	        if jobs.count != before { didChange() }
550	    }
551	
552	    private func didChange() {
553	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChangeNotification, object: self)
554	    }
555	}

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

1	import CoreGraphics
2	import CoreVideo
3	import Foundation
4	import ImageIO
5	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
6	
7	/// One composed frame written to a file: a `CGImage` and a format in, a URL
8	/// out (road map 2 phase 7a).
9	///
10	/// It is `AudioNormalize.swift`'s shape applied to pictures, and it is a value
11	/// type for the same reason that one is. **File ▸ Save Frame… and the agent's
12	/// `render_frame` call this and nothing else**, so "Save Frame's PNG is
13	/// byte-identical to `render_frame`'s" is a fact about the code rather than a
14	/// claim in a comment — and it is the only way the line can ever be checked,
15	/// because a save panel cannot be driven over MCP or offscreen and a proof
16	/// script can therefore never press the menu item. Anything that goes in here
17	/// changes both paths at once; anything that lives in only one of them is a
18	/// place the two can drift.
19	///
20	/// So there is deliberately **no `NSSavePanel`, no `ProjectDocument` and no
21	/// AppKit view in this file**. Picking the URL is
22	/// `EditorViewController+SaveFrame.swift`'s job and naming a temporary file is
23	/// `AgentServer+Render.swift`'s; both hand the result here.
24	///
25	/// **PNG's properties dictionary is `nil`, and it must stay `nil`.** That is
26	/// what `render_frame` has always passed (`AgentServer+Render.swift`), and
27	/// every phase from 1 to 6 compares PNG bytes against frames written that
28	/// way. Anything that ADDS metadata changes the file: phase 7's proof
29	/// mutated this to `[kCGImagePropertyDPIWidth: 144]` and caught it by the
30	/// extra `pHYs` chunk.
31	///
32	/// The honest limit, measured rather than assumed, because the sentence
33	/// above invites a stronger claim than the platform supports: on macOS
34	/// 26.5.1 an EMPTY dictionary and no dictionary write byte-identical PNGs
35	/// (same sha256, same 5330 bytes, same chunk list, across two processes).
36	/// So no BYTE comparison can catch `[:]` here — but the rule is not
37	/// unguarded, and saying it was would send the next reader looking for a
38	/// check that exists: `phase7_chrome.py` reads `destinationProperties != nil`
39	/// STRUCTURALLY through the probe, which is what an empty dictionary fails
40	/// and a byte comparison cannot. That is a fact about this ImageIO, not a
41	/// licence — the rule stays `nil`, because the next ImageIO owes us nothing
42	/// and the failure would then arrive as a rendering change in five scripts
43	/// at once.
44	///
45	/// **JPEG flattens onto BLACK, and it says so out loud.** JPEG is the one of
46	/// the three containers that cannot carry an alpha channel at all, and phase
47	/// 7b makes a transparent canvas reachable in this very phase — so a person
48	/// who has just set the canvas to Transparent and saves a JPEG would otherwise
49	/// get whatever ImageIO happens to do with the premultiplied pixels, silently.
50	/// Black is the choice rather than white because black is what the preview
51	/// well and the exported movie already show behind the canvas: the still then
52	/// matches the picture the person was looking at when they asked for it. The
53	/// flatten belongs to JPEG ALONE — PNG and HEIC both carry alpha, so nothing
54	/// is thrown away in those two, and adding a flatten to them would destroy
55	/// information the format was chosen for. The panel's hint carries the same
56	/// sentence, because a silent flatten is the thing being avoided. JPEG is
57	/// also the one that holds 8 bits a component whatever it is handed, which is
58	/// why `Format.carriesDepth` is false for it alone and no frame grabbed for a
59	/// JPEG is read through the reader (spec §11 PR-9).
60	///
61	/// **The quality is 0.9, not `MediaImporter.writeJPEG`'s 0.7.** Those two
62	/// numbers answer different questions: a filmstrip thumbnail is 54 px tall and
63	/// is discarded when the cache is cleared, while this is a delivery still
64	/// somebody is about to put in a document. Neither number is a compromise
65	/// between the two, which is why they are written down separately rather than
66	/// shared through a constant.
67	enum FrameWriter {
68	
69	    // MARK: - The formats
70	
71	    /// The three containers Save Frame writes, each declaring everything that
72	    /// is true of it in ONE place: its type, the extension a file of it takes,
73	    /// what a menu calls it, and whether it can hold an alpha channel.
74	    ///
75	    /// The `rawValue` is a stable identifier for the agent's vocabulary and is
76	    /// deliberately NOT the file extension — JPEG's are "jpeg" and "jpg" and
77	    /// collapsing them would make one of the two wrong. `format(for:)` reads
78	    /// both spellings back.
79	    ///
80	    /// `UTType.heic` and not `public.heif`: only the former is in
81	    /// `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()` on macOS 15, so a destination
82	    /// created for the latter is nil and the write fails at the last moment
83	    /// with nothing to say. Measured, not assumed.
84	    enum Format: String, CaseIterable {
85	        case png
86	        case jpeg
87	        case heic
88	
89	        var contentType: UTType {
90	            switch self {
91	            case .png: return .png
92	            case .jpeg: return .jpeg
93	            case .heic: return .heic
94	            }
95	        }
96	
97	        /// The extension a file of this format takes. One spelling per
98	        /// format: the panel writes it, `destinationURL` replaces with it and
99	        /// `format(for:)` reads every accepted spelling back to it.
100	        var fileExtension: String {
101	            switch self {
102	            case .png: return "png"
103	            case .jpeg: return "jpg"
104	            case .heic: return "heic"
105	            }
106	        }
107	
108	        /// Every spelling of this format's extension the app READS — one
109	        /// each, and JPEG's two, `fileExtension` first.
110	        ///
111	        /// It is the vocabulary and not just a list: `format(for:)` reads a
112	        /// name with it and the save panel's format popup decides with it
113	        /// which trailing dot-suffix is an EXTENSION it may replace and which
114	        /// is part of a name somebody typed. Those two questions have one
115	        /// answer and now have one home.
116	        var acceptedExtensions: [String] {
117	            switch self {
118	            case .png: return ["png"]
119	            case .jpeg: return ["jpg", "jpeg"]
120	            case .heic: return ["heic"]
121	            }
122	        }
123	
124	        /// What a popup row and a message call it.
125	        var displayName: String {
126	            switch self {
127	            case .png: return "PNG"
128	            case .jpeg: return "JPEG"
129	            case .heic: return "HEIC"
130	            }
131	        }
132	
133	        /// True where the container can hold an alpha channel — which is the
134	        /// whole of the flatten rule: the one format that cannot is the one
135	        /// format that gets a black backdrop.
136	        var carriesAlpha: Bool {
137	            switch self {
138	            case .png, .heic: return true
139	            case .jpeg: return false
140	            }
141	        }
142	
143	        /// The one line the save panel shows under the format popup. Every
144	        /// row gets one rather than only JPEG: a note that appears for one
145	        /// choice reads as a warning about that choice, where the fact worth
146	        /// carrying is that the three rows differ about alpha at all — which
147	        /// is what somebody who has just set the canvas to Transparent
148	        /// (phase 7b) needs to know before they pick, not after.
149	        var alphaNote: String {
150	            carriesAlpha
151	                ? "\(displayName) keeps the canvas's alpha channel."
152	                : FrameWriter.flattenNote
153	        }
154	
155	        /// The properties dictionary handed to `CGImageDestinationAddImage`,
156	        /// and `nil` for PNG on purpose (see the type's doc): PNG is lossless,
157	        /// there is nothing to ask it for, and the byte-identity every earlier
158	        /// phase's proof depends on is identity with a nil dictionary.
159	        var destinationProperties: CFDictionary? {
160	            switch self {
161	            case .png:
162	                return nil
163	            case .jpeg, .heic:
164	                return [kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality: quality] as CFDictionary
165	            }
166	        }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// The lossy quality both lossy rows are written at. A delivery still, not
170	    /// a thumbnail — see the type's doc for why this is 0.9 and
171	    /// `MediaImporter.writeJPEG`'s is 0.7.
172	    static let quality = 0.9
173	
174	    /// The one sentence the panel and any message about JPEG says, kept here
175	    /// beside the behaviour it describes so the two cannot drift.
176	    static let flattenNote =
177	        "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
178	
179	    // MARK: - Failures
180	
181	    /// Failures name the PATH, never a bare `false`. A frame grab that
182	    /// answered only "no" would leave a person guessing between a folder they
183	    /// cannot write, a format this Mac's ImageIO does not know and an encoder
184	    /// that gave up — three different things to do about it.
185	    ///
186	    /// **So the first two are two CASES and not one sentence**, and the
187	    /// review is what settled it: `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answers
188	    /// nil for both, and a single message asserting the format was the wrong
189	    /// one of the three for the case a caller actually hits. Measured here
190	    /// (macOS 26.5.1): it answers nil for `/card.png`, for
191	    /// `/private/var/db/x.png`, for `/System/nowhere/card.png` and for a
192	    /// path that is an existing directory — every one of them a PNG this Mac
193	    /// writes perfectly, and the agent reaches all four, because
194	    /// `render_frame` takes a caller's path and a launched `.app`'s working
195	    /// directory is `/`. Telling somebody to go looking for a missing
196	    /// encoder when the answer is a folder they cannot write is worse than
197	    /// saying nothing.
198	    enum WriteError: LocalizedError {
199	        /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answered nil for a type this
200	        /// machine's ImageIO does not WRITE. Decided by asking
201	        /// `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()`, which is a question
202	        /// about the machine and carries no URL in it.
203	        case unsupported(Format, URL)
204	        /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answered nil for a type this
205	        /// machine DOES write, so what it could not do is create the file:
206	        /// a folder that is not there, one this app may not write into, a
207	        /// read-only or absent volume, or a path that is itself a directory.
208	        /// ImageIO tells those apart nowhere, so the message names the CLASS
209	        /// and asks the two questions a person can answer, rather than
210	        /// inventing a cause. The agent is the caller that reaches it — an
211	        /// `NSSavePanel` choice confers access to the URL it returns even for
212	        /// an unsandboxed app, so Save Frame reaches it only where the volume
213	        /// or the folder went away between the panel and the write.
214	        case unwritable(Format, URL)
215	        /// The opaque bitmap the JPEG flatten draws into could not be made.
216	        case flattenFailed(URL)
217	        /// `CGImageDestinationFinalize` answered false.
218	        case encodingFailed(Format, URL)
219	        /// A JPEG asked of an HLG project's frame (spec §11 HD-13 (i)): eight
220	        /// bits labelled BT.709 cannot carry it until H-3's SDR version.
221	        case hlgJPEG
222	
223	        var errorDescription: String? {
224	            switch self {
225	            case .unsupported(let format, let url):
226	                return "Could not write \(format.displayName) to \(url.path). "
227	                    + "This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format."
228	            case .unwritable(let format, let url):
229	                return "Could not write \(format.displayName) to \(url.path). "
230	                    + "The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists "
231	                    + "and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it."
232	            case .flattenFailed(let url):
233	                return "Could not flatten the frame onto black for \(url.path)."
234	            case .encodingFailed(let format, let url):
235	                return "\(format.displayName) encoding failed for \(url.path)."
236	            case .hlgJPEG:
237	                return "JPEG cannot carry an HLG project's picture; save the frame as PNG or HEIC"
238	            }
239	        }
240	    }
241	
242	    /// Which of the two nil-destination failures happened, asked the only way
243	    /// ImageIO answers it: `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()` is the
244	    /// list of types this machine WRITES, so a format on that list did not
245	    /// fail for being unknown and the URL is what is left.
246	    ///
247	    /// It runs only on the failure path, so the ordinary write pays nothing
248	    /// for it; and it probes no file — `isWritableFile(atPath:)` answers a
249	    /// permission bit, which is not the question when the refusal is TCC's or
250	    /// the parent is missing, and a probe write would be a second way to
251	    /// create the very file being reported.
252	    private static func destinationFailure(_ format: Format, _ url: URL) -> WriteError {
253	        let writable = (CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers() as NSArray as? [String]) ?? []
254	        return writable.contains(format.contentType.identifier)
255	            ? .unwritable(format, url)
256	            : .unsupported(format, url)
257	    }
258	
259	    // MARK: - Reading a format off a name
260	
261	    /// The format `url` names, or `requested` when a caller has said. Both
262	    /// spellings of JPEG read back to one case; anything unrecognised is PNG,
263	    /// which is the row that loses nothing.
264	    ///
265	    /// It is `CaptionExporter.format(for:requested:)` verbatim in shape, and
266	    /// for that function's reason: the panel and the agent both end here, so
267	    /// "what did this path ask for" is answered once.
268	    ///
269	    /// The spellings read here are exactly the ones in
270	    /// `AgentServer.replaceableExtensions`, and they have to be: a name this
271	    /// app never writes is part of the NAME rather than an extension (that
272	    /// set's own rule), so recognising a spelling here that the set does not
273	    /// replace would turn `shot.heif` into `shot.heif.heic` — the doubled name
274	    /// the whole mechanism exists to prevent. `heif` is the one that tempts,
275	    /// and it is left out on both sides together.
276	    static func format(for url: URL, requested: Format? = nil) -> Format {
277	        if let requested = requested { return requested }
278	        let suffix = url.pathExtension.lowercased()
279	        return Format.allCases.first { $0.acceptedExtensions.contains(suffix) } ?? .png
280	    }
281	
282	    /// Every extension this app writes a still under, lower-cased — the union
283	    /// of the three formats' `acceptedExtensions`. `renamed` is the caller and
284	    /// carries the argument for having a set at all.
285	    static let knownExtensions = Set(Format.allCases.flatMap { $0.acceptedExtensions })
286	
287	    /// A save panel's name field rewritten for a newly chosen format: the
288	    /// stem it already holds, then that format's extension. `fallback` is
289	    /// what an empty field falls back to.
290	    ///
291	    /// **Only a suffix this app WRITES is an extension**, and the rest of the
292	    /// name is the person's. `deletingPathExtension` takes whatever follows
293	    /// the last dot whatever it is, so the format popup used to turn
294	    /// `Board v1.2` into `Board v1.jpg` — eating a character somebody typed
295	    /// on purpose while doing exactly what it was told. That is the same
296	    /// hazard `AgentServer.destinationURL` avoids for that same name — it
297	    /// strips only a member of `replaceableExtensions` and APPENDS otherwise,
298	    /// so `Board v1.2` over MCP is written as `Board v1.2.png` and always
299	    /// was; `knownExtensions` is this side's half of the one rule.
300	    /// Measured: `("Board v1.2" as NSString).deletingPathExtension` is
301	    /// "Board v1", and `("shot.final" as NSString)`'s is "shot".
302	    ///
303	    /// It is a function of a string and lives HERE rather than in the panel
304	    /// for the reason `write` does: an accessory view's private method is
305	    /// reachable by no proof this project can write, because a save panel
306	    /// cannot be driven over MCP or offscreen — so a rule kept there is a
307	    /// rule nothing can check. As a pure function a probe compiled from
308	    /// `app/Sources` calls it with a table of names (`AudioNormalize.swift`'s
309	    /// argument, and `CaptionCues`') — `tools/proof/remaining_probe.py`,
310	    /// section 1, the first instrument to have actually done so.
311	    static func renamed(_ name: String, as format: Format, fallback: String) -> String {
312	        let suffix = (name as NSString).pathExtension.lowercased()
313	        let stem =
314	            knownExtensions.contains(suffix)
315	            ? (name as NSString).deletingPathExtension : name
316	        return "\(stem.isEmpty ? fallback : stem).\(format.fileExtension)"
317	    }
318	
319	    // MARK: - Writing
320	
321	    /// Writes `image` to `url` and answers the URL it wrote. The caller owns
322	    /// the path — this creates no folders and replaces no extension, because
323	    /// the two callers disagree about both (the panel has already asked a
324	    /// person, and the agent runs its path through
325	    /// `AgentServer.destinationURL`).
326	    @discardableResult
327	    static func write(_ image: CGImage, as format: Format, to url: URL) throws -> URL {
328	        let subject = format.carriesAlpha ? image : try flattenedOntoBlack(image, for: url)
329	        guard let destination = CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL(
330	            url as CFURL, format.contentType.identifier as CFString, 1, nil)
331	        else {
332	            throw destinationFailure(format, url)
333	        }
334	        CGImageDestinationAddImage(destination, subject, format.destinationProperties)
335	        guard CGImageDestinationFinalize(destination) else {
336	            throw WriteError.encodingFailed(format, url)
337	        }
338	        return url
339	    }
340	
341	    /// `image` composited over black in an OPAQUE bitmap — the JPEG flatten.
342	    ///
343	    /// It is a real draw rather than a hint to the encoder because there is no
344	    /// such hint: handed premultiplied pixels with alpha, a JPEG destination
345	    /// simply drops the alpha channel, which leaves a half-transparent white
346	    /// title composited as mid-grey and a fully transparent canvas as black
347	    /// anyway — the right answer in one case and a wrong one in the other, with
348	    /// no way to tell them apart afterwards. Compositing first makes every
349	    /// pixel the same arithmetic the compositor and the exported movie already
350	    /// do against their black ground.
351	    ///
352	    /// It runs for EVERY JPEG, including a frame that carries no alpha at all.
353	    /// Short-circuiting an opaque source would be one branch and one saved
354	    /// copy, and it would buy a second way for a JPEG to be produced — a
355	    /// direct encode whose colour handling need not match the drawn one's, on
356	    /// a path nothing measures. One path per format is worth a full-frame
357	    /// draw at the speed a person presses a menu item.
358	    ///
359	    /// Eight bits a component, deliberately: JPEG has no more, so a frame from
360	    /// a 10-bit source (which `render_frame` writes as 16-bit float from a
361	    /// ProRes or HEVC Main 10 clip) is truncated here rather than at some
362	    /// later point where it would look like a rendering difference. The colour space is the image's own where it is
363	    /// an RGB one, so the flatten changes coverage and nothing else; a source
364	    /// in any other model falls back to device RGB, which is the only thing
365	    /// `noneSkipLast` can be built over.
366	    private static func flattenedOntoBlack(_ image: CGImage, for url: URL) throws -> CGImage {
367	        let space: CGColorSpace = {
368	            if let own = image.colorSpace, own.model == .rgb { return own }
369	            return CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB()
370	        }()
371	        guard image.width > 0, image.height > 0,
372	            let context = CGContext(
373	                data: nil, width: image.width, height: image.height, bitsPerComponent: 8,
374	                bytesPerRow: 0, space: space,
375	                bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.noneSkipLast.rawValue)
376	        else {
377	            throw WriteError.flattenFailed(url)
378	        }
379	        let rect = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: image.width, height: image.height)
380	        context.setFillColor(red: 0, green: 0, blue: 0, alpha: 1)
381	        context.fill(rect)
382	        context.draw(image, in: rect)
383	        guard let flattened = context.makeImage() else {
384	            throw WriteError.flattenFailed(url)
385	        }
386	        return flattened
387	    }
388	}

391	    /// The BT.709 label every rendered frame's file carries (spec §11 PR-11):
392	    /// the space `CVImageBufferCreateColorSpaceFromAttachments` makes of the
393	    /// BT.709 primaries, transfer function and matrix — the space the
394	    /// generator already gives a frame of a BT.709-tagged source,
395	    /// `kCGColorSpaceCoreMedia709` — else `CGColorSpace.itur_709`.
396	    static let frameSpace: CGColorSpace = {
397	        let attachments =

400	                kCVImageBufferTransferFunctionKey: REDACTED,
401	                kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrixKey: REDACTED,
402	            ] as CFDictionary

435	    /// unlabelled for `snapshot_ui`, `render_graphic`'s sheets and the look
436	    /// gallery's tiles. An HLG project's frame as JPEG is refused (spec §11
437	    /// HD-13 (i)).
438	    @discardableResult
439	    static func writeFrame(_ image: CGImage, as format: Format, to url: URL) throws -> URL {
440	        if format == .jpeg, isHLG(image) { throw WriteError.hlgJPEG }
441	        return try write(labelled(image), as: format, to: url)
442	    }
443	}

3	// `ExportWriter`'s chapter half: the chapter list an export writes, the text track that
4	// carries it, its pump, and the text samples themselves. A pure move out of
5	// `ExporterWriter.swift` at its size cap (issue batch B92); the members each file calls in
6	// the other lost `private`, and nothing else changed.
7	
8	// MARK: - Chapters
9	
10	/// One entry of the chapter list an export writes (spec §7.8).
11	///
12	/// Chapters come from the PROJECT, never from the composition plan: the plan
13	/// says what to decode and where to put it, and markers decode nothing, so
14	/// `plan.rs` emits no marker key at all. `Exporter` reads them off the
15	/// snapshot of the handle it was given and hands them over here, which is
16	/// also why an export shows the chapters the timeline had when the sheet was
17	/// confirmed rather than the ones it has when the write ends.
18	struct ExportChapter: Equatable {
19	    /// Timeline ticks, in the project's own time. Clamping into the exported
20	    /// range and rebasing to a zero-based file both happen when the samples
21	    /// are built, because only then is the range known.
22	    let start: Ticks
23	    /// What the chapter is called. Never empty — an unnamed marker becomes
24	    /// "Chapter <n>", because a chapter list of blank rows is worse in every
25	    /// player than no chapter list at all.
26	    let name: String
27	
28	    /// The project's `chapter` markers, in time order and named.
29	    ///
30	    /// Numbering is over the CHAPTER markers only, so deleting a plain marker
31	    /// cannot renumber the chapters around it.
32	    static func list(from markers: [MarkerSnapshot]) -> [ExportChapter] {
33	        markers
34	            .filter(\.chapter)
35	            .sorted { $0.time < $1.time }
36	            .enumerated()
37	            .map { index, marker in
38	                let name = marker.name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
39	                return ExportChapter(
40	                    start: marker.time, name: name.isEmpty ? "Chapter \(index + 1)" : name)
41	            }
42	    }
43	}

45	extension ExportChapter {
46	    /// The chapters clamped into `range` and rebased to zero, each with its span in the file:
47	    /// the one rule both writers write chapters by (`ExportWriter`'s text track,
48	    /// `ExportWebMWriter`'s Chapters element, spec §11 CX-15 (2)).
49	    ///
50	    /// Each chapter runs until the next one, and the last until the end of
51	    /// the range — a chapter list is a partition of the movie, not a set of
52	    /// points. A chapter that began BEFORE an in/out range is not dropped:
53	    /// the last of them is pinned to the start of the range, because the
54	    /// exported piece really is inside that chapter and a file whose first
55	    /// minutes belong to no chapter reads as a bug.
56	    static func partition(
57	        _ chapters: [ExportChapter], in range: CMTimeRange
58	    ) -> [(name: String, range: CMTimeRange)] {
59	        let start = CompositionBuilder.ticks(range.start)
60	        let end = start + CompositionBuilder.ticks(range.duration)
61	        guard end > start else { return [] }
62	
63	        var inside: [ExportChapter] = []
64	        for chapter in chapters where chapter.start < end {
65	            if chapter.start <= start {
66	                inside = [ExportChapter(start: start, name: chapter.name)]
67	            } else {
68	                inside.append(chapter)
69	            }
70	        }
71	        var parts: [(name: String, range: CMTimeRange)] = []
72	        for (index, chapter) in inside.enumerated() {
73	            let next = index + 1 < inside.count ? inside[index + 1].start : end
74	            guard next > chapter.start else { continue }
75	            parts.append((chapter.name, CMTimeRange(
76	                start: CompositionBuilder.time(chapter.start - start),
77	                duration: CompositionBuilder.time(next - chapter.start))))
78	        }
79	        return parts
80	    }
81	}

85	    /// The chapter track: a text track carrying one sample per chapter,
86	    /// associated with the movie's own track through
87	    /// `AVTrackAssociationTypeChapterList`, which is what writes the `chap`
88	    /// track reference every reader (QuickTime, `ffprobe -show_chapters`)
89	    /// looks for.
90	    ///
91	    /// Additive, never fatal: a build of macOS that will not take the text
92	    /// track loses the chapters, not the movie. The track is marked disabled
93	    /// so no player tries to draw the names over the picture.
94	    ///
95	    /// **A container that cannot hold a chapter track is refused HERE, not
96	    /// left to `canAdd`.** A chapter list is a second track associated with
97	    /// the first, which is a QuickTime-family idea; a RIFF or an IFF file is
98	    /// a header followed by samples with nowhere to put one. `canAdd` is the
99	    /// wrong guard for that because the failure it would let through is the
100	    /// expensive one: a `true` followed by a refusal at `finishWriting`
101	    /// loses the whole file, which is exactly what a malformed text format
102	    /// description already cost once (see `textFormat`).
103	    func addChapters(_ chapters: [ExportChapter], settings: ExportSettings) {
104	        guard Self.carriesChapters(settings), !chapters.isEmpty,
105	            let host = videoInput ?? audioInput, let format = Self.textFormat()
106	        else { return }
107	        let samples = Self.chapterSamples(chapters, in: range, format: format)
108	        guard !samples.isEmpty else { return }
109	
110	        let input = AVAssetWriterInput(
111	            mediaType: .text, outputSettings: nil, sourceFormatHint: format)
112	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
113	        input.marksOutputTrackAsEnabled = false
114	        guard writer.canAdd(input) else { return }
115	        writer.add(input)
116	        host.addTrackAssociation(
117	            withTrackOf: input, type: AVAssetTrack.AssociationType.chapterList.rawValue)
118	        chapterInput = input
119	        chapterSamples = samples
120	    }

122	    /// The chapter samples are a handful of tiny text buffers, all known
123	    /// before the write starts, so this pump has nothing to read — it drains
124	    /// its own array.
125	    func pumpChapters(
126	        _ input: AVAssetWriterInput, on queue: DispatchQueue, group: DispatchGroup
127	    ) {
128	        group.enter()
129	        var pending = chapterSamples
130	        var finished = false
131	        let stop: () -> Void = {
132	            guard !finished else { return }
133	            finished = true
134	            input.markAsFinished()
135	            group.leave()
136	        }
137	        input.requestMediaDataWhenReady(on: queue) { [weak self] in
138	            guard let self = self else { return }
139	            while input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
140	                guard !finished else { return }
141	                guard !self.isStopping, !pending.isEmpty else {
142	                    stop()
143	                    return
144	                }
145	                let sample = pending.removeFirst()
146	                guard input.append(sample) else {
147	                    // A chapter that will not write is not worth losing the
148	                    // movie over: the text track simply ends here.
149	                    stop()
150	                    return
151	                }
152	            }
153	        }
154	    }
155	
156	    // MARK: - Chapter samples
157	
158	    /// The format one chapter sample is written in: a QuickTime text
159	    /// (`'text'`) description, in every container this build writes.
160	    ///
161	    /// **Why the byte structure and not `CMFormatDescriptionCreate`.** A
162	    /// description created from a media type and a subtype alone carries no
163	    /// extensions, and `AVAssetWriter` cannot serialise that into a sample
164	    /// description — it fails the whole write at `finishWriting` with
165	    /// `kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter` (-12712), losing
166	    /// the movie, not just the chapters (measured). Handing the bridge the
167	    /// big-endian `TextDescription` the QuickTime file format specifies is
168	    /// exactly the shape it will write back out, so there is nothing left to
169	    /// guess at.
170	    ///
171	    /// **Why QuickTime text rather than 3GPP `tx3g` in the MPEG-4 family.**
172	    /// A `'text'` sample entry is what Apple's own chapter tracks use inside
173	    /// `.m4a`/`.m4v`/`.mp4`, and both QuickTime and `ffprobe`'s MOV demuxer
174	    /// read chapters from it; `tx3g` would mean a second byte layout and a
175	    /// font table for no gain.
176	    private static func textFormat() -> CMFormatDescription? {
177	        var description = Data()
178	        func be16(_ value: UInt16) { description.append(contentsOf: [
179	            UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: value >> 8), UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: value)]) }
180	        func be32(_ value: UInt32) { be16(UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: value >> 16))
181	            be16(UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: value)) }
182	
183	        be32(60)                                   // descSize, this whole record
184	        be32(0x7465_7874)                          // 'text'
185	        be32(0)                                    // reserved
186	        be16(0)                                    // reserved
187	        be16(1)                                    // data reference index
188	        be32(0)                                    // display flags: none
189	        be32(0)                                    // text justification: left
190	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(0)                  // background colour: black
191	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(0); be16(0)         // default text box: empty
192	        be32(0)                                    // default style: start char
193	        be16(0); be16(0)                           // height, ascent
194	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(12)                 // font, face, size
195	        be16(0xFFFF); be16(0xFFFF); be16(0xFFFF)   // foreground colour: white
196	        description.append(0)                      // font name, an empty
197	        description.append(0)                      //   Pascal string, padded
198	
199	        var format: CMFormatDescription?
200	        let status = description.withUnsafeBytes { bytes -> OSStatus in
201	            guard let base = bytes.bindMemory(to: UInt8.self).baseAddress else { return -1 }
202	            // A nil flavor is the QuickTime Movie one.
203	            return CMTextFormatDescriptionCreateFromBigEndianTextDescriptionData(
204	                allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, bigEndianTextDescriptionData: base,
205	                size: description.count, flavor: nil, mediaType: kCMMediaType_Text,
206	                formatDescriptionOut: &format)
207	        }
208	        return status == noErr ? format : nil
209	    }
210	
211	    /// The chapters as samples, clamped into `range` and rebased to zero
212	    /// (`ExportChapter.partition`).
213	    private static func chapterSamples(
214	        _ chapters: [ExportChapter], in range: CMTimeRange, format: CMFormatDescription
215	    ) -> [CMSampleBuffer] {
216	        ExportChapter.partition(chapters, in: range).compactMap {
217	            chapterSample($0.name, timeRange: $0.range, format: format)
218	        }
219	    }
220	
221	    /// One text sample: a 16-bit big-endian byte count followed by the UTF-8
222	    /// name, which is the payload both QuickTime text and 3GPP timed text
223	    /// carry. Names are truncated at the length that count can express —
224	    /// 64 KB of chapter title is not a case worth failing an export over.
225	    private static func chapterSample(
226	        _ name: String, timeRange: CMTimeRange, format: CMFormatDescription
227	    ) -> CMSampleBuffer? {
228	        var text = Array(name.utf8)
229	        if text.count > 0xFFFF { text = Array(text.prefix(0xFFFF)) }
230	        var payload: [UInt8] = [UInt8(text.count >> 8), UInt8(text.count & 0xFF)]
231	        payload.append(contentsOf: text)
232	
233	        var block: CMBlockBuffer?
234	        guard CMBlockBufferCreateWithMemoryBlock(
235	            allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, memoryBlock: nil, blockLength: payload.count,
236	            blockAllocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, customBlockSource: nil, offsetToData: 0,
237	            dataLength: payload.count, flags: 0, blockBufferOut: &block) == kCMBlockBufferNoErr,
238	            let buffer = block,
239	            CMBlockBufferReplaceDataBytes(
240	                with: payload, blockBuffer: buffer, offsetIntoDestination: 0,
241	                dataLength: payload.count) == kCMBlockBufferNoErr
242	        else { return nil }
243	
244	        var timing = CMSampleTimingInfo(
245	            duration: timeRange.duration, presentationTimeStamp: timeRange.start,
246	            decodeTimeStamp: .invalid)
247	        var size = payload.count
248	        var sample: CMSampleBuffer?
249	        guard CMSampleBufferCreate(
250	            allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, dataBuffer: buffer, dataReady: true,
251	            makeDataReadyCallback: nil, refcon: nil, formatDescription: format, sampleCount: 1,
252	            sampleTimingEntryCount: 1, sampleTimingArray: &timing, sampleSizeEntryCount: 1,
253	            sampleSizeArray: &size, sampleBufferOut: &sample) == noErr
254	        else { return nil }
255	        return sample
256	    }
257	}
