3	extension Exporter {
4	
5	    /// Why an export stopped. Every case is reported through `completion` —
6	    /// nothing here throws at the caller and nothing crashes.
7	    enum ExportError: LocalizedError {
8	        /// The core could not produce a composition plan for this project.
9	        case noPlan
10	        /// Nothing to write: no video and no audio track in the plan. Reached
11	        /// by an empty timeline AND by one holding only text, shapes and
12	        /// images, which need no composition track (spec §7.2) — so the
13	        /// message has to name the second case, which is the surprising one.
14	        case emptyTimeline
15	        /// This Mac will not encode what the core's preset resolved to — an
16	        /// unknown codec name, one `AVAssetWriter` refuses an input for, or
17	        /// one whose encoder is not found when the write starts
18	        /// (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`). Carries the preset id when the core
19	        /// gave one, else the codec.
20	        case presetUnavailable(String)
21	        /// The settings named a container this build cannot map to a file
22	        /// type.
23	        case fileTypeUnsupported(String)
24	        /// An alpha-carrying row was asked for a size of a different SHAPE
25	        /// from the canvas, which cannot be written correctly and so is not
26	        /// written at all (road map 2, phase 7b). Carries the canvas and the
27	        /// size the core resolved, in that order.
28	        ///
29	        /// **Which sizes reach it** (spec §11 G-33 (c)): on `prores_4444` and
30	        /// `hevc_alpha`, a frame more than a pixel off the canvas's shape
31	        /// (`ExportWriter.shapeGap`: `gap > limit`). A frame within a pixel is
32	        /// filled instead of padded and is written — the evened Document row
33	        /// on a canvas with an odd edge, a standard row whose long edge
34	        /// rounded, a size typed in the canvas's own proportions (evened
35	        /// first on `hevc_alpha`, so an odd one is written a pixel smaller),
36	        /// and on `prores_4444` a typed frame one pixel short. So no size of
37	        /// the canvas's shape is refused for being odd; a typed size of any
38	        /// other shape is judged as the even frame it becomes
39	        /// (1279 × 720 on 1920 × 1080 is 1278 × 720 on `hevc_alpha`, and
40	        /// refused).
41	        ///
42	        /// **Measured, not feared.** `AVVideoScalingModeResizeAspect` pads
43	        /// the frame to the asked-for shape, and the padding path destroys
44	        /// the alpha channel: a 320 × 180 transparent canvas written
45	        /// `prores_4444` at 240 × 240 comes back with the PICTURE at alpha 0
46	        /// and the letterbox BARS at alpha 255 — the answer inverted, not
47	        /// merely lost. The same canvas at 160 × 90 or 640 × 360 is correct
48	        /// at every pixel, so the fault is the padding and nothing else.
49	        ///
50	        /// It is refused rather than documented because the file would be
51	        /// silently wrong in the one respect the row exists for, and this
52	        /// codebase's rule for exactly that shape is `codecType(for:)`'s:
53	        /// a refusal, never a fallback that puts a file on disk which is not
54	        /// the one asked for. Nothing legitimate is blocked by accident —
55	        /// every row of the Size popup is fitted to the document's own
56	        /// aspect (`export_size.rs`), so only a hand-typed Custom size of
57	        /// another shape can reach this (or a canvas, or a typed size, with
58	        /// an edge of exactly 1 px, raised to 2 on `hevc_alpha`), and the
59	        /// message says what to type instead: every size with the canvas's
60	        /// proportions is written, odd or even, smaller or larger.
61	        case alphaAspectMismatch(width: Int, height: Int, wantWidth: Int, wantHeight: Int)
62	        /// The user pressed Cancel. The sheet dismisses without an alert.
63	        case cancelled
64	        /// The write ended in a state that is neither completed nor
65	        /// cancelled and had no error of its own — or one of the reader's or
66	        /// writer's own steps refused with a message worth showing.
67	        case failed(String)
68	        /// Graphic clips in the range whose module does not compile, or is
69	        /// not in `graphics/`, each with what is wrong: the export was refused
70	        /// before it started (G-8). Sorted by name.
71	        case graphicsNotCompiled([(name: String, message: String)])
72	        /// A graphic failed while the export drew it, at its own frame — nil
73	        /// when it did not compile. The export stopped and its file is gone.
74	        case graphicFailed(name: String, frame: Int?, message: String)
75	        /// A ramped clip's audio render failed (spec §11 SR-12 (g), (h)): the
76	        /// export waits for every ramp segment it plays and never writes one
77	        /// silent, so it stops, naming the clip and the renderer's reason.
78	        case rampAudioFailed(clip: UInt32, message: String)
79	        /// A clip's isolated voice (spec §11 AU-57) could not be rendered: the
80	        /// export waits for it as for a ramp, and stops naming the clip.
81	        case isolationFailed(clip: UInt32, message: String)
82	        /// A gated or de-essed clip's loudness was still not measured when the
83	        /// export's wait ran out (spec §11 AU-42): its thresholds are relative
84	        /// to it, so the export stops naming the clip rather than writing it
85	        /// ungated.
86	        case loudnessUnmeasured(clip: UInt32)
87	        /// A clip's voice effect (spec §11 AU-147) could not be rendered: the
88	        /// export waits for it as for its isolation, and stops naming the clip.
89	        case voiceFailed(clip: UInt32, message: String)
90	        /// A cut-out clip's person masks (spec §11 CO-6, CO-22 (e)), or a
91	        /// picture's foreground masks (`foreground`, CO-106), could not be made:
92	        /// the export waits for every mask it draws, a picture's too, and stops
93	        /// naming the clip rather than writing it uncut.
94	        case cutoutFailed(clip: UInt32, message: String, foreground: Bool = false)
95	
96	        var errorDescription: String? {
97	            switch self {
98	            case .noPlan:
99	                return "The project could not be prepared for export."
100	            case .emptyTimeline:
101	                return "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."
102	            case .presetUnavailable(let name):
103	                return "This Mac cannot export with the “\(name)” preset."
104	            case .fileTypeUnsupported(let container):
105	                return "“\(container)” is not a container this build can write."
106	            case .alphaAspectMismatch(let width, let height, let wantWidth, let wantHeight):
107	                return "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape. "
108	                    + "This canvas is \(width) × \(height) and \(wantWidth) × \(wantHeight) is a "
109	                    + "different shape, so the picture would be padded and the padding loses the "
110	                    + "alpha channel. Export at \(width) × \(height), at one of the sizes in the "
111	                    + "popup, or at any size with the same proportions."
112	            case .cancelled:
113	                return "The export was cancelled."
114	            case .failed(let message):
115	                return message
116	            case .graphicsNotCompiled(let refused):
117	                let clauses = refused.map { "the graphic \"\($0.name)\" \($0.message)" }
118	                return "The export was not started: " + clauses.joined(separator: "; ")
119	                    + ". Fix the module and export again."
120	            case .graphicFailed(let name, let frame?, let message):
121	                return "The export was stopped at frame \(frame) of the graphic \"\(name)\": "
122	                    + "\(message). No file was written."
123	            case .graphicFailed(let name, nil, let message):
124	                return "The export was stopped: the graphic \"\(name)\" does not compile — "
125	                    + "\(message). No file was written."
126	            case .rampAudioFailed(let clip, let message):
127	                return "Clip \(clip)'s retimed audio could not be rendered: \(message)."
128	            case .isolationFailed(let clip, let message):
129	                return "Clip \(clip)'s isolated voice could not be rendered: \(message)."
130	            case .loudnessUnmeasured(let clip):
131	                return "Clip \(clip)'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its "
132	                    + "gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to "
133	                    + "show the clip's loudness, then export again."
134	            case .voiceFailed(let clip, let message):
135	                return "Clip \(clip)'s voice effect could not be rendered: \(message)."
136	            case .cutoutFailed(let clip, let message, let foreground):
137	                return "Clip \(clip)'s \(foreground ? "foreground" : "person") masks could not be "
138	                    + "made: \(message)."
139	            }
140	        }
141	    }
142	
143	    /// What a finished write becomes when the reason it failed is that this
144	    /// Mac has no encoder for the row (spec §11 G-33 (e)): the preset's own
145	    /// sentence, and no file.
146	    ///
147	    /// `ExportWriter.addVideo` cannot see it. Measured with an encoder
148	    /// specification nothing satisfies, on `.hevcWithAlpha` and `.hevc`
149	    /// alike: `canApply` is true, the input constructs, `canAdd` is true, and
150	    /// `startWriting()` then fails with `AVFoundationErrorDomain` −11834
151	    /// ("Cannot Encode"), leaving a 0-byte file at the destination. So it is
152	    /// mapped here, where `startWriting` hears the pipeline: exactly that
153	    /// domain and code become `.presetUnavailable` with the preset's name and
154	    /// the file is removed, and every other result is returned as it came.
155	    static func encoderOutcome(
156	        _ result: Result<URL, any Error>, settings: ExportSettings, destination: URL
157	    ) -> Result<URL, any Error> {
158	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else { return result }
159	        let reason = error as NSError
160	        guard reason.domain == AVFoundationErrorDomain,
161	            reason.code == AVError.Code.encoderNotFound.rawValue
162	        else { return result }
163	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
164	        return .failure(ExportError.presetUnavailable(ExportWriter.presetName(settings)))
165	    }
166	}

4	/// An export's graphics (road map 10 §5f, G-8 and G-13, G3c): the gate that
5	/// refuses a module that does not compile before anything is built, and the
6	/// mapping from a graphic that failed mid-export to the error the caller
7	/// reads.
8	///
9	/// **The set is PINNED, not looked up.** `Exporter.export` and
10	/// `renderFrameReported` pin the `GraphicSet` their caller captured on their
11	/// own `RecipeSource` key (`GraphicRegistry.pin`), so an export draws the
12	/// modules as they compiled when it was asked for, whatever the document's
13	/// store does next, and a queued job draws the set it was ENQUEUED with.
14	/// Every pin has its `unpin` on each exit: `finish`, `deinit`, and
15	/// `renderFrameReported`'s `defer`.
16	///
17	/// **The gate is compile-only** (G-8 asks for no dry run): a module that
18	/// throws at frame 900 is found at frame 900. The render thread records the
19	/// failure on the export's key; the progress timer reads it on main and
20	/// cancels, and `finish` replaces whatever the pipeline answered with
21	/// `.graphicFailed` and removes the file.
22	extension Exporter {
23	
24	    /// One offline frame and what its graphics reported while it was drawn:
25	    /// the failure first, then the warnings (`GraphicRegistry.reports`); and
26	    /// each cursor file the frame could not draw (spec §11 CU-37 (c)); and
27	    /// each cut-out clip drawn uncut because its masks were not ready within
28	    /// the frame's wait, ascending (spec §11 CO-22 (f)).
29	    struct RenderedFrame {
30	        let image: CGImage?
31	        let graphics: [GraphicReport]
32	        let cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
33	        let uncut: [UInt32]
34	    }
35	
36	    /// `.graphicsNotCompiled` when a graphic clip the export will draw has a
37	    /// module that failed to compile or has none, else nil. Nothing to gate
38	    /// with no set or an audio-only export. The clips are the top level's in
39	    /// `settings`' range, plus every graphic clip of each nest reached from a
40	    /// clip in the range, however deep — the whole nest, not its window,
41	    /// which over-includes by decision.
42	    static func graphicsRefusal(
43	        project: ReelProject, settings: ExportSettings, graphics: GraphicSet?
44	    ) -> ExportError? {
45	        guard let graphics = graphics, !settings.isAudioOnly else { return nil }
46	        let names = graphicNames(project: project, settings: settings)
47	        let refused = names.sorted().compactMap { name -> (name: String, message: String)? in
48	            switch graphics.modules[name] {
49	            case nil:
50	                return (name, "has no module in graphics/")
51	            case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
52	                let reason = diagnostics.first?.located ?? "the engine gave no reason"
53	                return (name, "does not compile — " + reason)
54	            case .compiled?:
55	                return nil
56	            }
57	        }
58	        return refused.isEmpty ? nil : .graphicsNotCompiled(refused)
59	    }
60	
61	    /// The module names of every graphic clip the export draws: the top
62	    /// level's in `settings`' range, plus every graphic clip of each nest
63	    /// reached from a clip in the range, however deep.
64	    static func graphicNames(project: ReelProject, settings: ExportSettings) -> Set<String> {
65	        let range = settings.start..<(settings.start + settings.duration)
66	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
67	        var names = Set<String>()
68	        var visited = Set<UInt32>()
69	        for clip in snapshot.clips where clip.start < range.upperBound && clip.end > range.lowerBound {
70	            if let graphic = clip.graphic { names.insert(graphic.name) }
71	            guard let id = clip.source.nestID else { continue }
72	            collectGraphicNames(inNest: id, of: snapshot, into: &names, visited: &visited)
73	        }
74	        return names
75	    }
76	
77	    /// Starts the export's graphic prefetch (spec §11 G-26) — only for the
78	    /// `ExportWriter` and `ExportWebMWriter` paths, with a pinned set and a
79	    /// graphic in range — over the range the writer reads at the frame
80	    /// duration it reads at.
81	    /// `finish` and `deinit` stop it beside the unpin. Main thread.
82	    static func startGraphicPrefetch(
83	        key: Int?, project: ReelProject, graphics: GraphicSet?, built: BuiltComposition,
84	        settings: ExportSettings, pipeline: any ExportPipeline
85	    ) {
86	        guard let key = key, graphics != nil,
87	            pipeline is ExportWriter || pipeline is ExportWebMWriter, !settings.isAudioOnly,
88	            !graphicNames(project: project, settings: settings).isEmpty
89	        else { return }
90	        GraphicPrefetch.shared.start(
91	            key: key, range: Exporter.timeRange(settings, composition: built.composition),
92	            frameDuration: ExportWriter.videoComposition(built, settings: settings).frameDuration)
93	    }
94	
95	    /// Every graphic clip's module name in nest `id` and in each nest reached
96	    /// from it. `visited` is belt and braces: `check_nesting` refuses a
97	    /// cycle, but a hand-written file is not held to it (`pathToClip`'s rule).
98	    private static func collectGraphicNames(
99	        inNest id: UInt32, of snapshot: ProjectSnapshot,
100	        into names: inout Set<String>, visited: inout Set<UInt32>
101	    ) {
102	        guard visited.insert(id).inserted, let nest = snapshot.nest(id) else { return }
103	        for inner in nest.clips {
104	            if let graphic = inner.graphic { names.insert(graphic.name) }
105	            if let child = inner.source.nestID {
106	                collectGraphicNames(inNest: child, of: snapshot, into: &names, visited: &visited)
107	            }
108	        }
109	    }
110	
111	    /// `.graphicFailed` for one failed report.
112	    static func graphicFailed(_ report: GraphicReport) -> ExportError {
113	        .graphicFailed(
114	            name: report.name, frame: report.frame,
115	            message: report.diagnostics.first?.message ?? "the engine gave no reason")
116	    }
117	
118	    /// `result`, unless a graphic failed on `key`: then the file at
119	    /// `destination` is removed and the answer is `.graphicFailed`, whatever
120	    /// the pipeline said — a success, the cancel `pollProgress` asked for,
121	    /// or a reader's error.
122	    static func graphicOutcome(
123	        _ result: Result<URL, any Error>, key: Int?, destination: URL?
124	    ) -> Result<URL, any Error> {
125	        guard let key = key, let failure = GraphicRegistry.shared.failure(for: key) else {
126	            return result
127	        }
128	        if let destination = destination { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination) }
129	        return .failure(graphicFailed(failure))
130	    }
131	
132	    /// The pin's non-failed reports, one per diagnostic; each (name,
133	    /// message) once, its first frame kept, in arrival order (G-24 (c)).
134	    static func graphicWarnings(from reports: [GraphicReport]) -> [ExportGraphicWarning] {
135	        var seen = Set<[String]>()
136	        var warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning] = []
137	        for report in reports where !report.failed {
138	            for diagnostic in report.diagnostics
139	            where seen.insert([report.name, diagnostic.located]).inserted {
140	                warnings.append(ExportGraphicWarning(
141	                    name: report.name, frame: report.frame, message: diagnostic.located))
142	            }
143	        }
144	        return warnings
145	    }
146	
147	    /// `graphicWarnings(from:)` over what `key`'s pin holds; `[]` for nil.
148	    static func graphicWarnings(on key: Int?) -> [ExportGraphicWarning] {
149	        guard let key = key else { return [] }
150	        return graphicWarnings(from: GraphicRegistry.shared.reports(for: key))
151	    }
152	
153	    /// The count a finished export's line ends with: "" for none. `hover`
154	    /// true (the progress sheet) adds "(hover for details)"; false is the
155	    /// queue's row, whose label truncates its tail.
156	    static func graphicWarningSuffix(
157	        _ warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning], hover: Bool = true
158	    ) -> String {
159	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return "" }
160	        let count = warnings.count == 1 ? "1 graphic warning" : "\(warnings.count) graphic warnings"
161	        return " " + count + (hover ? " (hover for details)." : ".")
162	    }
163	
164	    /// The tooltip's list, one line each: "\"<name>\" at frame F: <message>"
165	    /// ("\"<name>\": <message>" with no frame); nil for none.
166	    static func graphicWarningDetails(_ warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]) -> String? {
167	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
168	        return warnings.map { warning in
169	            let place = warning.frame.map { " at frame \($0)" } ?? ""
170	            return "\"\(warning.name)\"\(place): \(warning.message)"
171	        }.joined(separator: "\n")
172	    }
173	}
174	
175	/// One distinct warning a graphic gave while an export drew it: the graphic,
176	/// the first frame (its own) it was given at, and the located message.
177	struct ExportGraphicWarning: Equatable {
178	    let name: String
179	    let frame: Int?
180	    let message: String
181	}
182	
183	extension GraphicDiagnostic {
184	    /// The message, then ` (line L, column C)` when it has a line.
185	    var located: String {
186	        guard let line = line else { return message }
187	        return message + " (line \(line)" + (column.map { ", column \($0)" } ?? "") + ")"
188	    }
189	}

content.content:
## Writing the file

The sheet has three buttons:

- **Cancel** closes the sheet. Nothing is written and nothing is remembered.
- **Export…** opens a save panel, then writes the file behind a progress sheet.
- **Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the Export Queue so you can keep editing.

Both are greyed out while the sheet cannot work out a valid file, for example when a custom field is empty. The readout then says what to fix.

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension (`Board v1.2.mp4`). It says what is being written: "Export the timeline as a movie.", "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." or "Export the timeline's audio."

## The Export Queue

**Window ▸ Export Queue** lists queued exports. It opens on its own whenever you click **Add to Queue**.

- Jobs run **one at a time**, in the order they were added, while you keep editing.
- An **AV1** or **VP9** job also waits for memory. These formats are encoded in software and use a lot of it: about 1.2–2.4 GB at 1080p and 4.4–8.1 GB at 4K for AV1, depending on Speed, and about 0.4–0.5 GB at 1080p and 1.1–1.6 GB at 4K for VP9. All AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job at once, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may use up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. A queued AV1 or VP9 job that would go over waits until enough of them finish, and its row says why. The row's status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit, which at most window widths is before the figures; hold the pointer over the row and its tooltip ends with the whole sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB." While it waits, a later job that fits runs first. When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large. An **Export…** sheet never waits: it is counted, and starts straight away.
- A job holds the timeline **as it was when you confirmed it**, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics. Edits, undos, relinks and even closing the document afterwards do not change what it writes.
- Each row shows the file's name and its state: **Waiting** (or the memory wait above), *Writing · 42 %* (or the measuring phase), the "Exported …" line with its graphic and cursor warning counts and its loudness figures, **Cancelled.**, **Cancelled before it started.**, or the reason a job failed. The tooltip shows the full path, the format, size and frame rate, the whole memory-wait sentence while a job waits for memory, and any graphic and cursor warnings.
- **Cancel** on a row stops that job and removes its half-written file. On a finished row the button reads **Remove** and takes the row out of the list. **Show** reveals a finished file in the Finder.
- If a later export writes to the same file, the earlier finished row reads "Overwritten by a later export to the same file."
- **Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row. **Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one.
- The line at the bottom, beside **Clear Finished** and **Cancel All**, counts the jobs: "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished".
- With nothing queued, the window says so: "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."

Closing the window stops nothing. Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** there is no progress sheet in the way: you can resume playback and keep editing while the job runs.

Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first: "An export is still being written." The message names the running file and counts the jobs still waiting ("“*name*” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting."). **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue and deletes the partly written file. This question comes after Frame Job has asked about unsaved documents.

Only queued exports are protected this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing does not ask, and the half-written file is left behind. Cancel that export first.

## Saving a single frame

**File ▸ Save Frame…** (⌥⌘E) saves the frame under the playhead as a still. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` for `:` (`Board 00-00-12-05.png`). Its **Format** popup offers:

| Format | Alpha | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PNG** | Kept | The default. |
| **JPEG** | None | A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. |
| **HEIC** | Kept | |

- The **Format** popup opens on PNG every time. It does not remember your last choice.
- Under the popup, a line says what the chosen format does with transparency: "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
- Choosing a format changes the file name's extension in the panel. A name you typed is kept.
- JPEG and HEIC are written at 90 % quality.

- The frame is drawn the way an export draws it, at the canvas's full size. Preview Quality, Show Ungraded and Show SDR Version never change it. There is no timecode burn-in.
- Inside a nest, the frame is the nest's own picture at the nest's time.
- A frame showing a deep still or a 10-bit VP9 clip is saved as a 16-bit PNG or 10-bit HEIC. JPEG is always 8-bit.
- In an HDR (HLG) project, PNG and HEIC keep the HLG picture and a JPEG is the SDR version (see [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md)).
- A clip with Remove Background waits up to 30 seconds for the person masks of that frame. When they are not ready by then, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet says so: "Saved without Remove Background", naming the clip's file.
- When there is no frame at the playhead, an alert says so.
- If the file cannot be written, an alert says why: the folder is missing or Frame Job cannot write into it, or this Mac has no encoder for the format.

Save Frame… is greyed out while the timeline is empty.

*Agents:* `render_frame` writes the same file for the same frame (see [For agents](#for-agents)).

## HDR projects

In an HDR (HLG) project the sheet has a **Dynamic Range** row under Format:

| Choice | What the file holds |
|---|---|
| **HDR (HLG)** | The HLG master. The default. |
| **HDR10 (PQ)** | An HDR10 file with fixed mastering metadata. |
| **SDR version** | The project converted to SDR. |

Only HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR (VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is always 8-bit and writes the SDR version). VP9 (WebM) is 10-bit (VP9 Profile 2) for HLG and HDR10, and 8-bit (Profile 0, which every player decodes) for the SDR version. On every other video format the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).

## Transparency

A canvas whose background is transparent (the **Background** row in the Document tab's Appearance section; see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#appearance)) keeps its transparency only in **ProRes 4444**, **HEVC with Alpha**, **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** and **Animated PNG**. When the format carries an alpha channel, the footnote ends in "alpha". Every other format composites the picture onto black. A GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so it is not one of the four.

Which transparent movie to send:

- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** plays with its transparency in Chrome and Firefox, in a web page's `<video>`. Safari has not been confirmed to show it (see Limits). Only a player that decodes VP9 with the libvpx decoder shows the transparency; others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque.
- **HEVC with Alpha** is the transparent movie for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
- **ProRes 4444** is the master for another editor.

The colour in all three is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.

While the canvas background is transparent, the Document tab says how many formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." These are the four formats above.

## Chapters

Chapter markers on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)) become chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter's name is the marker's name, or "Chapter *n*" for an unnamed one. A range export keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file, and the chapter already running when the range starts opens the file. WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG have no chapters.

MP4 and M4A files are written with their index at the front, so a player can start before the whole file has downloaded.

## What an export includes

- **The same picture and sound as the preview.** The export uses the same composition and the same compositor. View-only settings never reach it: Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version, Show Selection, safe areas and the scopes.
- **Speed ramps and Keep pitch off.** An export waits for the rendered audio of every speed ramp, and of every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, to finish before it writes, and shows "Preparing…" meanwhile. That sound is never exported silent (see [Speed](speed.md)). If it cannot be rendered, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …".
- **Remove Background.** A clip with Remove Background is drawn as the person alone in every frame of the file. Its person masks are made on this Mac as soon as the cutout is set, and an export waits, showing "Preparing…", until every mask it draws is made — GIF and APNG too. If they cannot be made, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file.
- **The gate, the leveller and the de-esser.** Their thresholds follow each clip's measured loudness, and the leveller works from the clip's speech too, so an export waits, showing "Preparing…", until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip in it has been measured. If a measurement has not landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." (see [Audio](audio.md#gate)).
- **Missing media.** A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence instead of failing the export.
- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Captions** are ordinary text clips, so they are always burned into the picture. To write a separate subtitle file, use **File ▸ Export Captions…** (see [Captions](captions.md)).

## For agents

`export` mirrors **Export…** with **Add to Queue**: it checks the request, puts the job in the Export Queue and answers at once with `{export_id, path, status}`. Status is `queued` or `running`.

| Argument | The sheet's control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` (required) | Format | `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif`, `apng`. |
| `path` (required) | Save panel | The folder must exist. An existing file is replaced. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and a different known media extension is replaced: `cut.mov` with `h264` writes `cut.mp4`. Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `size` | Size | `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (GIF and APNG only), or `[width, height]`. |
| `range` | Range | `project` (default) or `in_out`. Refused when there is no in/out range. |
| `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate` | Quality | Bits per second. On `av1`, `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft cap the file usually stays under. On `vp9_alpha_webm` it is the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone, and the transparency's stream comes on top of it (about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, measured). `audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate. |
| `loudness_lufs` | Loudness | −70 to 0. |
| `peak_dbtp` | (fixed at −1 on the sheet) | −20 to 0: the master limiter's ceiling, −1 when absent. Legal with or without `loudness_lufs`. |
| `audio_bits` | Bit depth | `16` (default) or `24`. `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only; refused on every other format. |
| `stems` | Stems | `tracks` or `names`. `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only; refused on every other format and when no track can be heard. See [Stems](#stems). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Burn in timecode | |
| `dynamic_range` | Dynamic Range | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. |
| `encoder_speed` | Speed | `faster`, `balanced` (default) or `smaller`. `av1` and `av1_webm` only; refused on every other format, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm` included. |

There is no frame-rate argument. An agent's export uses the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own.

Every refusal comes back from `export` itself, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline, or a graphic that does not compile.

- `export_status {export_id}` answers the job's row without waiting: `queued`, `running` (with `progress` from 0 to 1 and `phase`), `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Call it again after a pause until the job finishes.
  - Every answer has `path` and `elapsed` (seconds).
  - `done` adds `bytes`, the settings the file was written with, `burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range` in an HLG project, `encoder_speed` for AV1 and AV1 (WebM), `audio_bits` for WAV and AIFF, `stems` (`[{name, tracks, path}]`, each file beside the mix) when stems were asked, any `graphic_warnings` and, for every format with sound, `loudness`: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp` (the master limiter's), `limited_db` (how far it turned the loudest peak down), `capped_by_gain` (the 40 dB limit decided the gain) and `target_lufs`.
  - `queued` adds `waiting`, the row's "Waiting for memory: …" sentence, while an AV1 or VP9 job waits for memory.
  - `queued` and `running` add `estimated_seconds` for `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`: the export sheet's estimate of the whole export, in whole seconds.
  - `failed` and `cancelled` add `reason`, the queue row's sentence.
- `cancel_export {export_id}` is the row's Cancel.
- An `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
- `render_frame` renders one frame through the same path as Save Frame…. It returns the image inline and as a file, and with no `path` it writes a temporary PNG and names it. An explicit `format` wins and replaces the path's extension, so `{path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` writes `shot.png`. When a graphic in the frame warned or failed, the reply names it, its frame and the message, and a failed graphic draws its error card in the picture. A clip with Remove Background waits up to 30 s for its person masks, as Save Frame… does, and past that is drawn whole with "Clip *n* is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." in the reply. It takes `t` (default: the playhead), `path`, `format` (`png`, `jpeg`, `heic`), `max_width` and `burn_in_timecode`, plus `sdr_version`, `ungraded`, `selection` and the scope measurements described in [Colour grading](color-grading.md) and [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).

The full reference is [MCP](mcp.md).

## Limits

- An animated GIF or APNG holds at most **600 frames**: 48 seconds at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 seconds at APNG's 25 fps. A longer range is refused. Shorten the range or lower the frame rate.
- A loudness target more than 40 dB above the mix lands quieter than asked, and the report's `capped_by_gain` says so.
- The master limiter cannot be turned off; 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while editing than in the file.
- ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) refuse a custom size of a different shape from the canvas.
- VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only: an HDR project writes its SDR version, and HDR is refused on it.
- A VP9 with Alpha (WebM) file re-imported into Frame Job keeps its picture and loses its transparency: it shows opaque, with black where it was transparent. Export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha for a transparent clip to bring back in.
- Whether Safari shows VP9 with Alpha (WebM)'s transparency has not been confirmed; use HEVC with Alpha for Safari.
- A Mac with no encoder for a format reports "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." and leaves no file.
- 24-bit is offered on WAV and AIFF only. ProRes, AAC and Opus sound is 16-bit, and nothing is dithered.
- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
- Captions are burned in, never a switchable subtitle track.
- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
- The estimated time is the median of three measured exports per format and size, of real 4K camera footage on one idle Mac (an Apple M2 Max). On exports it was not fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time; a slower Mac, a busy one or a heavier timeline takes longer.
- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

1	import CoreGraphics
2	import CoreVideo
3	import Foundation
4	import ImageIO
5	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
6	
7	/// One composed frame written to a file: a `CGImage` and a format in, a URL
8	/// out (road map 2 phase 7a).
9	///
10	/// It is `AudioNormalize.swift`'s shape applied to pictures, and it is a value
11	/// type for the same reason that one is. **File ▸ Save Frame… and the agent's
12	/// `render_frame` call this and nothing else**, so "Save Frame's PNG is
13	/// byte-identical to `render_frame`'s" is a fact about the code rather than a
14	/// claim in a comment — and it is the only way the line can ever be checked,
15	/// because a save panel cannot be driven over MCP or offscreen and a proof
16	/// script can therefore never press the menu item. Anything that goes in here
17	/// changes both paths at once; anything that lives in only one of them is a
18	/// place the two can drift.
19	///
20	/// So there is deliberately **no `NSSavePanel`, no `ProjectDocument` and no
21	/// AppKit view in this file**. Picking the URL is
22	/// `EditorViewController+SaveFrame.swift`'s job and naming a temporary file is
23	/// `AgentServer+Render.swift`'s; both hand the result here.
24	///
25	/// **PNG's properties dictionary is `nil`, and it must stay `nil`.** That is
26	/// what `render_frame` has always passed (`AgentServer+Render.swift`), and
27	/// every phase from 1 to 6 compares PNG bytes against frames written that
28	/// way. Anything that ADDS metadata changes the file: phase 7's proof
29	/// mutated this to `[kCGImagePropertyDPIWidth: 144]` and caught it by the
30	/// extra `pHYs` chunk.
31	///
32	/// The honest limit, measured rather than assumed, because the sentence
33	/// above invites a stronger claim than the platform supports: on macOS
34	/// 26.5.1 an EMPTY dictionary and no dictionary write byte-identical PNGs
35	/// (same sha256, same 5330 bytes, same chunk list, across two processes).
36	/// So no BYTE comparison can catch `[:]` here — but the rule is not
37	/// unguarded, and saying it was would send the next reader looking for a
38	/// check that exists: `phase7_chrome.py` reads `destinationProperties != nil`
39	/// STRUCTURALLY through the probe, which is what an empty dictionary fails
40	/// and a byte comparison cannot. That is a fact about this ImageIO, not a
41	/// licence — the rule stays `nil`, because the next ImageIO owes us nothing
42	/// and the failure would then arrive as a rendering change in five scripts
43	/// at once.
44	///
45	/// **JPEG flattens onto BLACK, and it says so out loud.** JPEG is the one of
46	/// the three containers that cannot carry an alpha channel at all, and phase
47	/// 7b makes a transparent canvas reachable in this very phase — so a person
48	/// who has just set the canvas to Transparent and saves a JPEG would otherwise
49	/// get whatever ImageIO happens to do with the premultiplied pixels, silently.
50	/// Black is the choice rather than white because black is what the preview
51	/// well and the exported movie already show behind the canvas: the still then
52	/// matches the picture the person was looking at when they asked for it. The
53	/// flatten belongs to JPEG ALONE — PNG and HEIC both carry alpha, so nothing
54	/// is thrown away in those two, and adding a flatten to them would destroy
55	/// information the format was chosen for. The panel's hint carries the same
56	/// sentence, because a silent flatten is the thing being avoided. JPEG is
57	/// also the one that holds 8 bits a component whatever it is handed, which is
58	/// why `Format.carriesDepth` is false for it alone and no frame grabbed for a
59	/// JPEG is read through the reader (spec §11 PR-9).
60	///
61	/// **The quality is 0.9, not `MediaImporter.writeJPEG`'s 0.7.** Those two
62	/// numbers answer different questions: a filmstrip thumbnail is 54 px tall and
63	/// is discarded when the cache is cleared, while this is a delivery still
64	/// somebody is about to put in a document. Neither number is a compromise
65	/// between the two, which is why they are written down separately rather than
66	/// shared through a constant.
67	enum FrameWriter {
68	
69	    // MARK: - The formats
70	
71	    /// The three containers Save Frame writes, each declaring everything that
72	    /// is true of it in ONE place: its type, the extension a file of it takes,
73	    /// what a menu calls it, and whether it can hold an alpha channel.
74	    ///
75	    /// The `rawValue` is a stable identifier for the agent's vocabulary and is
76	    /// deliberately NOT the file extension — JPEG's are "jpeg" and "jpg" and
77	    /// collapsing them would make one of the two wrong. `format(for:)` reads
78	    /// both spellings back.
79	    ///
80	    /// `UTType.heic` and not `public.heif`: only the former is in
81	    /// `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()` on macOS 15, so a destination
82	    /// created for the latter is nil and the write fails at the last moment
83	    /// with nothing to say. Measured, not assumed.
84	    enum Format: String, CaseIterable {
85	        case png
86	        case jpeg
87	        case heic
88	
89	        var contentType: UTType {
90	            switch self {
91	            case .png: return .png
92	            case .jpeg: return .jpeg
93	            case .heic: return .heic
94	            }
95	        }
96	
97	        /// The extension a file of this format takes. One spelling per
98	        /// format: the panel writes it, `destinationURL` replaces with it and
99	        /// `format(for:)` reads every accepted spelling back to it.
100	        var fileExtension: String {
101	            switch self {
102	            case .png: return "png"
103	            case .jpeg: return "jpg"
104	            case .heic: return "heic"
105	            }
106	        }
107	
108	        /// Every spelling of this format's extension the app READS — one
109	        /// each, and JPEG's two, `fileExtension` first.
110	        ///
111	        /// It is the vocabulary and not just a list: `format(for:)` reads a
112	        /// name with it and the save panel's format popup decides with it
113	        /// which trailing dot-suffix is an EXTENSION it may replace and which

180	
181	    /// Failures name the PATH, never a bare `false`. A frame grab that
182	    /// answered only "no" would leave a person guessing between a folder they
183	    /// cannot write, a format this Mac's ImageIO does not know and an encoder
184	    /// that gave up — three different things to do about it.
185	    ///
186	    /// **So the first two are two CASES and not one sentence**, and the
187	    /// review is what settled it: `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answers
188	    /// nil for both, and a single message asserting the format was the wrong
189	    /// one of the three for the case a caller actually hits. Measured here
190	    /// (macOS 26.5.1): it answers nil for `/card.png`, for
191	    /// `/private/var/db/x.png`, for `/System/nowhere/card.png` and for a
192	    /// path that is an existing directory — every one of them a PNG this Mac
193	    /// writes perfectly, and the agent reaches all four, because
194	    /// `render_frame` takes a caller's path and a launched `.app`'s working
195	    /// directory is `/`. Telling somebody to go looking for a missing
196	    /// encoder when the answer is a folder they cannot write is worse than
197	    /// saying nothing.
198	    enum WriteError: LocalizedError {
199	        /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answered nil for a type this
200	        /// machine's ImageIO does not WRITE. Decided by asking
201	        /// `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()`, which is a question
202	        /// about the machine and carries no URL in it.
203	        case unsupported(Format, URL)
204	        /// `CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL` answered nil for a type this
205	        /// machine DOES write, so what it could not do is create the file:
206	        /// a folder that is not there, one this app may not write into, a
207	        /// read-only or absent volume, or a path that is itself a directory.
208	        /// ImageIO tells those apart nowhere, so the message names the CLASS
209	        /// and asks the two questions a person can answer, rather than
210	        /// inventing a cause. The agent is the caller that reaches it — an
211	        /// `NSSavePanel` choice confers access to the URL it returns even for
212	        /// an unsandboxed app, so Save Frame reaches it only where the volume
213	        /// or the folder went away between the panel and the write.
214	        case unwritable(Format, URL)
215	        /// The opaque bitmap the JPEG flatten draws into could not be made.
216	        case flattenFailed(URL)
217	        /// `CGImageDestinationFinalize` answered false.
218	        case encodingFailed(Format, URL)
219	        /// A JPEG asked of an HLG project's frame (spec §11 HD-13 (i)): eight
220	        /// bits labelled BT.709 cannot carry it until H-3's SDR version.
221	        case hlgJPEG
222	
223	        var errorDescription: String? {
224	            switch self {
225	            case .unsupported(let format, let url):
226	                return "Could not write \(format.displayName) to \(url.path). "
227	                    + "This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format."
228	            case .unwritable(let format, let url):
229	                return "Could not write \(format.displayName) to \(url.path). "
230	                    + "The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists "
231	                    + "and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it."
232	            case .flattenFailed(let url):
233	                return "Could not flatten the frame onto black for \(url.path)."
234	            case .encodingFailed(let format, let url):
235	                return "\(format.displayName) encoding failed for \(url.path)."
236	            case .hlgJPEG:
237	                return "JPEG cannot carry an HLG project's picture; save the frame as PNG or HEIC"
238	            }
239	        }
240	    }

242	    /// Which of the two nil-destination failures happened, asked the only way
243	    /// ImageIO answers it: `CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers()` is the
244	    /// list of types this machine WRITES, so a format on that list did not
245	    /// fail for being unknown and the URL is what is left.
246	    ///
247	    /// It runs only on the failure path, so the ordinary write pays nothing
248	    /// for it; and it probes no file — `isWritableFile(atPath:)` answers a
249	    /// permission bit, which is not the question when the refusal is TCC's or
250	    /// the parent is missing, and a probe write would be a second way to
251	    /// create the very file being reported.
252	    private static func destinationFailure(_ format: Format, _ url: URL) -> WriteError {
253	        let writable = (CGImageDestinationCopyTypeIdentifiers() as NSArray as? [String]) ?? []
254	        return writable.contains(format.contentType.identifier)
255	            ? .unwritable(format, url)
256	            : .unsupported(format, url)
257	    }

261	    /// The format `url` names, or `requested` when a caller has said. Both
262	    /// spellings of JPEG read back to one case; anything unrecognised is PNG,
263	    /// which is the row that loses nothing.
264	    ///
265	    /// It is `CaptionExporter.format(for:requested:)` verbatim in shape, and
266	    /// for that function's reason: the panel and the agent both end here, so
267	    /// "what did this path ask for" is answered once.
268	    ///
269	    /// The spellings read here are exactly the ones in
270	    /// `AgentServer.replaceableExtensions`, and they have to be: a name this
271	    /// app never writes is part of the NAME rather than an extension (that
272	    /// set's own rule), so recognising a spelling here that the set does not
273	    /// replace would turn `shot.heif` into `shot.heif.heic` — the doubled name
274	    /// the whole mechanism exists to prevent. `heif` is the one that tempts,
275	    /// and it is left out on both sides together.
276	    static func format(for url: URL, requested: Format? = nil) -> Format {
277	        if let requested = requested { return requested }
278	        let suffix = url.pathExtension.lowercased()
279	        return Format.allCases.first { $0.acceptedExtensions.contains(suffix) } ?? .png
280	    }

282	    /// Every extension this app writes a still under, lower-cased — the union
283	    /// of the three formats' `acceptedExtensions`. `renamed` is the caller and
284	    /// carries the argument for having a set at all.
285	    static let knownExtensions = Set(Format.allCases.flatMap { $0.acceptedExtensions })

287	    /// A save panel's name field rewritten for a newly chosen format: the
288	    /// stem it already holds, then that format's extension. `fallback` is
289	    /// what an empty field falls back to.
290	    ///
291	    /// **Only a suffix this app WRITES is an extension**, and the rest of the
292	    /// name is the person's. `deletingPathExtension` takes whatever follows
293	    /// the last dot whatever it is, so the format popup used to turn
294	    /// `Board v1.2` into `Board v1.jpg` — eating a character somebody typed
295	    /// on purpose while doing exactly what it was told. That is the same
296	    /// hazard `AgentServer.destinationURL` avoids for that same name — it
297	    /// strips only a member of `replaceableExtensions` and APPENDS otherwise,
298	    /// so `Board v1.2` over MCP is written as `Board v1.2.png` and always
299	    /// was; `knownExtensions` is this side's half of the one rule.
300	    /// Measured: `("Board v1.2" as NSString).deletingPathExtension` is
301	    /// "Board v1", and `("shot.final" as NSString)`'s is "shot".
302	    ///
303	    /// It is a function of a string and lives HERE rather than in the panel
304	    /// for the reason `write` does: an accessory view's private method is
305	    /// reachable by no proof this project can write, because a save panel
306	    /// cannot be driven over MCP or offscreen — so a rule kept there is a
307	    /// rule nothing can check. As a pure function a probe compiled from
308	    /// `app/Sources` calls it with a table of names (`AudioNormalize.swift`'s
309	    /// argument, and `CaptionCues`') — `tools/proof/remaining_probe.py`,
310	    /// section 1, the first instrument to have actually done so.
311	    static func renamed(_ name: String, as format: Format, fallback: String) -> String {
312	        let suffix = (name as NSString).pathExtension.lowercased()
313	        let stem =
314	            knownExtensions.contains(suffix)
315	            ? (name as NSString).deletingPathExtension : name
316	        return "\(stem.isEmpty ? fallback : stem).\(format.fileExtension)"
317	    }

321	    /// Writes `image` to `url` and answers the URL it wrote. The caller owns
322	    /// the path — this creates no folders and replaces no extension, because
323	    /// the two callers disagree about both (the panel has already asked a
324	    /// person, and the agent runs its path through
325	    /// `AgentServer.destinationURL`).
326	    @discardableResult
327	    static func write(_ image: CGImage, as format: Format, to url: URL) throws -> URL {
328	        let subject = format.carriesAlpha ? image : try flattenedOntoBlack(image, for: url)
329	        guard let destination = CGImageDestinationCreateWithURL(
330	            url as CFURL, format.contentType.identifier as CFString, 1, nil)
331	        else {
332	            throw destinationFailure(format, url)
333	        }
334	        CGImageDestinationAddImage(destination, subject, format.destinationProperties)
335	        guard CGImageDestinationFinalize(destination) else {
336	            throw WriteError.encodingFailed(format, url)
337	        }
338	        return url
339	    }

341	    /// `image` composited over black in an OPAQUE bitmap — the JPEG flatten.
342	    ///
343	    /// It is a real draw rather than a hint to the encoder because there is no
344	    /// such hint: handed premultiplied pixels with alpha, a JPEG destination
345	    /// simply drops the alpha channel, which leaves a half-transparent white
346	    /// title composited as mid-grey and a fully transparent canvas as black
347	    /// anyway — the right answer in one case and a wrong one in the other, with
348	    /// no way to tell them apart afterwards. Compositing first makes every
349	    /// pixel the same arithmetic the compositor and the exported movie already
350	    /// do against their black ground.
351	    ///
352	    /// It runs for EVERY JPEG, including a frame that carries no alpha at all.
353	    /// Short-circuiting an opaque source would be one branch and one saved
354	    /// copy, and it would buy a second way for a JPEG to be produced — a
355	    /// direct encode whose colour handling need not match the drawn one's, on
356	    /// a path nothing measures. One path per format is worth a full-frame
357	    /// draw at the speed a person presses a menu item.
358	    ///
359	    /// Eight bits a component, deliberately: JPEG has no more, so a frame from
360	    /// a 10-bit source (which `render_frame` writes as 16-bit float from a
361	    /// ProRes or HEVC Main 10 clip) is truncated here rather than at some
362	    /// later point where it would look like a rendering difference. The colour space is the image's own where it is
363	    /// an RGB one, so the flatten changes coverage and nothing else; a source
364	    /// in any other model falls back to device RGB, which is the only thing
365	    /// `noneSkipLast` can be built over.
366	    private static func flattenedOntoBlack(_ image: CGImage, for url: URL) throws -> CGImage {
367	        let space: CGColorSpace = {
368	            if let own = image.colorSpace, own.model == .rgb { return own }
369	            return CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB()
370	        }()
371	        guard image.width > 0, image.height > 0,
372	            let context = CGContext(
373	                data: nil, width: image.width, height: image.height, bitsPerComponent: 8,
374	                bytesPerRow: 0, space: space,
375	                bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.noneSkipLast.rawValue)
376	        else {
377	            throw WriteError.flattenFailed(url)
378	        }
379	        let rect = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: image.width, height: image.height)
380	        context.setFillColor(red: 0, green: 0, blue: 0, alpha: 1)
381	        context.fill(rect)
382	        context.draw(image, in: rect)
383	        guard let flattened = context.makeImage() else {
384	            throw WriteError.flattenFailed(url)
385	        }
386	        return flattened
387	    }
388	}

3	// `ExportWriter`'s chapter half: the chapter list an export writes, the text track that
4	// carries it, its pump, and the text samples themselves. A pure move out of
5	// `ExporterWriter.swift` at its size cap (issue batch B92); the members each file calls in
6	// the other lost `private`, and nothing else changed.
7	
8	// MARK: - Chapters
9	
10	/// One entry of the chapter list an export writes (spec §7.8).
11	///
12	/// Chapters come from the PROJECT, never from the composition plan: the plan
13	/// says what to decode and where to put it, and markers decode nothing, so
14	/// `plan.rs` emits no marker key at all. `Exporter` reads them off the
15	/// snapshot of the handle it was given and hands them over here, which is
16	/// also why an export shows the chapters the timeline had when the sheet was
17	/// confirmed rather than the ones it has when the write ends.
18	struct ExportChapter: Equatable {
19	    /// Timeline ticks, in the project's own time. Clamping into the exported
20	    /// range and rebasing to a zero-based file both happen when the samples
21	    /// are built, because only then is the range known.
22	    let start: Ticks
23	    /// What the chapter is called. Never empty — an unnamed marker becomes
24	    /// "Chapter <n>", because a chapter list of blank rows is worse in every
25	    /// player than no chapter list at all.
26	    let name: String
27	
28	    /// The project's `chapter` markers, in time order and named.
29	    ///
30	    /// Numbering is over the CHAPTER markers only, so deleting a plain marker
31	    /// cannot renumber the chapters around it.
32	    static func list(from markers: [MarkerSnapshot]) -> [ExportChapter] {
33	        markers
34	            .filter(\.chapter)
35	            .sorted { $0.time < $1.time }
36	            .enumerated()
37	            .map { index, marker in
38	                let name = marker.name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
39	                return ExportChapter(
40	                    start: marker.time, name: name.isEmpty ? "Chapter \(index + 1)" : name)
41	            }
42	    }
43	}

45	extension ExportChapter {
46	    /// The chapters clamped into `range` and rebased to zero, each with its span in the file:
47	    /// the one rule both writers write chapters by (`ExportWriter`'s text track,
48	    /// `ExportWebMWriter`'s Chapters element, spec §11 CX-15 (2)).
49	    ///
50	    /// Each chapter runs until the next one, and the last until the end of
51	    /// the range — a chapter list is a partition of the movie, not a set of
52	    /// points. A chapter that began BEFORE an in/out range is not dropped:
53	    /// the last of them is pinned to the start of the range, because the
54	    /// exported piece really is inside that chapter and a file whose first
55	    /// minutes belong to no chapter reads as a bug.
56	    static func partition(
57	        _ chapters: [ExportChapter], in range: CMTimeRange
58	    ) -> [(name: String, range: CMTimeRange)] {
59	        let start = CompositionBuilder.ticks(range.start)
60	        let end = start + CompositionBuilder.ticks(range.duration)
61	        guard end > start else { return [] }
62	
63	        var inside: [ExportChapter] = []
64	        for chapter in chapters where chapter.start < end {
65	            if chapter.start <= start {
66	                inside = [ExportChapter(start: start, name: chapter.name)]
67	            } else {
68	                inside.append(chapter)
69	            }
70	        }
71	        var parts: [(name: String, range: CMTimeRange)] = []
72	        for (index, chapter) in inside.enumerated() {
73	            let next = index + 1 < inside.count ? inside[index + 1].start : end
74	            guard next > chapter.start else { continue }
75	            parts.append((chapter.name, CMTimeRange(
76	                start: CompositionBuilder.time(chapter.start - start),
77	                duration: CompositionBuilder.time(next - chapter.start))))
78	        }
79	        return parts
80	    }
81	}

85	    /// The chapter track: a text track carrying one sample per chapter,
86	    /// associated with the movie's own track through
87	    /// `AVTrackAssociationTypeChapterList`, which is what writes the `chap`
88	    /// track reference every reader (QuickTime, `ffprobe -show_chapters`)
89	    /// looks for.
90	    ///
91	    /// Additive, never fatal: a build of macOS that will not take the text
92	    /// track loses the chapters, not the movie. The track is marked disabled
93	    /// so no player tries to draw the names over the picture.
94	    ///
95	    /// **A container that cannot hold a chapter track is refused HERE, not
96	    /// left to `canAdd`.** A chapter list is a second track associated with
97	    /// the first, which is a QuickTime-family idea; a RIFF or an IFF file is
98	    /// a header followed by samples with nowhere to put one. `canAdd` is the
99	    /// wrong guard for that because the failure it would let through is the
100	    /// expensive one: a `true` followed by a refusal at `finishWriting`
101	    /// loses the whole file, which is exactly what a malformed text format
102	    /// description already cost once (see `textFormat`).
103	    func addChapters(_ chapters: [ExportChapter], settings: ExportSettings) {
104	        guard Self.carriesChapters(settings), !chapters.isEmpty,
105	            let host = videoInput ?? audioInput, let format = Self.textFormat()
106	        else { return }
107	        let samples = Self.chapterSamples(chapters, in: range, format: format)
108	        guard !samples.isEmpty else { return }
109	
110	        let input = AVAssetWriterInput(
111	            mediaType: .text, outputSettings: nil, sourceFormatHint: format)
112	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
113	        input.marksOutputTrackAsEnabled = false
114	        guard writer.canAdd(input) else { return }
115	        writer.add(input)
116	        host.addTrackAssociation(
117	            withTrackOf: input, type: AVAssetTrack.AssociationType.chapterList.rawValue)

122	    /// The chapter samples are a handful of tiny text buffers, all known
123	    /// before the write starts, so this pump has nothing to read — it drains
124	    /// its own array.
125	    func pumpChapters(
126	        _ input: AVAssetWriterInput, on queue: DispatchQueue, group: DispatchGroup
127	    ) {
128	        group.enter()
129	        var pending = chapterSamples
130	        var finished = false
131	        let stop: () -> Void = {
132	            guard !finished else { return }
133	            finished = true
134	            input.markAsFinished()
135	            group.leave()
136	        }
137	        input.requestMediaDataWhenReady(on: queue) { [weak self] in
138	            guard let self = self else { return }
139	            while input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
140	                guard !finished else { return }
141	                guard !self.isStopping, !pending.isEmpty else {
142	                    stop()
143	                    return
144	                }
145	                let sample = pending.removeFirst()
146	                guard input.append(sample) else {
147	                    // A chapter that will not write is not worth losing the
148	                    // movie over: the text track simply ends here.
149	                    stop()
150	                    return
151	                }
152	            }
153	        }
154	    }

157	
158	    /// The format one chapter sample is written in: a QuickTime text
159	    /// (`'text'`) description, in every container this build writes.
160	    ///
161	    /// **Why the byte structure and not `CMFormatDescriptionCreate`.** A
162	    /// description created from a media type and a subtype alone carries no
163	    /// extensions, and `AVAssetWriter` cannot serialise that into a sample
164	    /// description — it fails the whole write at `finishWriting` with
165	    /// `kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter` (-12712), losing
166	    /// the movie, not just the chapters (measured). Handing the bridge the
167	    /// big-endian `TextDescription` the QuickTime file format specifies is
168	    /// exactly the shape it will write back out, so there is nothing left to
169	    /// guess at.
170	    ///
171	    /// **Why QuickTime text rather than 3GPP `tx3g` in the MPEG-4 family.**
172	    /// A `'text'` sample entry is what Apple's own chapter tracks use inside
173	    /// `.m4a`/`.m4v`/`.mp4`, and both QuickTime and `ffprobe`'s MOV demuxer
174	    /// read chapters from it; `tx3g` would mean a second byte layout and a
175	    /// font table for no gain.
176	    private static func textFormat() -> CMFormatDescription? {
177	        var description = Data()
178	        func be16(_ value: UInt16) { description.append(contentsOf: [
179	            UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: value >> 8), UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: value)]) }
180	        func be32(_ value: UInt32) { be16(UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: value >> 16))
181	            be16(UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: value)) }
182	
183	        be32(60)                                   // descSize, this whole record
184	        be32(0x7465_7874)                          // 'text'
185	        be32(0)                                    // reserved
186	        be16(0)                                    // reserved
187	        be16(1)                                    // data reference index
188	        be32(0)                                    // display flags: none
189	        be32(0)                                    // text justification: left
190	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(0)                  // background colour: black
191	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(0); be16(0)         // default text box: empty
192	        be32(0)                                    // default style: start char
193	        be16(0); be16(0)                           // height, ascent
194	        be16(0); be16(0); be16(12)                 // font, face, size
195	        be16(0xFFFF); be16(0xFFFF); be16(0xFFFF)   // foreground colour: white
196	        description.append(0)                      // font name, an empty
197	        description.append(0)                      //   Pascal string, padded
198	
199	        var format: CMFormatDescription?
200	        let status = description.withUnsafeBytes { bytes -> OSStatus in
201	            guard let base = bytes.bindMemory(to: UInt8.self).baseAddress else { return -1 }
202	            // A nil flavor is the QuickTime Movie one.
203	            return CMTextFormatDescriptionCreateFromBigEndianTextDescriptionData(
204	                allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, bigEndianTextDescriptionData: base,
205	                size: description.count, flavor: nil, mediaType: kCMMediaType_Text,
206	                formatDescriptionOut: &format)
207	        }
208	        return status == noErr ? format : nil
209	    }
210	
211	    /// The chapters as samples, clamped into `range` and rebased to zero
212	    /// (`ExportChapter.partition`).
213	    private static func chapterSamples(
214	        _ chapters: [ExportChapter], in range: CMTimeRange, format: CMFormatDescription
215	    ) -> [CMSampleBuffer] {
216	        ExportChapter.partition(chapters, in: range).compactMap {
217	            chapterSample($0.name, timeRange: $0.range, format: format)
218	        }
219	    }
220	
221	    /// One text sample: a 16-bit big-endian byte count followed by the UTF-8
222	    /// name, which is the payload both QuickTime text and 3GPP timed text
223	    /// carry. Names are truncated at the length that count can express —
224	    /// 64 KB of chapter title is not a case worth failing an export over.
225	    private static func chapterSample(
226	        _ name: String, timeRange: CMTimeRange, format: CMFormatDescription
227	    ) -> CMSampleBuffer? {
228	        var text = Array(name.utf8)
229	        if text.count > 0xFFFF { text = Array(text.prefix(0xFFFF)) }
230	        var payload: [UInt8] = [UInt8(text.count >> 8), UInt8(text.count & 0xFF)]
231	        payload.append(contentsOf: text)
232	
233	        var block: CMBlockBuffer?
234	        guard CMBlockBufferCreateWithMemoryBlock(
235	            allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, memoryBlock: nil, blockLength: payload.count,
236	            blockAllocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, customBlockSource: nil, offsetToData: 0,
237	            dataLength: payload.count, flags: 0, blockBufferOut: &block) == kCMBlockBufferNoErr,
238	            let buffer = block,
239	            CMBlockBufferReplaceDataBytes(
240	                with: payload, blockBuffer: buffer, offsetIntoDestination: 0,
241	                dataLength: payload.count) == kCMBlockBufferNoErr
242	        else { return nil }
243	
244	        var timing = CMSampleTimingInfo(
245	            duration: timeRange.duration, presentationTimeStamp: timeRange.start,
246	            decodeTimeStamp: .invalid)
247	        var size = payload.count
248	        var sample: CMSampleBuffer?
249	        guard CMSampleBufferCreate(
250	            allocator: kCFAllocatorDefault, dataBuffer: buffer, dataReady: true,
251	            makeDataReadyCallback: nil, refcon: nil, formatDescription: format, sampleCount: 1,
252	            sampleTimingEntryCount: 1, sampleTimingArray: &timing, sampleSizeEntryCount: 1,
253	            sampleSizeArray: &size, sampleBufferOut: &sample) == noErr
254	        else { return nil }
255	        return sample
256	    }
257	}

143	    /// What a finished write becomes when the reason it failed is that this
144	    /// Mac has no encoder for the row (spec §11 G-33 (e)): the preset's own
145	    /// sentence, and no file.
146	    ///
147	    /// `ExportWriter.addVideo` cannot see it. Measured with an encoder
148	    /// specification nothing satisfies, on `.hevcWithAlpha` and `.hevc`
149	    /// alike: `canApply` is true, the input constructs, `canAdd` is true, and
150	    /// `startWriting()` then fails with `AVFoundationErrorDomain` −11834
151	    /// ("Cannot Encode"), leaving a 0-byte file at the destination. So it is
152	    /// mapped here, where `startWriting` hears the pipeline: exactly that
153	    /// domain and code become `.presetUnavailable` with the preset's name and
154	    /// the file is removed, and every other result is returned as it came.
155	    static func encoderOutcome(
156	        _ result: Result<URL, any Error>, settings: ExportSettings, destination: URL
157	    ) -> Result<URL, any Error> {
158	        guard case .failure(let error) = result else { return result }
159	        let reason = error as NSError
160	        guard reason.domain == AVFoundationErrorDomain,
161	            reason.code == AVError.Code.encoderNotFound.rawValue
162	        else { return result }
163	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
164	        return .failure(ExportError.presetUnavailable(ExportWriter.presetName(settings)))
165	    }
