## Writing the file

The sheet has three buttons:

- **Cancel** closes the sheet. Nothing is written and nothing is remembered.
- **Export…** opens a save panel, then writes the file behind a progress sheet.
- **Add to Queue** opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the Export Queue so you can keep editing.

Both are greyed out while the sheet cannot work out a valid file, for example when a custom field is empty. The readout then says what to fix.

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension (`Board v1.2.mp4`). It says what is being written: "Export the timeline as a movie.", "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." or "Export the timeline's audio."

## The Export Queue

**Window ▸ Export Queue** lists queued exports. It opens on its own whenever you click **Add to Queue**.

- Jobs run **one at a time**, in the order they were added, while you keep editing.
- An **AV1** or **VP9** job also waits for memory. These formats are encoded in software and use a lot of it: about 1.2–2.4 GB at 1080p and 4.4–8.1 GB at 4K for AV1, depending on Speed, and about 0.4–0.5 GB at 1080p and 1.1–1.6 GB at 4K for VP9. All AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job at once, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may use up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. A queued AV1 or VP9 job that would go over waits until enough of them finish, and its row says why. The row's status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit, which at most window widths is before the figures; hold the pointer over the row and its tooltip ends with the whole sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB." While it waits, a later job that fits runs first. When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large. An **Export…** sheet never waits: it is counted, and starts straight away.
- A job holds the timeline **as it was when you confirmed it**, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics. Edits, undos, relinks and even closing the document afterwards do not change what it writes.
- Each row shows the file's name and its state: **Waiting** (or the memory wait above), *Writing · 42 %* (or the measuring phase), the "Exported …" line with its graphic and cursor warning counts and its loudness figures, **Cancelled.**, **Cancelled before it started.**, or the reason a job failed. The tooltip shows the full path, the format, size and frame rate, the whole memory-wait sentence while a job waits for memory, and any graphic and cursor warnings.
- **Cancel** on a row stops that job and removes its half-written file. On a finished row the button reads **Remove** and takes the row out of the list. **Show** reveals a finished file in the Finder.
- If a later export writes to the same file, the earlier finished row reads "Overwritten by a later export to the same file."
- **Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row. **Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one.
- The line at the bottom, beside **Clear Finished** and **Cancel All**, counts the jobs: "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished".
- With nothing queued, the window says so: "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."

Closing the window stops nothing. Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** there is no progress sheet in the way: you can resume playback and keep editing while the job runs.

Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first: "An export is still being written." The message names the running file and counts the jobs still waiting ("“*name*” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting."). **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue and deletes the partly written file. This question comes after Frame Job has asked about unsaved documents.

Only queued exports are protected this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing does not ask, and the half-written file is left behind. Cancel that export first.

## Saving a single frame

**File ▸ Save Frame…** (⌥⌘E) saves the frame under the playhead as a still. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` for `:` (`Board 00-00-12-05.png`). Its **Format** popup offers:

| Format | Alpha | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PNG** | Kept | The default. |
| **JPEG** | None | A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. |
| **HEIC** | Kept | |

- The **Format** popup opens on PNG every time. It does not remember your last choice.
- Under the popup, a line says what the chosen format does with transparency: "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."
- Choosing a format changes the file name's extension in the panel. A name you typed is kept.
- JPEG and HEIC are written at 90 % quality.

- The frame is drawn the way an export draws it, at the canvas's full size. Preview Quality, Show Ungraded and Show SDR Version never change it. There is no timecode burn-in.
- Inside a nest, the frame is the nest's own picture at the nest's time.
- A frame showing a deep still or a 10-bit VP9 clip is saved as a 16-bit PNG or 10-bit HEIC. JPEG is always 8-bit.
- In an HDR (HLG) project, PNG and HEIC keep the HLG picture and a JPEG is the SDR version (see [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md)).
- A clip with Remove Background waits up to 30 seconds for the person masks of that frame. When they are not ready by then, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet says so: "Saved without Remove Background", naming the clip's file.
- When there is no frame at the playhead, an alert says so.
- If the file cannot be written, an alert says why: the folder is missing or Frame Job cannot write into it, or this Mac has no encoder for the format.

Save Frame… is greyed out while the timeline is empty.

*Agents:* `render_frame` writes the same file for the same frame (see [For agents](#for-agents)).

## HDR projects

In an HDR (HLG) project the sheet has a **Dynamic Range** row under Format:

| Choice | What the file holds |
|---|---|
| **HDR (HLG)** | The HLG master. The default. |
| **HDR10 (PQ)** | An HDR10 file with fixed mastering metadata. |
| **SDR version** | The project converted to SDR. |

Only HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR (VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is always 8-bit and writes the SDR version). VP9 (WebM) is 10-bit (VP9 Profile 2) for HLG and HDR10, and 8-bit (Profile 0, which every player decodes) for the SDR version. On every other video format the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).

## Transparency

A canvas whose background is transparent (the **Background** row in the Document tab's Appearance section; see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#appearance)) keeps its transparency only in **ProRes 4444**, **HEVC with Alpha**, **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** and **Animated PNG**. When the format carries an alpha channel, the footnote ends in "alpha". Every other format composites the picture onto black. A GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so it is not one of the four.

Which transparent movie to send:

- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** plays with its transparency in Chrome and Firefox, in a web page's `<video>`. Safari has not been confirmed to show it (see Limits). Only a player that decodes VP9 with the libvpx decoder shows the transparency; others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque.
- **HEVC with Alpha** is the transparent movie for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
- **ProRes 4444** is the master for another editor.

The colour in all three is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.

While the canvas background is transparent, the Document tab says how many formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." These are the four formats above.

## Chapters

Chapter markers on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)) become chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter's name is the marker's name, or "Chapter *n*" for an unnamed one. A range export keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file, and the chapter already running when the range starts opens the file. WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG have no chapters.

MP4 and M4A files are written with their index at the front, so a player can start before the whole file has downloaded.

## What an export includes

- **The same picture and sound as the preview.** The export uses the same composition and the same compositor. View-only settings never reach it: Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version, Show Selection, safe areas and the scopes.
- **Speed ramps and Keep pitch off.** An export waits for the rendered audio of every speed ramp, and of every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, to finish before it writes, and shows "Preparing…" meanwhile. That sound is never exported silent (see [Speed](speed.md)). If it cannot be rendered, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …".
- **Remove Background.** A clip with Remove Background is drawn as the person alone in every frame of the file. Its person masks are made on this Mac as soon as the cutout is set, and an export waits, showing "Preparing…", until every mask it draws is made — GIF and APNG too. If they cannot be made, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file.
- **The gate, the leveller and the de-esser.** Their thresholds follow each clip's measured loudness, and the leveller works from the clip's speech too, so an export waits, showing "Preparing…", until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip in it has been measured. If a measurement has not landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." (see [Audio](audio.md#gate)).
- **Missing media.** A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence instead of failing the export.
- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Captions** are ordinary text clips, so they are always burned into the picture. To write a separate subtitle file, use **File ▸ Export Captions…** (see [Captions](captions.md)).

## For agents

`export` mirrors **Export…** with **Add to Queue**: it checks the request, puts the job in the Export Queue and answers at once with `{export_id, path, status}`. Status is `queued` or `running`.

| Argument | The sheet's control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` (required) | Format | `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif`, `apng`. |
| `path` (required) | Save panel | The folder must exist. An existing file is replaced. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and a different known media extension is replaced: `cut.mov` with `h264` writes `cut.mp4`. Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `size` | Size | `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (GIF and APNG only), or `[width, height]`. |
| `range` | Range | `project` (default) or `in_out`. Refused when there is no in/out range. |
| `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate` | Quality | Bits per second. On `av1`, `av1_webm` and `vp9_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft cap the file usually stays under. On `vp9_alpha_webm` it is the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone, and the transparency's stream comes on top of it (about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, measured). `audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate. |
| `loudness_lufs` | Loudness | −70 to 0. |
| `peak_dbtp` | (fixed at −1 on the sheet) | −20 to 0: the master limiter's ceiling, −1 when absent. Legal with or without `loudness_lufs`. |
| `audio_bits` | Bit depth | `16` (default) or `24`. `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only; refused on every other format. |
| `stems` | Stems | `tracks` or `names`. `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only; refused on every other format and when no track can be heard. See [Stems](#stems). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Burn in timecode | |
| `dynamic_range` | Dynamic Range | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. |
| `encoder_speed` | Speed | `faster`, `balanced` (default) or `smaller`. `av1` and `av1_webm` only; refused on every other format, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm` included. |

There is no frame-rate argument. An agent's export uses the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own.

Every refusal comes back from `export` itself, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline, or a graphic that does not compile.

- `export_status {export_id}` answers the job's row without waiting: `queued`, `running` (with `progress` from 0 to 1 and `phase`), `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Call it again after a pause until the job finishes.
  - Every answer has `path` and `elapsed` (seconds).
  - `done` adds `bytes`, the settings the file was written with, `burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range` in an HLG project, `encoder_speed` for AV1 and AV1 (WebM), `audio_bits` for WAV and AIFF, `stems` (`[{name, tracks, path}]`, each file beside the mix) when stems were asked, any `graphic_warnings` and, for every format with sound, `loudness`: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp` (the master limiter's), `limited_db` (how far it turned the loudest peak down), `capped_by_gain` (the 40 dB limit decided the gain) and `target_lufs`.
  - `queued` adds `waiting`, the row's "Waiting for memory: …" sentence, while an AV1 or VP9 job waits for memory.
  - `queued` and `running` add `estimated_seconds` for `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`: the export sheet's estimate of the whole export, in whole seconds.
  - `failed` and `cancelled` add `reason`, the queue row's sentence.
- `cancel_export {export_id}` is the row's Cancel.
- An `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
- `render_frame` renders one frame through the same path as Save Frame…. It returns the image inline and as a file, and with no `path` it writes a temporary PNG and names it. An explicit `format` wins and replaces the path's extension, so `{path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` writes `shot.png`. When a graphic in the frame warned or failed, the reply names it, its frame and the message, and a failed graphic draws its error card in the picture. A clip with Remove Background waits up to 30 s for its person masks, as Save Frame… does, and past that is drawn whole with "Clip *n* is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." in the reply. It takes `t` (default: the playhead), `path`, `format` (`png`, `jpeg`, `heic`), `max_width` and `burn_in_timecode`, plus `sdr_version`, `ungraded`, `selection` and the scope measurements described in [Colour grading](color-grading.md) and [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).

The full reference is [MCP](mcp.md).

## Limits

- An animated GIF or APNG holds at most **600 frames**: 48 seconds at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 seconds at APNG's 25 fps. A longer range is refused. Shorten the range or lower the frame rate.
- A loudness target more than 40 dB above the mix lands quieter than asked, and the report's `capped_by_gain` says so.
- The master limiter cannot be turned off; 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while editing than in the file.
- ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) refuse a custom size of a different shape from the canvas.
- VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only: an HDR project writes its SDR version, and HDR is refused on it.
- A VP9 with Alpha (WebM) file re-imported into Frame Job keeps its picture and loses its transparency: it shows opaque, with black where it was transparent. Export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha for a transparent clip to bring back in.
- Whether Safari shows VP9 with Alpha (WebM)'s transparency has not been confirmed; use HEVC with Alpha for Safari.
- A Mac with no encoder for a format reports "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." and leaves no file.
- 24-bit is offered on WAV and AIFF only. ProRes, AAC and Opus sound is 16-bit, and nothing is dithered.
- On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot play or re-import its own AV1 file, MP4 or WebM; QuickTime cannot either. Those Macs have no AV1 decoder. A VP9 (WebM) file re-imports on any Apple silicon Mac.
- AV1's and VP9's file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1 and about 1.15 times with VP9.
- Captions are burned in, never a switchable subtitle track.
- Queued jobs run one at a time. **Export…** does not join the queue: it writes straight away, behind its own progress sheet.
- A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. The memory each needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee: a heavier timeline can use more. An **Export…** sheet is never held, so starting several AV1 or VP9 sheets at once can go past that quarter.
- The estimated time is the median of three measured exports per format and size, of real 4K camera footage on one idle Mac (an Apple M2 Max). On exports it was not fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time; a slower Mac, a busy one or a heavier timeline takes longer.
- Quitting during an **Export…** progress-sheet export does not ask and leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.

    /// the only thing that can end a `.terminateLater`, so an exporter that
    /// never called back would leave a person unable to quit by any means but
    /// Force Quit. Five seconds is longer than a cancel has ever taken and
    /// short enough that nobody reaches for the Dock.
    private func waitForQueueThenTerminate() {
        var observer: (any NSObjectProtocol)? = nil
        var replied = false
        func reply() {
            guard !replied else { return }
            replied = true
            if let observer = observer { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(observer) }
            NSApp.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate: true)
        }
        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: .main
        ) { _ in
            if ExportQueueController.shared.isIdle { reply() }
        }
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 5) { reply() }
    }

    /// The socket is released and not joined: its file is unlinked only

    /// process exit, so a call in flight cannot hold the quit (its handler
    /// and context live for the process).
    func applicationWillTerminate(_ notification: Notification) {
        AgentServer.shared.unbindSocket()

## VP9 with Alpha (WebM)

VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox. Safari hasn't been confirmed to show its transparency, and Safari's transparent movie is [HEVC with Alpha (MOV)](/export/h264-and-hevc/#hevc-with-alpha-mov). Only a player that decodes VP9 with libvpx shows the transparency, and others show the picture opaque.

- The picture is 8-bit, with the transparency as a second stream beside it. The [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`.
- It's SDR only, so an HDR project writes its SDR version, and **Dynamic Range:** stays greyed out on **SDR version**.
- The sound is Opus, as in VP9 (WebM).
- A **Custom…** size of a different shape from the canvas won't export, because padding would lose the alpha. After the save panel the export stops with a message naming the canvas's size. Every row in the **Size:** popup is fine.
- Imported back into Frame Job it shows opaque, with black where it was transparent. For a transparent clip to bring back in, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.

## The rate as a soft cap
## Memory and the queue

A job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) waits while the AV1 and VP9 exports already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. Its row says why, for example "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 6.0 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 3.0 GB." A later job may run first meanwhile.

A job always starts when no other AV1 or VP9 export is running. **Export…** never waits, so starting several at once behind their progress sheets can go past that quarter. The memory each job needs is a measured figure, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.

## The footnote

The small line under the readout names what the file is made of. It lists these in order, leaving out whatever doesn't apply:

1. The codec, such as `H264`, `AV1` or `PRORES422`.
2. The container, unless it's the same word as the codec, as in `GIF`.
3. The AV1 speed, such as `Balanced`.
4. `24-bit` for a 24-bit WAV or AIFF.
5. The number of stems, such as `3 stems`.
6. The video rate, when you've picked a Quality tier. AV1 and VP9 rates read `usually ≤ …`, because the rate is a [soft cap](/export/av1-and-vp9/#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap).
7. The audio rate, when you've picked a Quality tier, such as `192 kbps audio`.
8. The loudness target, such as `−14 LUFS`.
9. `alpha`, when the format keeps transparency.

So a plain export reads `H264 · MP4`, an AV1 file `AV1 · MP4 · Balanced` or `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`, and a transparent web movie `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`. With High quality and a loudness target at 1080p and 30 fps, an H.264 file reads `H264 · MP4 · 8.0 Mbps · 256 kbps audio · −14 LUFS`.

## Export or Add to Queue

The sheet ends in three buttons.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Cancel** | Closes the sheet. Nothing is written and nothing is remembered. |
| **Export…** | Opens a save panel, then writes the file behind a [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/). It doesn't join the queue and never waits for memory. |
| **Add to Queue** | Opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/). The job keeps the project as it is now, and you can go on editing. |

**Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out while the sheet can't work out a valid file, for example with an empty custom field, or when the file would have no length.

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written: "Export the timeline as a movie.", "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." or "Export the timeline's audio."

## Good to know

title: "Canvas background and timecode"
description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |

Each change is one undo step.

## Set the background colour

Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.

To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

## Make the background transparent

Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.

Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.

---
title: "The Export Queue"
description: "Write exports behind the editor, one at a time, while you keep working, and follow, cancel or reveal each one from a single window."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Export Queue writes the same file as **Export…** without making you wait for it. Jobs run one at a time behind the editor while you keep working.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Window ▸ Export Queue"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Add to Queue"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Add to Queue

<Steps>

1. Set up the file in the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).

2. Choose **Add to Queue**. It's available whenever **Export…** is.

3. Name the file in the save panel and choose **Save**. This is the same panel **Export…** opens.

</Steps>

The **Export Queue** window then opens on its own, with the job in it. Your settings are remembered as the last choice, as they are for **Export…**.

Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** no progress sheet is in the way. You can start playback again and go on editing while the job runs.

## The Export Queue window

Choose **Window ▸ Export Queue** to open it at any time. It has no keyboard shortcut.

The window lists every queued, running and finished export. Jobs run one at a time, in the order they were added, unless a job has to [wait for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). Closing the window stops nothing. Open it again and the jobs are where they'd got to.

The line at the bottom counts the jobs, for example "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished". With nothing in the list, the window reads "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."

The list isn't saved. It starts empty each time you open Frame Job.

## Rows and their states

Each row shows the file's name and where the job has got to.

| The row says | What it means | Button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Waiting` | Queued behind the running job. | **Cancel** |
| `Waiting for memory: …` | An AV1 or VP9 job [waiting for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). | **Cancel** |
| `Writing · 42 %` | The job is running, with a progress bar beside it. It can stay at `Writing · 0 %` while the job [waits for what it needs](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs). | **Cancel** |
| `Measuring loudness… · 12 %` | The job is measuring the mix before it writes. | **Cancel** |
| `Stopping…` | You cancelled the job and it hasn't stopped yet. | **Cancel** |
| `Exported “Board.mp4”.` | The file landed. Any stems, graphic warnings and cursor warnings are counted after the name, then come the [loudness figures](/export/progress-and-report/). | **Show**, **Remove** |
| `Overwritten by a later export to the same file.` | The job finished, but a later job has since started writing to the same path. | **Remove** |
| `Cancelled.` | You stopped it while it ran. | **Remove** |
| `Cancelled before it started.` | You stopped it while it waited. | **Remove** |
| The reason it failed | The job stopped with an error. | **Remove** |

Hold the pointer over a row for its tooltip: the full path, the container, the size and the frame rate, then the whole memory sentence while a job waits for memory, then each graphic and cursor warning.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Cancel** | Stops that job and removes its half-written file. A waiting job is cancelled before it starts. |
| **Remove** | Takes a finished row out of the list. The file stays where it is. |
| **Show** | Reveals the finished file in the Finder. If the file has since been moved or deleted, Frame Job beeps. |

## Clear Finished and Cancel All

**Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row and leaves the queue running. It's dimmed when there's nothing to clear, and it deletes no files.

**Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one. It's dimmed when nothing is running or waiting.

A cancelled job's half-written file is removed. A job that failed leaves on disk whatever it had written, unless its message says no file was written.

## A queued job's snapshot

A job holds the timeline as it was when you chose **Save** in the save panel, including its media files, reversed clips, graphics, chapters and any timecode burn-in.

Edits, undos and relinks made afterwards don't change what it writes, and neither does closing the document. You can queue one version, go on cutting, and queue another.

## Quit with jobs in the queue

Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first, after Frame Job has asked about any unsaved documents.

The alert reads "An export is still being written." and names the running file, for example "“Board.mp4” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting. Quitting now stops it and deletes the partly written file."

- **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue, deletes the partly written file and quits.
- **Cancel** keeps Frame Job open and the queue running.

:::caution
Only the queue is guarded this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel that export first.
:::

## The encoder memory wait

AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, and they use a lot of memory.

| Format | At 1080p | At 4K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM), depending on [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) | About 1.2–2.4 GB | About 4.4–8.1 GB |
| VP9 (WebM) | About 0.4–0.5 GB | About 1.1–1.6 GB |
| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | About 0.7 GB | About 2.2 GB |

All the AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may hold up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. On a 16 GB Mac that's 4.0 GB.

A queued AV1 or VP9 job starts only if it fits in that quarter with what's already running. The queue itself runs one job at a time, so what holds a job back is an AV1 or VP9 export running behind an **Export…** progress sheet.

- When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large.
- While a job waits, a later job that fits runs first, and so does any job in a format the Mac encodes itself, such as H.264 or ProRes.
- An **Export…** sheet never waits. It's counted and starts straight away, so several sheets at once can go past the quarter.

The row's status is one line, so the sentence usually ends in "…" before its figures. The tooltip ends with all of it: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB."

The figures are measured, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.

## Good to know

- **Export…** doesn't join the queue. It writes straight away behind its [own progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/), and it can run while a queued job runs.
- Two jobs can name the same file. The save panel asks about replacing a file only if it's already on disk, so two quick **Add to Queue** choices with one name may not ask at all. The later job replaces the file as it starts writing, whether or not it goes on to finish, and the earlier row stops offering **Show**.

## With an agent

An agent's `export` always goes through the queue, never a progress sheet. Its job is a row like any other, but the window doesn't open on its own. `export_status` reads that row and `cancel_export` is its **Cancel**. An agent can follow and stop only the jobs it started. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/)
- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | About 0.7 GB | About 2.2 GB |

All the AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may hold up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. On a 16 GB Mac that's 4.0 GB.

A queued AV1 or VP9 job starts only if it fits in that quarter with what's already running. The queue itself runs one job at a time, so what holds a job back is an AV1 or VP9 export running behind an **Export…** progress sheet.

- When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large.
- While a job waits, a later job that fits runs first, and so does any job in a format the Mac encodes itself, such as H.264 or ProRes.
- An **Export…** sheet never waits. It's counted and starts straight away, so several sheets at once can go past the quarter.

The row's status is one line, so the sentence usually ends in "…" before its figures. The tooltip ends with all of it: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB."

The figures are measured, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.

## Good to know

- **Export…** doesn't join the queue. It writes straight away behind its [own progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/), and it can run while a queued job runs.
- Two jobs can name the same file. The save panel asks about replacing a file only if it's already on disk, so two quick **Add to Queue** choices with one name may not ask at all. The later job replaces the file as it starts writing, whether or not it goes on to finish, and the earlier row stops offering **Show**.

## With an agent

An agent's `export` always goes through the queue, never a progress sheet. Its job is a row like any other, but the window doesn't open on its own. `export_status` reads that row and `cancel_export` is its **Cancel**. An agent can follow and stop only the jobs it started. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

---
title: "Save Frame"
description: "Save the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC, drawn at full size the way an export draws it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Save Frame writes the frame under the playhead to a still image: a thumbnail, a poster frame or a picture for a document.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Save Frame…" keys="⌥⌘E" tools="render_frame" />

## Save a frame

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the frame.

2. Choose **File ▸ Save Frame…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>. It's greyed out while the timeline is empty.

3. Pick a **Format:** and a place. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` in place of `:`, such as `Board 00-00-12-05.png`.

4. Choose **Save**.

</Steps>

The frame is the one the playhead was on when you opened the panel. When the save works, nothing else appears. The file is where you put it.

If it doesn't work, an alert says why:

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing." | Frame Job couldn't draw a frame at that time. |
| "Could not write PNG to … The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it." | The folder is missing, or Frame Job can't write into it. |
| "Could not write HEIC to … This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format." | This Mac has no encoder for the format. |

## PNG, JPEG or HEIC

| **Format:** | File | Transparency | Depth | Compression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PNG** | `.png` | Kept | 8-bit, or 16-bit for a [deep frame](#deep-and-hdr-frames) | Lossless |
| **JPEG** | `.jpg` | None. A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. | Always 8-bit | 90 % quality |
| **HEIC** | `.heic` | Kept | 8-bit, or 10-bit for a deep frame | 90 % quality |

The popup opens on **PNG** every time and doesn't remember your last choice. A line under it says what the chosen format does with transparency, such as "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."

Choosing a format changes the extension in the file name and keeps a name you've typed. Only `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` and `.heic` count as extensions, so `Board v1.2` keeps its `.2` and becomes `Board v1.2.jpg`.

## Drawn the way an export draws it

The frame is drawn the way an [export](/export/what-an-export-includes/) draws it, at the canvas's full size.

Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version and Show Selection never change it. It never carries a timecode burn-in, even if you use one on your exports.

## Inside a nest

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the saved frame is the picture the canvas is showing: the nest's own, at the nest's size and the nest's time. The timecode in the suggested name is the nest's too. Save Frame is greyed out in an empty nest, however full the timeline is.

This is the opposite of an export, which always writes the whole timeline.

## Deep and HDR frames

Most frames are saved at 8 bits a channel and labelled BT.709. These are saved with more:

- **A deep frame.** A frame showing a still deeper than 8 bits, or a 10-bit VP9 clip, is saved as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, still labelled BT.709. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip is saved deep too, when every video track in the timeline is that deep.
- **An [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/).** Every PNG and HEIC keeps the HLG picture, as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG.

JPEG is always 8-bit. In an HDR project a JPEG is the project's [SDR version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), labelled BT.709.

See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/) for how depth runs through the rest of the app.

## Waiting for masks

A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, which are made on this Mac. Past that, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the clip's file, for example "speech.mov drawn whole: the person masks were not ready within 30 seconds."

Save the frame again once the clip's **Status** row shows the masks are done. An export never does this: it [waits as long as the masks take](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs).

## Good to know

A graphic that fails draws its error card in the saved frame, and a clip whose cursor file can't be read is drawn without its cursor. Save Frame doesn't warn you about either, so look at the picture.

## The same still for an agent

`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame for the same frame and format. It answers with the picture itself as well as a file, and with no path it writes a temporary PNG and names it.

It also reports what Save Frame keeps quiet: when a graphic in the frame warned or failed it names the graphic, its frame and the message, and it names a cursor file it couldn't read or a clip drawn without its masks. An agent can ask for more than the menu offers, such as a timecode burn-in, an ungraded picture or scope measurements. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
- [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/)
- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)

---
title: "Transparent exports"
description: "Export a title or overlay with a transparent background, and choose the format that keeps it for the place it's going."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A transparent canvas lets you export a title, a lower third or an overlay that sits on top of something else. Only four formats keep the transparency, so the format is the choice that matters.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Document tab ▸ Appearance ▸ Background', 'Export sheet ▸ Format']}
  tools={['set_canvas', 'export']}
/>

## Export with transparency

<Steps>

1. [Make the canvas background transparent](/projects/background-and-timecode/#make-the-background-transparent) in the Document tab.

2. Open the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) and pick a format that keeps transparency. The sheet's [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`, for example `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`.

3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.

</Steps>

## Which formats keep transparency

A transparent canvas stays transparent in four formats:

- **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**
- **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**
- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)**
- **Animated PNG**

Every other format composites the picture onto black. **Animated GIF** isn't one of the four: a GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partly transparent survives it.

For a single frame, [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#png-jpeg-or-heic) keeps transparency in PNG and HEIC, and JPEG flattens onto black.

## The Transparency note

While the canvas background isn't fully opaque, the **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) says which formats will keep it. Today it reads "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats."

The note names the formats when there are one or two, and counts them from three up. In a document with no length it reads "Transparent — needs an alpha format."

## Which transparent movie to send

| Send | For | Good to know |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** | The web: a `<video>` in a page, in Chrome and Firefox | Only a player that decodes VP9 with libvpx shows the transparency. Others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque. Safari hasn't been confirmed to show it. |
| **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)** | Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps | The transparent movie for Apple's players. |
| **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** | Another editor | The master. |

To bring a transparent clip back into Frame Job, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha. A VP9 with Alpha file keeps its picture when you import it but loses its transparency, showing black where it was transparent.

## Straight alpha

The colour in all three transparent movies is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.

Frame Job also fills the transparent pixels just outside the picture, up to 4 pixels out, with the colour of the edge beside them. Without that, a codec that averages colour across pixels would darken the edge. This is automatic, and there's nothing to set.

## The same-shape rule

ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha won't write a frame of a different shape from the canvas. Fitting the picture into another shape would pad it, and the padding destroys the alpha channel.

Every row in the [**Size:** popup](/export/size/) has the canvas's shape, so this only happens with a **Custom…** size. Scaling is fine, larger or smaller, as long as the proportions hold, and a size within a pixel of the canvas's shape is written.

After the save panel, the export stops with a message naming both sizes: "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape. This canvas is 1920 × 1080 and 1000 × 1000 is a different shape, so the picture would be padded and the padding loses the alpha channel. Export at 1920 × 1080, at one of the sizes in the popup, or at any size with the same proportions."

## Good to know

- HEVC with Alpha, VP9 with Alpha and Animated PNG are 8-bit. In an [HDR project](/hdr/export-hdr/) they write the SDR version, so use ProRes 4444 to keep both HDR and transparency.
- Transparency here means the canvas. A format that keeps it changes nothing for a canvas with an opaque background, or for a clip that covers the whole frame.

## Related

- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [ProRes](/export/prores/)
- [H.264 and HEVC](/export/h264-and-hevc/)
- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
- [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/)

---
title: "Chapters"
description: "Turn chapter markers into chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, and see how a range export treats them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Chapters let someone jump through a long video in their player. In Frame Job they come from the markers you've ticked as chapters, with nothing to set on the export sheet.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Markers ▸ Chapter" tools={['export', 'add_marker', 'set_marker']} />

## Chapters in exports

[Mark a chapter](/timeline/markers/#make-a-chapter) on the timeline, then export to any format that writes an MP4, MOV, M4A or WebM file. Chapter markers become the file's chapters, in time order.

- **Names.** A chapter takes its marker's name. An unnamed marker becomes "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on, counted over the chapter markers only, so removing a plain marker never renumbers them. A name of only spaces counts as unnamed.
- **Lengths.** Each chapter runs to the next one, and the last runs to the end of the file. Time before the first chapter marker belongs to no chapter, so put a marker on the first frame if you want the file to open in one.
- **Queued jobs.** A job writes the chapters the timeline had when you confirmed it, whatever you do to the markers afterwards. See [A queued job's snapshot](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot).

WAV, AIFF, Animated GIF and Animated PNG files have no chapters. Neither do [stems](/export/stems/): only the mix carries them.

## Chapters in a range export

An [export of a range](/export/range/) keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file. The chapter already running when the range starts opens the file, and a chapter starting at or after the range's end is left out.

Say the timeline has chapters at 0:00, 1:00 and 3:00, named Intro, Demo and Outro, and you export from 2:00 to 4:00. The file has two chapters: Demo at 0:00 and Outro at 1:00.

An unnamed chapter keeps its number from the whole timeline, so the third chapter marker is still "Chapter 3" in a file that holds only two.

## Related

- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

---
title: "What an export includes"
description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />

## The same picture and sound

An export uses the same composition and the same compositor as the preview, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.

View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).

The sound has one thing the preview doesn't: the master limiter, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Waiting for what it needs

Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip.

| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture) and no file is written |
| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |

Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.

While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.

[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.

## Missing media

A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.

An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Graphics

An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a module is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.

If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.

That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."

## Captions

Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).

## Colour labels

An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

---
title: "The Export Queue"
description: "Write exports behind the editor, one at a time, while you keep working, and follow, cancel or reveal each one from a single window."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Export Queue writes the same file as **Export…** without making you wait for it. Jobs run one at a time behind the editor while you keep working.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Window ▸ Export Queue"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Add to Queue"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Add to Queue

<Steps>

1. Set up the file in the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).

2. Choose **Add to Queue**. It's available whenever **Export…** is.

3. Name the file in the save panel and choose **Save**. This is the same panel **Export…** opens.

</Steps>

The **Export Queue** window then opens on its own, with the job in it. Your settings are remembered as the last choice, as they are for **Export…**.

Opening the export sheet pauses playback whichever button you use, but after **Add to Queue** no progress sheet is in the way. You can start playback again and go on editing while the job runs.

## The Export Queue window

Choose **Window ▸ Export Queue** to open it at any time. It has no keyboard shortcut.

The window lists every queued, running and finished export. Jobs run one at a time, in the order they were added, unless a job has to [wait for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). Closing the window stops nothing. Open it again and the jobs are where they'd got to.

The line at the bottom counts the jobs, for example "1 exporting · 2 waiting · 3 finished". With nothing in the list, the window reads "Nothing queued. The Export card's Add to Queue button puts a confirmed export here instead of waiting for it, and they run one at a time while you keep editing."

The list isn't saved. It starts empty each time you open Frame Job.

## Rows and their states

Each row shows the file's name and where the job has got to.

| The row says | What it means | Button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Waiting` | Queued behind the running job. | **Cancel** |
| `Waiting for memory: …` | An AV1 or VP9 job [waiting for memory](#the-encoder-memory-wait). | **Cancel** |
| `Writing · 42 %` | The job is running, with a progress bar beside it. It can stay at `Writing · 0 %` while the job [waits for what it needs](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs). | **Cancel** |
| `Measuring loudness… · 12 %` | The job is measuring the mix before it writes. | **Cancel** |
| `Stopping…` | You cancelled the job and it hasn't stopped yet. | **Cancel** |
| `Exported “Board.mp4”.` | The file landed. Any stems, graphic warnings and cursor warnings are counted after the name, then come the [loudness figures](/export/progress-and-report/). | **Show**, **Remove** |
| `Overwritten by a later export to the same file.` | The job finished, but a later job has since started writing to the same path. | **Remove** |
| `Cancelled.` | You stopped it while it ran. | **Remove** |
| `Cancelled before it started.` | You stopped it while it waited. | **Remove** |
| The reason it failed | The job stopped with an error. | **Remove** |

Hold the pointer over a row for its tooltip: the full path, the container, the size and the frame rate, then the whole memory sentence while a job waits for memory, then each graphic and cursor warning.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Cancel** | Stops that job and removes its half-written file. A waiting job is cancelled before it starts. |
| **Remove** | Takes a finished row out of the list. The file stays where it is. |
| **Show** | Reveals the finished file in the Finder. If the file has since been moved or deleted, Frame Job beeps. |

## Clear Finished and Cancel All

**Clear Finished** removes every finished, cancelled and failed row and leaves the queue running. It's dimmed when there's nothing to clear, and it deletes no files.

**Cancel All** stops the running job and every waiting one. It's dimmed when nothing is running or waiting.

A cancelled job's half-written file is removed. A job that failed leaves on disk whatever it had written, unless its message says no file was written.

## A queued job's snapshot

A job holds the timeline as it was when you chose **Save** in the save panel, including its media files, reversed clips, graphics, chapters and any timecode burn-in.

Edits, undos and relinks made afterwards don't change what it writes, and neither does closing the document. You can queue one version, go on cutting, and queue another.

## Quit with jobs in the queue

Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first, after Frame Job has asked about any unsaved documents.

The alert reads "An export is still being written." and names the running file, for example "“Board.mp4” is not finished, and 2 more are waiting. Quitting now stops it and deletes the partly written file."

- **Quit Anyway** cancels the queue, deletes the partly written file and quits.
- **Cancel** keeps Frame Job open and the queue running.

:::caution
Only the queue is guarded this way. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves the half-written file behind. Cancel that export first.
:::

## The encoder memory wait

AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software, and they use a lot of memory.

| Format | At 1080p | At 4K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM), depending on [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) | About 1.2–2.4 GB | About 4.4–8.1 GB |
| VP9 (WebM) | About 0.4–0.5 GB | About 1.1–1.6 GB |
| VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | About 0.7 GB | About 2.2 GB |

All the AV1 and VP9 exports running in Frame Job, from the queue and from **Export…** progress sheets, may hold up to a quarter of the Mac's memory together. On a 16 GB Mac that's 4.0 GB.

A queued AV1 or VP9 job starts only if it fits in that quarter with what's already running. The queue itself runs one job at a time, so what holds a job back is an AV1 or VP9 export running behind an **Export…** progress sheet.

- When nothing else is running, a job always starts, however large.
- While a job waits, a later job that fits runs first, and so does any job in a format the Mac encodes itself, such as H.264 or ProRes.
- An **Export…** sheet never waits. It's counted and starts straight away, so several sheets at once can go past the quarter.

The row's status is one line, so the sentence usually ends in "…" before its figures. The tooltip ends with all of it: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 4.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 2.2 GB."

The figures are measured, not a guarantee, and a heavier timeline can use more.

## Good to know

- **Export…** doesn't join the queue. It writes straight away behind its [own progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/), and it can run while a queued job runs.
- Two jobs can name the same file. The save panel asks about replacing a file only if it's already on disk, so two quick **Add to Queue** choices with one name may not ask at all. The later job replaces the file as it starts writing, whether or not it goes on to finish, and the earlier row stops offering **Show**.

## With an agent

An agent's `export` always goes through the queue, never a progress sheet. Its job is a row like any other, but the window doesn't open on its own. `export_status` reads that row and `cancel_export` is its **Cancel**. An agent can follow and stop only the jobs it started. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/)
- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

---
title: "Save Frame"
description: "Save the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC, drawn at full size the way an export draws it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Save Frame writes the frame under the playhead to a still image: a thumbnail, a poster frame or a picture for a document.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Save Frame…" keys="⌥⌘E" tools="render_frame" />

## Save a frame

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the frame.

2. Choose **File ▸ Save Frame…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>. It's greyed out while the timeline is empty.

3. Pick a **Format:** and a place. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` in place of `:`, such as `Board 00-00-12-05.png`.

4. Choose **Save**.

</Steps>

The frame is the one the playhead was on when you opened the panel. When the save works, nothing else appears. The file is where you put it.

If it doesn't work, an alert says why:

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "There is no frame at the playhead. The time is past the end of the timeline, the timeline is empty, or the media is missing." | Frame Job couldn't draw a frame at that time. |
| "Could not write PNG to … The file could not be created there — check that the folder exists and that Frame Job is allowed to write into it." | The folder is missing, or Frame Job can't write into it. |
| "Could not write HEIC to … This Mac's image encoders do not offer that format." | This Mac has no encoder for the format. |

## PNG, JPEG or HEIC

| **Format:** | File | Transparency | Depth | Compression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PNG** | `.png` | Kept | 8-bit, or 16-bit for a [deep frame](#deep-and-hdr-frames) | Lossless |
| **JPEG** | `.jpg` | None. A transparent canvas is flattened onto black. | Always 8-bit | 90 % quality |
| **HEIC** | `.heic` | Kept | 8-bit, or 10-bit for a deep frame | 90 % quality |

The popup opens on **PNG** every time and doesn't remember your last choice. A line under it says what the chosen format does with transparency, such as "PNG keeps the canvas's alpha channel." or "JPEG has no alpha channel: a transparent canvas is flattened onto black."

Choosing a format changes the extension in the file name and keeps a name you've typed. Only `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` and `.heic` count as extensions, so `Board v1.2` keeps its `.2` and becomes `Board v1.2.jpg`.

## Drawn the way an export draws it

The frame is drawn the way an [export](/export/what-an-export-includes/) draws it, at the canvas's full size.

Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version and Show Selection never change it. It never carries a timecode burn-in, even if you use one on your exports.

## Inside a nest

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the saved frame is the picture the canvas is showing: the nest's own, at the nest's size and the nest's time. The timecode in the suggested name is the nest's too. Save Frame is greyed out in an empty nest, however full the timeline is.

This is the opposite of an export, which always writes the whole timeline.

## Deep and HDR frames

Most frames are saved at 8 bits a channel and labelled BT.709. These are saved with more:

- **A deep frame.** A frame showing a still deeper than 8 bits, or a 10-bit VP9 clip, is saved as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC, still labelled BT.709. A 10-bit HEVC or ProRes clip is saved deep too, when every video track in the timeline is that deep.
- **An [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/).** Every PNG and HEIC keeps the HLG picture, as a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG.

JPEG is always 8-bit. In an HDR project a JPEG is the project's [SDR version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), labelled BT.709.

See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/) for how depth runs through the rest of the app.

## Waiting for masks

A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, which are made on this Mac. Past that, the frame is saved with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the clip's file, for example "speech.mov drawn whole: the person masks were not ready within 30 seconds."

Save the frame again once the clip's **Status** row shows the masks are done. An export never does this: it [waits as long as the masks take](/export/what-an-export-includes/#waiting-for-what-it-needs).

## Good to know

A graphic that fails draws its error card in the saved frame, and a clip whose cursor file can't be read is drawn without its cursor. Save Frame doesn't warn you about either, so look at the picture.

## The same still for an agent

`render_frame` writes the same bytes as Save Frame for the same frame and format. It answers with the picture itself as well as a file, and with no path it writes a temporary PNG and names it.

It also reports what Save Frame keeps quiet: when a graphic in the frame warned or failed it names the graphic, its frame and the message, and it names a cursor file it couldn't read or a clip drawn without its masks. An agent can ask for more than the menu offers, such as a timecode burn-in, an ungraded picture or scope measurements. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
- [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/)
- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)

---
title: "Transparent exports"
description: "Export a title or overlay with a transparent background, and choose the format that keeps it for the place it's going."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A transparent canvas lets you export a title, a lower third or an overlay that sits on top of something else. Only four formats keep the transparency, so the format is the choice that matters.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Document tab ▸ Appearance ▸ Background', 'Export sheet ▸ Format']}
  tools={['set_canvas', 'export']}
/>

## Export with transparency

<Steps>

1. [Make the canvas background transparent](/projects/background-and-timecode/#make-the-background-transparent) in the Document tab.

2. Open the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) and pick a format that keeps transparency. The sheet's [footnote](/export/export-sheet/#the-footnote) ends in `alpha`, for example `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`.

3. Choose **Export…** or **Add to Queue**.

</Steps>

## Which formats keep transparency

A transparent canvas stays transparent in four formats:

- **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**
- **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)**
- **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)**
- **Animated PNG**

Every other format composites the picture onto black. **Animated GIF** isn't one of the four: a GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partly transparent survives it.

For a single frame, [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#png-jpeg-or-heic) keeps transparency in PNG and HEIC, and JPEG flattens onto black.

## The Transparency note

While the canvas background isn't fully opaque, the **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) says which formats will keep it. Today it reads "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats."

The note names the formats when there are one or two, and counts them from three up. In a document with no length it reads "Transparent — needs an alpha format."

## Which transparent movie to send

| Send | For | Good to know |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** | The web: a `<video>` in a page, in Chrome and Firefox | Only a player that decodes VP9 with libvpx shows the transparency. Others, ffmpeg's default decoder among them, show the picture opaque. Safari hasn't been confirmed to show it. |
| **HEVC with Alpha (MOV)** | Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps | The transparent movie for Apple's players. |
| **ProRes 4444 (MOV)** | Another editor | The master. |

To bring a transparent clip back into Frame Job, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha. A VP9 with Alpha file keeps its picture when you import it but loses its transparency, showing black where it was transparent.

## Straight alpha

The colour in all three transparent movies is straight, not multiplied by the transparency, so a re-imported file composites to the right colour.

Frame Job also fills the transparent pixels just outside the picture, up to 4 pixels out, with the colour of the edge beside them. Without that, a codec that averages colour across pixels would darken the edge. This is automatic, and there's nothing to set.

## The same-shape rule

ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha won't write a frame of a different shape from the canvas. Fitting the picture into another shape would pad it, and the padding destroys the alpha channel.

Every row in the [**Size:** popup](/export/size/) has the canvas's shape, so this only happens with a **Custom…** size. Scaling is fine, larger or smaller, as long as the proportions hold, and a size within a pixel of the canvas's shape is written.

After the save panel, the export stops with a message naming both sizes: "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape. This canvas is 1920 × 1080 and 1000 × 1000 is a different shape, so the picture would be padded and the padding loses the alpha channel. Export at 1920 × 1080, at one of the sizes in the popup, or at any size with the same proportions."

## Good to know

- HEVC with Alpha, VP9 with Alpha and Animated PNG are 8-bit. In an [HDR project](/hdr/export-hdr/) they write the SDR version, so use ProRes 4444 to keep both HDR and transparency.
- Transparency here means the canvas. A format that keeps it changes nothing for a canvas with an opaque background, or for a clip that covers the whole frame.

## Related

- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [ProRes](/export/prores/)
- [H.264 and HEVC](/export/h264-and-hevc/)
- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
- [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/)

---
title: "Chapters"
description: "Turn chapter markers into chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, and see how a range export treats them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Chapters let someone jump through a long video in their player. In Frame Job they come from the markers you've ticked as chapters, with nothing to set on the export sheet.

<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Markers ▸ Chapter" tools={['export', 'add_marker', 'set_marker']} />

## Chapters in exports

[Mark a chapter](/timeline/markers/#make-a-chapter) on the timeline, then export to any format that writes an MP4, MOV, M4A or WebM file. Chapter markers become the file's chapters, in time order.

- **Names.** A chapter takes its marker's name. An unnamed marker becomes "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on, counted over the chapter markers only, so removing a plain marker never renumbers them. A name of only spaces counts as unnamed.
- **Lengths.** Each chapter runs to the next one, and the last runs to the end of the file. Time before the first chapter marker belongs to no chapter, so put a marker on the first frame if you want the file to open in one.
- **Queued jobs.** A job writes the chapters the timeline had when you confirmed it, whatever you do to the markers afterwards. See [A queued job's snapshot](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot).

WAV, AIFF, Animated GIF and Animated PNG files have no chapters. Neither do [stems](/export/stems/): only the mix carries them.

## Chapters in a range export

An [export of a range](/export/range/) keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file. The chapter already running when the range starts opens the file, and a chapter starting at or after the range's end is left out.

Say the timeline has chapters at 0:00, 1:00 and 3:00, named Intro, Demo and Outro, and you export from 2:00 to 4:00. The file has two chapters: Demo at 0:00 and Outro at 1:00.

An unnamed chapter keeps its number from the whole timeline, so the third chapter marker is still "Chapter 3" in a file that holds only two.

## Related

- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

---
title: "What an export includes"
description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />

## The same picture and sound

An export uses the same composition and the same compositor as the preview, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) you pick, even with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open.

View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/), [safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) and the [scopes](/color/scopes/).

The sound has one thing the preview doesn't: the master limiter, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Waiting for what it needs

Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip.

| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture) and no file is written |
| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |

Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip that will never be measured, because it's silent or under 0.4 seconds, doesn't hold the export up and exports as the preview plays it.

While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for masks and cursor tracks.

[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.

## Missing media

A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. So does a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/) whose backwards copy isn't rendered yet.

An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence, rather than failing the export. To put the real footage back first, [relink the media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Graphics

An export draws the [graphics](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/) as they were when you asked for it, even if a module is saved again while it runs. That also keeps a [queued job](/export/export-queue/#a-queued-jobs-snapshot) stable.

If a graphic in the range doesn't compile or has no module, the export doesn't start: "The export was not started: the graphic "lower-third" … Fix the module and export again." This counts every graphic in a nest the range reaches, even one outside the part that plays. An audio-only export skips the check.

That check is only a compile, so a graphic can still fail part-way through. The export then stops at that frame, names the graphic and leaves no file: "The export was stopped at frame 120 of the graphic "lower-third": … No file was written."

## Captions

Captions are ordinary text clips, so they're always burned into the picture. They're never a subtitle track a viewer can switch off. To write a separate subtitle file, use [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).

## Colour labels

An exported file carries colour labels, so players read it correctly. SDR files are labelled BT.709, and [HDR files](/hdr/export-hdr/) BT.2020 with HLG or PQ. A GIF carries no label.

- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)
